salinity.details: CSSRI variety information records sodicity tolerance up to about pH 9.9 and salinity tolerance up to 10.0 dS/m, with suitability for sodic and coastal saline areas (name recorded as CSR 27 on the CSSRI page). In a hydroponic screen at 200 mM NaCl, CSR 27 was one of eight genotypes and showed smaller declines in relative water content and membrane stability than most entries, and it kept a lower Na/K ratio, similar to Pokkali and CSR 10. A marker-assisted study reports that near-isogenic lines in the CSR27 background tolerated salinity up to about EC 10 dS/m at the seedling stage, and CSR 27 was among high-yielding reproductive-stage salt-tolerant genotypes. Reproductive-stage spikelet fertility is supported by the fine-mapped QTL qSSISFH8.1 on chromosome 8. The CSC record describes salt injury as less than that of check varieties, with negligible tip burning.

flood.details: No evidence found in searched sources.

disease_resistance.summary: From the CSC variety record (ground truth; no digest URL attached): moderately resistant to blast, bacterial leaf blight (BLB), sheath rot and brown spot. The digest's own searches found no evidence of disease resistance for CSR-27, so this rests on the CSC record alone.

pest_resistance.summary: From the CSC variety record (ground truth; no digest URL attached): resistant to leaf folder and moderately resistant to whitebacked planthopper (WBPH). The digest's own searches found no evidence of pest resistance for CSR-27, so this rests on the CSC record alone.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- Salt tolerance is recorded for CSR-27 as a CSSRI variety, with sodicity tolerance up to about pH 9.9 and salinity tolerance up to 10.0 dS/m, suited to sodic and coastal saline areas (name: CSC "CSR-27 (IET-13765,CSR-88-IR-6)"; CSSRI page uses "CSR 27") -- https://cssri.res.in/varieties-developed/
- A hydroponic salinity screen at 200 mM NaCl included CSR 27 as one of eight genotypes; it showed smaller declines in relative water content and membrane stability than most entries and kept a lower Na/K ratio, similar to Pokkali and CSR 10 (name: "CSR 27") -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/288965462_New_Salt_tolerant_variety_of_rice_CSR_36
- A marker-assisted study reports that near-isogenic lines in the CSR27 background tolerated salinity up to about EC 10 dS/m at seedling stage, and CSR 27 was among high-yielding reproductive-stage salt-tolerant genotypes (name: "CSR27") -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361442656_Development_of_Salt-Tolerant_Rice_Varieties_to_Enhancing_Productivity_in_Salt-Affected_Environments
- Drought, heat, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found for disease or pest resistance of CSR-27 in the searches (searched under CSC and Seednet-style name; results were about salinity only).

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Plant height about 115 cm, maturity about 125 days, long slender grain (name: "CSR 27") -- https://cssri.res.in/varieties-developed/
- CSR 13 and CSR 27 were added as new checks in place of CSR 10 in a salt-tolerance trial programme; the page does not give yield data for CSR 27 (name: "CSR 27") -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/379529917_Recent_Approaches_in_Breeding_for_Salt_Tolerance_in_Rice_in_Bangladesh
- Hydroponic yield/physiology comparison (see STRESS TOLERANCE) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/288965462_New_Salt_tolerant_variety_of_rice_CSR_36
- Field-trial yield values for CSR 27: No evidence found (the yield figures on the CSSRI variety page belong to a neighbouring entry, not verifiably to CSR 27)
- Multi-location trial results: No evidence found

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage: Nona Bokra / IR 5657-33-2; developed by recombination breeding; breeding-line codes IET 13765 and CSR-88-IR-6 (name: "CSR 27 (IET 13765), CSR-88IR-6") -- https://www.researchsquare.com/article/rs-213648/v1
- Recombination breeding method also recorded in an IRRI salt-tolerance breeding course page -- http://www.knowledgebank.irri.org/ricebreedingcourse/Breeding_for_salt_tolerance.htm
- QTL mapping: 25 QTLs for 17 traits (seedling salt injury, Na+, K+, Cl–, Na+/K+ ratio) in an F2:F3 population from CSR27/MI48 (Ammar et al., 2009, cited via preprint) -- https://www.researchsquare.com/article/rs-213648/v1
- Major reproductive-stage spikelet-fertility QTL qSSISFH8.1 on chromosome 8, fine-mapped in CSR27 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361442656_Development_of_Salt-Tolerant_Rice_Varieties_to_Enhancing_Productivity_in_Salt-Affected_Environments
- Use as parent: DRR Dhan 48 and DRR Dhan 49 carry the cross RP Bio 226*1/CSR 27 (listed with ICAR-IIRR); this confirms breeding use of the line but the page does not state the IET code (name: "CSR 27") -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/nutrition/articles/10.3389/fnut.2020.00026/full
- Genome resources (sequence, markers, accession IDs): No evidence found

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Breeder name(s): No evidence found. The searches returned staff names from CSSRI on unrelated pages; none is tied to CSR-27, so none is recorded here.
- Institution: Central Soil Salinity Research Institute (CSSRI), Karnal, is listed as developer of CSR 27 -- https://cssri.res.in/highlights/
- Release date discrepancy: CSSRI's crop-improvement page gives 1998 for CSR 13 and CSR 27 -- https://cssri.res.in/crop-improvement/ ; the Bihar notified-variety list gives 1999 with notification 1050(E) dated 26/10/1999 for "CSR-27 (IET-13765,CSR-88-IR-6)" -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf
- Station: No evidence found for a specific station (CSSRI Karnal headquarters per the institute pages)

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute: Central Soil Salinity Research Institute, Karnal (address as given in the input record "KARNAL-132001"; not confirmed by a retrieved page) -- institute website: https://cssri.res.in/
- Institute contact page URL, official email, phone: No evidence found in retrieved text
- Breeder contact: No evidence found

PUBLICATIONS
- Ammar et al. (2009). QTL mapping of salt tolerance traits in CSR27/MI48 population (cited within preprint; journal not retrieved). -- https://www.researchsquare.com/article/rs-213648/v1
- Authors not retrieved (year not retrieved). Development of Salt-Tolerant Rice Varieties to Enhancing Productivity in Salt-Affected Environments. Journal not retrieved. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361442656_Development_of_Salt-Tolerant_Rice_Varieties_to_Enhancing_Productivity_in_Salt-Affected_Environments
- Authors not retrieved (year not retrieved). New Salt tolerant variety of rice: CSR 36 (PDF, includes CSR 27 hydroponic comparison). Journal not retrieved. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/288965462_New_Salt_tolerant_variety_of_rice_CSR_36

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Sudhir (IET-10543), Rice (Paddy)

Name note: The CSC minutes name and the Seednet name are both "Sudhir (IET-10543)", so one search set covered both. None of the four searches returned a seednet.gov.in page, so no Seednet-specific evidence was found. The "Sudhir" name also matches unrelated people and products (a Sudhir Kumar at ICAR-IIAB, a Sudhir Yadav at IRRI/UQ, a Prasad Seeds manager, a Sudhir Chakravarti). I discarded those.

STRESS TOLERANCE: Two sources list resistance traits for the variety. One lists resistance to Sheath Rot, Sheath Blight, brown spot, blast, BLB, Leaf Folder and WBPH/Stem Borer (SB), and the other lists blast, BLB, LF, WBPH and SB. Yield is given as 27 q/ha. The resistance list is the same across both pages, so the sources are not independent. -- https://drdpat.bih.nic.in/Rice%20Varieties%20-%2009.htm ; https://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0
Drought: An IRRI Rice Research Notes article titled "Sudhir, a progeny of FR13A" lists "Drought resistance" as a keyword. The page metadata alone does not confirm drought tolerance for this line, so treat it as unverified. -- https://zenodo.org/records/6999390

DISEASE AND PEST: Resistant to blast, bacterial leaf blight (BLB), brown spot, leaf folder (LF), whorl-type leaf-sheath disease (listed as Sh.R/Sh.B in the source), and sheath blight/rot (listed as Sh.R/Sh.B), plus white-backed planthopper (WBPH) and stem borer (SB). Same source as STRESS TOLERANCE. -- https://drdpat.bih.nic.in/Rice%20Varieties%20-%2009.htm ; https://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: Maturity 150-160 days. Semi-deep water type. Tall plant (140-150 cm). Long slender (LS) grain. Yield 27 q/ha. -- https://drdpat.bih.nic.in/Rice%20Varieties%20-%2009.htm ; https://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0
No multi-location trial data or AICRP report entries were found for this variety.

GENETICS AND QTL: Parentage FR-13A x CNM-539 (matches the user-supplied FR 13A/BIRAJ(CNM 539)). -- https://drdpat.bih.nic.in/Rice%20Varieties%20-%2009.htm ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/382209019_Translating_Science_for_the_Benefits_of_Society_The_Direct_and_Indirect_Impacts_of_NRRI
Listed as "148 Sudhir FR 13A × CNM 539 IET-10543 1999 CVRC" in an NRRI impact report, which gives the IET code. Breeding method, breeding-line codes beyond IET-10543, and genome/QTL resources: No evidence found.
Other pages mention "Sudhir" as a parent (NRRI variety pedigrees such as Gayatri/Sudhir//Varshadhan). These describe other varieties and are not evidence about Sudhir itself. -- https://icar-nrri.in/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Rice-Varieties-of-NRRI.pdf

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: Breeder or scientist names: No evidence found. The only institution evidence is the NRRI listing above, which conflicts with the user-supplied Rice Research Station, Chinsurah, Hooghly, as the developing station. Both may be true because the station is part of the Indian national rice institute network, but no source confirms this. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/382209019_Translating_Science_for_the_Benefits_of_Society_The_Direct_and_Indirect_Impacts_of_NRRI

CONTACT DETAILS: No breeder contact found. No institute contact page or official email, phone or postal address for the Rice Research Station, Chinsurah, or for NRRI, was returned by these searches. Do not use the unrelated "Sudhir Kumar" (ICAR-IIAB) or "Sudhir Yadav" (IRRI) contacts; they belong to different people.

PUBLICATIONS: No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report, or KrishiKosh thesis naming this variety was found. The only item is a title match: Authors not shown (year not shown). Sudhir, a progeny of FR13A. International Rice Research Notes (IRRI) -- https://zenodo.org/records/6999390 . The page metadata does not list the authors or the full text, so it is unverified as a source on this variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY: No current seed dealer, State Seed Corporation or KVK listing for Sudhir was found. The WBSSCL (West Bengal) availability list does not include Sudhir. The Assam and Bihar/Jharkhand lists name Sudhir only as a notified variety, not as seed on sale. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/list-of-notified-paddy-varieties-for-assam/ ; https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/list-of-notified-paddy-varieties-for-bihar-and-jharkhand/ ; https://www.wbsscl.com/availability-of-seeds/

RECOMMENDED STATES: The recommendation text reads "West Bengal, Assam, Bihar and Uttar Pradesh" (the release table reads "W Bl, Assam, Bihar, UP"). This replaces the "Unknown" value in the input record. -- https://drdpat.bih.nic.in/Rice%20Varieties%20-%2009.htm ; https://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0

RELEASE/NOTIFICATION (supporting): Released 1999. Notified 13/09/2000 under S.O. 821(E). Listed on the Bihar notified-varieties list. -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Narendra Usar-3 (rice / PADDY (DHAN)), variety_code A0102153

Search status: Four web_search calls ran, covering variety/release, breeder, research and seed availability. A fifth verification pass hit the tool's search limit, so I could not open the full page text. Several results were only visible as short snippets, so I could not confirm that any page names this variety. Because of that, every heading below reads "No evidence found," and nothing is attributed to Narendra Usar-3.

Name check: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "Narendra Usar-3" / "NARENDRA USAR-3". No separate Seednet search result was obtained, so I cannot say whether the two names differ on the portal.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. Searches returned no page confirming this variety's drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence response.

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found. The only candidate was an NDUAT research-highlights PDF (https://www.nduat.org/Doc/skteditedResearchAchievementsfoNet-2014.pdf). Its visible snippet covered kharif variety comparisons but did not show the name "Usar-3", so I have not attributed it.

GENETICS AND QTL (parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources): No evidence found. The stated parentage (LEUNG YAI 148 / IR 9125-209-2-2-2-1 / IR 18272-27-3-1) was not found on any retrieved page.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: No evidence found. The "developed by" search returned only a hybrid-rice seed production guideline (https://static.vikaspedia.in/media/files_en/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/hybrid-rice-seed-production.pdf), which is not about this variety.

CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found. The institution named in the record is the Department of Genetics & Plant Breeding, NDUAT, Kumarganj, Faizabad. No contact details were retrieved from a source. The NDUAT domain (nduat.org) appeared in results, but no contact page was opened.

PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found. One rice paper appeared (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/374189714_Correlation_and_Path_Coefficients_Analysis_for_Yield_and_its_Contributing_Traits_in_Rice_Oryza_sativa_L._under_Sodic_Soil). Its visible title and snippet did not name Narendra Usar-3, so it is not listed as a publication for this variety. I could not verify the authors, year or journal.

SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES: No evidence found. The CSC record lists "Unknown", and no source resolved this.

Next steps for a complete record: open the NDUAT research-highlights PDF and the ResearchGate paper in full to check for the variety name. Then check the NDUAT Department of Genetics & Plant Breeding page for contacts, and the CSC/Seednet notification entry for release details. KrishiKosh and the ICAR rice AICRP reports are also worth searching directly.

No multi-location trial, yield or AICRP results were found for this variety.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage given as PR-19-2 x RR-149-1129 -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2023.1268739/full
Discrepancy: the input record gives parentage as "RR 19-2/RR 149-1129", while the Frontiers page gives "PR-19-2 x RR-149-1129" (PR vs RR for the first parent). Not resolved; verify against the original CSC/release record.
Breeding-line codes IET-16430 and RR-347-166 appear in the variety name -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf
Breeding method, QTL/marker studies and genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Institution per input record: Central Rainfed Upland Rice Research Station, Hazaribag, Bihar (CRURRS). No page confirming CRURRS as the developing station was retrieved.
Conflicting attribution: a ResearchGate document titled "Rice Varieties of NRRI" lists Anjali among NRRI varieties -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/338966196_Rice_Varieties_of_NRRI . This does not establish NRRI as the developer, and the page was not verified in full; it is recorded as a conflict, not a finding.

No AICRP/ICAR annual report, KrishiKosh thesis, conference paper or peer-reviewed paper specifically on this variety was found beyond the item above.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Bihar: listed in the state's notified-variety document (year of release 2002; notification date 04/09/2002; notification no. 937(E)) -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name check: The CSC/notification-style name is "Hybrid lndam 200-022 (lndam 200-022) (IET 20710)" and the Seednet name is "Hybrid lndam 200- 022 (lndam 200-022) (IET 20710)". Search results use "Indam 200-022 (IET 20710)" and "INDAM 200-022". I treated these as the same variety because the number and IET code match. Searches 1 and 2 used the CSC name, and search 3 used the short form. Search 4 was run under the short form too.

Discrepancies to resolve before using this record:
- Release year: the user record says 2017, but the retrieved notice is dated 25 September 2023.
- Recommended state: the user record says Madhya Pradesh, but the retrieved notice says Assam.
- Parentage (IAHS 19A/IASN 71R) and the institution (Indo-American Hybrid Seeds, Rice R&D farm, Hyderabad) come only from the input record. Searches did not confirm either.

STRESS TOLERANCE: Only one retrieved trial in Ghana mentions this hybrid's disease reaction. It reports blast and bacterial leaf blight (BLB) scoring for introduced hybrids, but the snippet does not clearly attribute any tolerance rating to INDAM 200-022. No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/331741636_Evaluation_of_Yield_Reaction_to_Diseases_and_Grain_Physical_Attributes_of_Some_Introduced_Rice_Hybrids_in_Ghana

DISEASE AND PEST: The same Ghana study scores BLB and blast severity in its trial and notes that the inbred check showed disease symptoms. Its disease-reaction table includes an INDAM 200-022 row, but the retrieved text does not give a clear resistance rating for it. No Indian disease or pest evidence was found. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/331741636_Evaluation_of_Yield_Reaction_to_Diseases_and_Grain_Physical_Attributes_of_Some_Introduced_Rice_Hybrids_in_Ghana

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: A Ghana multi-location trial reports that INDAM 200-022 had the highest mean yield in 2014, at 6.56 t/ha across locations. That is about 12% above the best inbred, AgraRice (5.91 t/ha). This is a Ghana trial, not an Indian AICRP or ICAR trial. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/331741636_Evaluation_of_Yield_Reaction_to_Diseases_and_Grain_Physical_Attributes_of_Some_Introduced_Rice_Hybrids_in_Ghana
No Indian multi-location, AICRP or state trial result for this hybrid was found. -- No evidence found in searches 1 and 3.

GENETICS AND QTL: Parentage IAHS 19A/IASN 71R appears only in the input record and was not found in any retrieved source. No breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources, QTL or marker studies for this hybrid were found. The retrieved genomics papers concern other rice hybrids, such as IR79156A/IL50-13 and the rice heterosis study, and are discarded as irrelevant. -- No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: No lead breeder or scientist name was found for this hybrid. The only institution found is the marketing company, Indam Seeds, which lists INDAM 200-022 as an F1 hybrid rice product. The development station named in the input record (Rice R&D farm, Hyderabad) was not confirmed by any search result. -- https://www.indamseeds.com/field-crops

CONTACT DETAILS: No breeder contact, institute contact or postal address was found. The company website lists the product but was returned without contact details in the retrieved snippet. -- https://www.indamseeds.com/field-crops

Authors not shown in retrieved snippet (year not confirmed; ResearchGate record). Evaluation of Yield, Reaction to Diseases, and Grain Physical Attributes of Some Introduced Rice Hybrids in Ghana. Journal not shown -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/331741636_Evaluation_of_Yield_Reaction_to_Diseases_and_Grain_Physical_Attributes_of_Some_Introduced_Rice_Hybrids_in_Ghana
No Indian peer-reviewed paper, AICRP/ICAR report, KrishiKosh thesis or conference paper for this hybrid was found. -- No evidence found in searches 1 and 3.

RECOMMENDED STATES: The retrieved notice recommends this hybrid for sale in Assam. It reports the release notification as dated 25 September 2023, issued by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare after consultation with the Central Seed Committee. Madhya Pradesh, the state in the input record, is not supported by any search result. drought.details: No evidence found for drought tolerance specific to CSR 49 or IET 20329 in the searched sources.

heat.details: No evidence found for heat tolerance specific to CSR 49 or IET 20329 in the searched sources.

salinity.details: CSR 49 (IET 20329) is described as part of a salt-tolerant rice series developed by CSSRI Karnal, with salt tolerance as the stated breeding goal. The brief describes the variety as high yielding and tolerant to salinity and alkalinity, and as suited to alkaline locations, with a yield of 36 q/ha in salt-affected soils against 65 q/ha in normal soils (the brief lists the unit as 'Q/ha app' and 'Kg/Ha'; the unit is inconsistent in the source). A multi-location saline and alkaline trial under the name CSR-2K-242 found the line superior and stable among tested genotypes with higher mean yields, but its performance differed between saline and sodic soils and it was not reported as best under both. The link between CSR-2K-242 and IET 20329 is inferred from the name in the brief and is not stated in the source. No seedling-stage salinity or alkalinity scores were found. The level is rated medium because the evidence is group-level or inferred rather than variety-specific trial data.

flood.details: No evidence found for flood tolerance specific to CSR 49 or IET 20329 in the searched sources.

disease_resistance.summary: Brief (original variety data): moderately resistant to leaf and neck blast, brown spot and sheath rot; stress reaction notes tolerance to some major pests and diseases. ICAR AR 2019-20: moderate resistance to blast and sheath rot listed in a rice table row for CSR 49 (IET 20329). The digest states the text is fragmented and the attribution to CSR 49 must be verified against the full table, so the ICAR notes are unverified. No other disease evidence was found.

pest_resistance.summary: ICAR AR 2019-20 lists moderate resistance to brown planthopper and leaf folder for CSR 49 (IET 20329). The attribution is unverified because the text is fragmented. The original variety data field for pest reaction is recorded as '0' (no data). No other pest evidence was found.

agronomic_details.yield: Original variety data: normal soils 65 q/ha; salt-affected soils 36 q/ha (unit recorded as 'Kg/Ha' in the brief, which is inconsistent). ICAR AR 2019-20 table row for CSR 49 (IET 20329), Uttar Pradesh: 66.8 q/ha, but attribution is unverified because the text is fragmented.
agronomic_details.stability: In a multi-location saline and alkaline trial under the name CSR-2K-242 (inferred link), the line was superior and stable among tested genotypes with higher mean yields. Performance differed between saline and sodic soils. Stability data specific to CSR 49 are otherwise not found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Irrigated, transplanted, kharif conditions with high fertility; alkaline and irrigated alkaline areas of Uttar Pradesh. Most suitable for irrigated, transplanted alkaline locations of Uttar Pradesh (original variety data). ICAR AR 2019-20 row also indicates suitability for irrigated, high-fertility, transplanted conditions (attribution unverified).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Semi-dwarf; resistant to shattering; suitable for high alkaline conditions (original variety data). ICAR AR 2019-20 row, attribution unverified: medium slender grains. Brown rice zinc 26.06 ppm and iron 14.70 ppm from the same ICAR source, attribution unverified. Planting dates and fertilizer schedule: not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Multi-location saline and alkaline trial (2017 paper, name CSR-2K-242, link to IET 20329 inferred): line superior and stable with higher mean yields; not reported as best under both saline and sodic soils. (2) ICAR AR 2019-20 table row for CSR 49 (IET 20329), Uttar Pradesh: yield 66.8 q/ha, medium slender grains, 110-119 days maturity, zinc and iron values; attribution unverified. (3) CSSRI-led development paper (2022) lists CSR 49 among salt-tolerant varieties with no trial data in the retrieved text. No yield table, planting date or fertilizer trial specific to CSR 49 was found.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Not found in searched sources. Generic CSSRI marker-assisted work on the Saltol QTL was found but is not attributed to this variety.

commercial_info.seed_corporations: Not found in searched sources. No evidence from NSC or UP Beej Nigam.
commercial_info.availability_status: Not found in searched sources. CSSRI reports breeder and truthfully labelled seed for its salt-tolerant rice varieties as a group, with no per-variety figure for CSR 49. No Seednet portal page for IET 20329 (CSR 2K 242) CSR 49 was found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- CSR 49 (IET 20329) is described in the context of a salt-tolerant rice series developed by CSSRI Karnal (CSR 49 named; salt tolerance is the stated breeding goal) -- https://cssri.res.in/crop-improvement/
- Under the name CSR-2K-242, a multi-location saline and alkaline trial found this line superior and stable among tested genotypes, with higher mean yields. Its performance differed between saline and sodic soils, so it was not reported as best under both -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC5554213/ (the source does not state the CSR-2K-242 to IET 20329 link; this is inferred from the name given in the brief)
- No evidence found for seedling-stage salinity or alkalinity scores, submergence, drought, heat, or flood tolerance specific to CSR 49 or IET 20329.

DISEASE AND PEST
- The ICAR 2019-20 annual report lists CSR 49 (IET 20329) in a rice table and gives it moderate resistance to blast, sheath rot, brown planthopper and leaf folder. The text is fragmented, so the attribution of these resistance notes to CSR 49 specifically needs checking against the full table -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-09/AR-2019-20.pdf
- No other evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- ICAR AR 2019-20 table row for CSR 49 (IET 20329), Uttar Pradesh: suited to irrigated, high-fertility, transplanted conditions. The same fragmented text gives a yield of 66.8 q/ha, medium slender grains and 110–119 days maturity. Attribution to this row must be verified -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-09/AR-2019-20.pdf
- The same source gives brown rice zinc 26.06 ppm and iron 14.70 ppm, with the same attribution caveat -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-09/AR-2019-20.pdf
- The CSSRI-led development paper lists CSR 49 among its salt-tolerant rice varieties, with no trial data in the retrieved text -- https://doi.org/10.3390/environsciproc2022016030
- No evidence found for a yield table, planting dates or fertilizer schedule specific to CSR 49 in the retrieved pages.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage (IR 5711-3B-7-B-9-1-8 / NDRK 5012) comes from the brief only; no web source confirmed it.
- Breeding method: CSR 49 is described as developed through conventional breeding -- https://doi.org/10.3390/environsciproc2022016030
- Breeding-line code: CSR-2K-242 appears in the 2017 trial paper, matching the second name in the brief -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC5554213/
- No QTL, marker or genome-resource evidence found specific to CSR 49 or IET 20329. Generic CSSRI marker-assisted work on the Saltol QTL was not attributed to this variety -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Salt-tolerant-rice-varieties-developed-by-CSSRI-Karnal-and-released-by-CVRC_tbl1_257650699 (general context only)

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Swarna Smriddhi Dhan (IET 24306), Rice

Name check: the CSC name and the Seednet name are identical in the input, both "Swarna Smriddhi Dhan (IET 24306)". Most sources spell it "Swarna Samriddhi Dhan", and one uses "Swarna Samridhi". All findings below refer to this variety, not to Swarna, Swarna Sub1, Swarna Sukha Dhan, Swarna Shakti Dhan or CR Dhan 411. I did not reach a Seednet page, so the Seednet record is unverified.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Beside drought tolerance at the reproductive stage, the variety tolerates 10–12 days of submergence at the vegetative stage, and it suits water-limiting irrigated and drought-prone rainfed fields. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/view/131717
- Lodging resistance is listed among its traits (semi-dwarf, with drought, submergence, disease and insect tolerance) -- https://icarrcer.org.in/wp-content/uploads/VarietyReleased.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- Moderate resistance is reported to leaf blast, brown spot, sheath blight, false smut, stem borer, leaf folder and gall midge -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/view/131717
- A false smut review names it among varieties recommended for resistance, with no field data given -- https://www.researchgate.net/scientific-contributions/Ajay-Prakash-Singh-2307164987

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Medium duration of 135–140 days, with 5.5–6.0 t/ha yield potential -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/view/131717
- Grain quality: 77.8% hulling, 62.0% milling and 55.6% head rice recovery -- https://icarrcer.org.in/wp-content/uploads/VarietyReleased.pdf
- ICAR-RCER Annual Report 2023 frontline demonstrations: the farmers'-field average for this variety was 5.11 t/ha (the value sits in a list of five varieties, so the mapping is inferred from order) -- https://icarrcer.org.in/wp-content/uploads/AnnualReport2023.pdf
- A Ramgarh (Jharkhand) KVK frontline demonstration reported higher net returns (Rs 64,774/ha) than local practice (Rs 50,300/ha) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/396442488_Evaluating_the_Impact_of_Frontline_Demonstrations_on_Rice_Crops_in_Ramgarh_District
- Eastern India package of practices lists it as a medium-duration (125–140 d) and multiple-stress (drought and submergence) variety -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/390733768_Rice_Package_of_Practices_for_Eastern_India

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- The parentage IR72022-46-2-3-3-2/IR57514-PMI 5-B-1-2 was supplied in the task. No source I retrieved confirmed it.
- Breeding line code IET 24306 is confirmed (the name carries the code in every source).
- The variety was developed with IRRI collaboration -- https://icarrcer.org.in/wp-content/uploads/VarietyReleased.pdf
- No breeding method, QTL, marker or genome data for this variety was found. The marker-assisted Swarna Sub1 and CR Dhan 800 studies are about different lines and were excluded.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Authors of the Indian Farming release paper: Santosh Kumar, Rakesh Kumar and A K Choudhary, all at ICAR Research Complex for Eastern Region, Patna, Bihar 800 014 -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/view/131717
- Institute: ICAR Research Complex for Eastern Region (ICAR-RCER), Patna, which developed the variety with IRRI -- https://icarrcer.org.in/wp-content/uploads/VarietyReleased.pdf
- Institute director in 2020, named in a foundation-day report (not necessarily the current director): B.P. Bhatt -- https://icar.org.in/en/node/11177
- Institute director in 2021, named in a foundation-day report (not necessarily the current director): Ujjwal Kumar -- https://www.icar.org.in/en/icar-rcer-patna-celebrates-its-21st-foundation-day

CONTACT DETAILS
- Postal address on the ICAR-RCER variety page: ICAR Research Complex For Eastern Region, ICAR Parisar, P. O.: Bihar Veterinary College, Patna, Bihar – 800014 -- https://icarrcer.icar.gov.in/variety-released-2/
- Breeder-level email, phone and personal contact pages: No evidence found. Institute email and phone were not present in the retrieved pages.

PUBLICATIONS
- Kumar, S., Kumar, R., & Choudhary, A. K. (2023). Swarna Samriddhi Dhan: A high yielding, multiple stress tolerant rice variety for irrigated and rainfed shallow lowland ecology. Indian Farming, 73(2), 09-11 -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/view/131717
- ICAR-RCER, Patna (2021). Annual Report 2021. ICAR Research Complex for Eastern Region, Patna -- https://icarrcer.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2021/Annual%20Report%202021.pdf
- ICAR-RCER, Patna (2023). Annual Report 2023. ICAR Research Complex for Eastern Region, Patna -- https://icarrcer.org.in/wp-content/uploads/AnnualReport2023.pdf
- Incomplete record (authors, year and journal not confirmed): a ResearchGate item on FLDs in Ramgarh district -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/396442488_Evaluating_the_Impact_of_Frontline_Demonstrations_on_Rice_Crops_in_Ramgarh_District
- Incomplete record (authors, title and journal not confirmed): a false smut paper by Ajay Prakash Singh -- https://www.researchgate.net/scientific-contributions/Ajay-Prakash-Singh-2307164987
- No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP report entry or DOI for this variety was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- ICAR-RCER reported breeder seed (98.9 q), nucleus seed (2.75 q) and truthfully labelled seed (72 q) for this variety in 2021 -- https://icarrcer.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2021/Annual%20Report%202021.pdf
- The 2021 report also records more than 10 q distributed to over 250 farmers in Bihar and Jharkhand -- https://icarrcer.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2021/Annual%20Report%202021.pdf
- ICAR-RCER distributed quality seed of this variety to about 200 farmers in 2021 -- https://www.icar.org.in/en/icar-rcer-patna-celebrates-its-21st-foundation-day
- NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing: No evidence found. The Swarna Seeds and Maa Agrotech pages are unrelated companies and were excluded.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Bihar: the Bihar State Seed Sub-Committee (SVRC) released and recommended it for notification -- https://icarrcer.org.in/wp-content/uploads/VarietyReleased.pdf
- Suitable for transplanted irrigated and rainfed shallow lowland conditions in Bihar -- https://icarrcer.org.in/wp-content/uploads/VarietyReleased.pdf
- Jharkhand: field demonstrations and seed distribution in Ramgarh district, and seed to farmers in Bihar and Jharkhand, were reported -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/396442488_Evaluating_the_Impact_of_Frontline_Demonstrations_on_Rice_Crops_

1.	No pigmentation on any plant part.
2.	The proposed strain has aromatic short bold grain with desirable quality.

Name note: the CSC/release name and the Seednet name are both "Janki" (SEEDNET: "JANKI", code A0102408). All evidence below refers to the same name and crop. Searches 1 and 3 returned no Janki-specific pages, so those headings say so.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. The stress-tolerance search returned only other rice varieties (Naveen, Reeta, Hardinath 3, DRR Dhan 46, CSR36) and general stress papers. None of these name Janki, so none are used.

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found. The search returned no Janki-specific disease or pest data.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found. The only Janki-specific source is a station listing that gives no agronomic or trial data (see BREEDER AND INSTITUTION). A Janki-named paddy seed listing (SKB Seeds) gives no agronomic data either.

GENETICS AND QTL: No evidence found for the parentage or breeding-line codes. The input record gives parentage as a pure-line selection from Chenab rice of North Bihar. No source confirmed this. The search also returned "Chenab 64-117", a Bihar deep-water variety from a 1978 IRRI newsletter (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7002451), and "Chenab Basmati", a Pakistani line (https://www.academia.edu/Documents/in/Rice_Research). Both are different varieties and are excluded, so they must not be treated as Janki's parent or relatives.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION:
- Janki is listed among varieties developed at the Patna Agricultural Research Institute, under Rajendra Agricultural University (Pusa, Samastipur), with release year 1983 -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Centers/03%20Patna.pdf
- The same AICRIP centre profile says the station was established in 1973 under the university and aims to develop varieties for irrigated medium and rainfed shallow ecologies. This describes the station's mandate, not Janki specifically -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Centers/03%20Patna.pdf
- No lead breeder or scientist name is linked to Janki in any source. Names found on the RPCAU pages (e.g., Dr. Neelanjaya, Dr. Rajesh Kumar) are general programme staff and are not attributed to this variety -- https://rpcau.ac.in/researchprojects/
- The input's "Mithapur, Patna" location is not confirmed by any source found; the AICRIP record places the station under Pusa.

CONTACT DETAILS:
- No breeder contact found. No official email or phone for the Patna station or Janki was found.
- Institute-level address, as shown on the RPCAU page (the university that now succeeds Rajendra Agricultural University; the source does not state this link explicitly): "Dr. Rajendra Prasad Central Agricultural University, Pusa, Samastipur – 848 125, Bihar, India" -- https://rpcau.ac.in/researchprojects/
- The contact page for this address was not retrieved. Verify before use.

PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found for any paper, AICRP report, thesis or KrishiKosh record on Janki. Searches returned only unrelated rice papers, including the Chenab 64-117 newsletter and the Chenab Basmati paper (both excluded above). No Janki items are listed.

SEED AVAILABILITY:
- A Janki listing appears in the notified paddy varieties list for Bihar and Jharkhand (2022) -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/list-of-notified-paddy-varieties-for-bihar-and-jharkhand/
- A private seed company (SKB Seeds) offers a product called Janki. The page is a commercial product list, not an official source, and does not give the seed source or the breeder -- https://www.skbseeds.com/blog/paddy-seeds-variety-in-india
- No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK or SAU seed-sale record for Janki was found.
- Discarded: "Janki Traders" (Buxar) is a trader name, not this variety -- https://www.tradeindia.com/buxar/paddy-seed-city-185615.html

RECOMMENDED STATES: The input field reads "Unknown". The 2022 notified-varieties list for Bihar and Jharkhand includes Janki, which suggests notification for Bihar and Jharkhand, but the list does not show the notification scope or conditions -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/list-of-notified-paddy-varieties-for-bihar-and-jharkhand/

Gaps to close: official Seednet and CSC record for A0102408, the original 1983 release notification, the station contact page, and any SAU or AICRIP trial data.

Name check: The CSC release name is "Bhuvan (IET-7804)" and the Seednet name is "BHUVAN (IET-7804)". The only difference is capitalisation. Searches were run under both forms, and every finding below refers to the same variety under either name.

Searches run: 4 of 4 allowed. Seednet itself was not reached, and no official ICAR or SAU page for this variety surfaced.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Listed as resistant to bacterial leaf blight (BLB), gall midge (GM) and brown planthopper (BPH), and moderately resistant to blast, brown spot (BS) and sheath blight (SB) -- https://rice-garud.icar-web.com/varieties.php
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. Searched under the stress-tolerance query; the only source is the variety database above, which lists no tolerance data for these traits.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Same record as above: resistance to BLB, GM and BPH; moderate resistance to blast, BS and SB -- https://rice-garud.icar-web.com/varieties.php
- No independent disease or pest screening report found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Duration listed as 135 days, ecosystem irrigated, dwarf plant height of about 85 cm, yield listed as 40 q/ha -- https://rice-garud.icar-web.com/varieties.php
- No evidence found for multi-location trial results, AICRP entries or on-farm trial data.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage recorded as OR-158 (IR-8 x Siam-29) x Parijat x Rasi -- https://rice-garud.icar-web.com/varieties.php
- The "IET-7804" designation is the breeding-line code carried in the variety name; no source describes its derivation or breeding method.
- No evidence found for QTL, marker or genome-resource studies on this variety.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The Bihar notified-variety list gives the institution as the Rice Research Station, Bhubaneswar, and records release in 1989 -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf
- No evidence found naming the lead breeder or scientist.
- The search for a breeder returned an unrelated Bhuvan Pathak (Ahmedabad University, CRISPR rice work) -- https://ahduni.edu.in/faculty/bhuvan-pathak/. This is a different person and is discarded.
- The ICAR-NRRI event page (https://icar-nrri.in/icar-nrri-showcases-rice-research-at-iiwm-bhubaneswar/) mentions popular rice varieties in general, not this one. It is not attributed to this variety.

CONTACT DETAILS
- No evidence found for an official email, phone, postal address or contact page of the Rice Research Station, Bhubaneswar (or of its parent organisation). The only institute-level name is the Rice Research Station, Bhubaneswar, from the Bihar list above, with no contact fields.

PUBLICATIONS
- No evidence found for peer-reviewed papers, theses, KrishiKosh records or conference papers on this variety.
- Discarded as non-matching: Pathak et al. (2019), 3 Biotech, and Pathak et al. (2022), Plants, both CRISPR studies by a different author on other rice genes (https://ahduni.edu.in/faculty/bhuvan-pathak/ and https://scholarworks.uark.edu/csespub/40/). The Zenodo IRRI newsletter item on BW 78 concerns a different variety (https://zenodo.org/records/7219367).

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found from NSC, state seed corporations, KVKs, SAU seed sales or private dealers. The searches returned only notified-variety lists, not seed-supply records.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- The rice variety database lists the recommended states as "All India" -- https://rice-garud.icar-web.com/varieties.php
- The input record's field says "Unknown", so the two sources conflict.
- Notification lists place the variety in several states: Bihar and Jharkhand, Uttar Pradesh and Uttaranchal, Kerala, Gujarat, Goa, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Jammu and Kashmir, and Arunachal Pradesh (https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/list-of-notified-paddy-varieties-for-bihar-and-jharkhand/ ; https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/list-of-notified-paddy-varieties-for-kerala/ ; https://www.en.krishakjagat.org/seed-industry/list-of-notified-rice-varieties-in-uttar-pradesh-uttaranchal/). Notification in a state is not the same as a recommendation for that state.
- Assam is also listed in a drdpat.bih.nic.in state page (https://drdpat.bih.nic.in//State-Assam.htm), which is a weaker source.

Gaps to close: confirm the breeder from the Rice Research Station, Bhubaneswar and its parent institute (ICAR-NRRI, Cuttack); check the official Seednet record and the CSC release notification (SO 280(E), 1989) directly; and search KrishiKosh and the AICRP-Rice reports for trial data.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: Heera (IET-10973), Rice

Name note: The evidence refers to the name "Heera (IET-10973)" as written in the notified-variety lists. No Seednet page for "HEERA (IET-10973)" (code A0102499) was returned, so no Seednet-specific evidence exists.

STRESS TOLERANCE (name: Heera (IET-10973))
- Dwarf (70-75 cm), yield: 2.5-3.5 t/ha -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/CRRIs-varieties-1968-2024.pdf
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found. The CRRI list snippet lists a stress-tolerance column, but the Heera entry was truncated before any tolerance rating -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/CRRIs-varieties-1968-2024.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST (name: Heera (IET-10973))
- The CRRI variety list has a disease/pest resistance code column for Heera (entry 34, upland, 1988, Odisha, 68 days), but the code string in the snippet is garbled and cannot be read reliably -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/CRRIs-varieties-1968-2024.pdf
- Specific resistance genes or pest ratings for Heera: No evidence found in the retrieved pages.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS (name: Heera (IET-10973))
- Ecosystem: Rainfed Upland, 65-68 days duration, released 1989 -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10694615
- Productivity and quality: CRRI rice variety Heera released in 1989 with very high per day productivity was identified as high protein rice with 12% protein in brown rice and 10-10.5% in milled rice grains. -- https://crri.icar.gov.in/res_high.php
- Nitrogen-use trial (four seasons, N0-N150): Heera recorded the highest chlorophyll a content at N50 (2.34 mg/g fw), and Heera exhibited higher NUpE and grain yield at N0 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/375905161_Promising_physiological_traits_associated_with_nitrogen_use_efficiency_in_rice_under_reduced_N_application
- Grain quality: Heera had an amylose content of 25.6%, above the intermediate range of other tested genotypes -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/314783932_Studies_on_Grain_Yield_Physico-Chemical_and_Cooking_Characters_of_Elite_Rice_Varieties_Oryza_sativa_L_in_Eastern_India
- Upland-trial and farm-level yield: Yield in Heera-growing areas remained low, around 1,500 kg/ha -- http://books.irri.org/TechnicalBulletin16_content.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage: Heera (IET-10973), CR-404-48 x CR-289-1208, released 1989 -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10694615
- Pedigree line: the NRRI figure lists CR544-1-2 (IET10973) as the line, from CR408-48/CR289-1208. This page dates release to 1988, which conflicts with the 1989 release date. The 1988 date is an unresolved conflict; the 1989 date is used elsewhere -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/339974652_Rice_Varieties_of_NRRI_Yield_Quality_Special_Traits_and_Tolerance_to_Biotic_and_Abiotic_Stresses
- Donor parents listed in the input (PTB 18, PTB 21, TKM-6, IR 8, ARC materials): No evidence found in retrieved pages.
- Breeding method (selection from cross): No evidence found beyond the parentage above.
- Genes, QTL and markers: No evidence found for this variety.

- Developing institution: CRRI, Cuttack. Heera was released by CRRI in 1989 -- https://crri.icar.gov.in/res_high.php
- Institute now renamed: Central Rice Research Institute (CRRI), Odisha, Cuttack is now known as ICAR-National Rice Research Institute (NRRI) -- https://zollege.in/college/165869-central-rice-research-institute-cuttack

EVIDENCE DIGEST: Nalini (IET-8987), Rice (Paddy)

Search budget: all four searches were run (one batch of four queries), so the four-search limit is used up. Most headings have little or no evidence. Only the notification record and state-level listings are confirmed.

Name note: "variety_name" (Nalini (IET-8987)) and "seednet_variety_name" (NALINI (IET- 8987)) refer to the same entry in the Bihar-hosted notified-varieties list, which shows it under the "PADDY (DHAN)" group. The findings below apply to both names.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The searches returned no page that describes drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for this variety. A search hit on "Muktoshri" (arsenic tolerance, Chinsurah) is a different variety and was discarded.

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. No page on blast, BPH, sheath blight or other resistance for this variety was returned.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
No evidence found. No maturity, yield, or multi-location trial data for this variety was returned.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage "pure line selection from a local tall indica cultivar Sindurmukhi" comes only from the user-supplied record. No search result confirmed it. -- user-supplied input, not verified
- Discarded: a Deng & Zhou (1994) paper on a thermo-sensitive male-sterile rice labelled "8987" appears in a hybrid-rice review. It is a different line with a similar number and is not attributed to this variety. -- https://doi.org/10.48130/seedbio-0024-0018 (review citing the 1994 paper)
- No QTL, marker or genome-resource evidence was found for this variety.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- No lead breeder or scientist name was found for this variety. -- No evidence found
- The user-supplied institution, Rice Research Station, Chinsurah, Hooghly, is not confirmed as the developer by any search result. The station's background is described in a book chapter by Indrani Dana, which gives its founding year and state-department status. That chapter does not name Nalini. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/346650099_Twenty_years_of_achievements_of_the_EIRLSBN_at_the_Rice_Research_Station_Chinsurah
- The same chapter says the Chinsurah network released at least 20 varieties. It does not list Nalini, so this is context only. -- https://www.academia.edu/44661978/Twenty_years_of_achievements_of_the_EIRLSBN_at_the_Rice_Research_Station_Chinsurah

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder contact, institute email, phone, postal address or contact-page URL was found in any result. -- No evidence found
- Suggested next step: check the Rice Research Station, Chinsurah contact page through the West Bengal Department of Agriculture site, which was not reached in these searches.

PUBLICATIONS
- No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP/ICAR report, or KrishiKosh thesis specifically on Nalini (IET-8987) was found. -- No evidence found
- One hybrid-rice thesis on socio-economic impact in Udham Singh Nagar lists "Nalini (IET-8987)" under an overview of hybrid rice in Uttarakhand. The page is about hybrid rice adoption, so the listing is unclear and is not treated as a publication about this variety. -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/a55e1a4b-a29e-474e-b6b8-f0c932d24134/content
- The KrishiKosh repository pages returned were general descriptions and did not contain this variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY

- A paddy-seed dealer listing in Gobardanga, West Bengal names a product "Ajit Total" and does not mention Nalini. It was discarded. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/paddy-seeds-dhan-22827845497.html
- Not checked: NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, or SAU seed-sale pages.

disease_resistance.summary: Rice tungro virus (RTV): resistant (drdpat list as tungro resistance; CSC record as RTV resistant). Blast: tolerant (drdpat list; CSC record). Bacterial leaf blight: resistant (CRRI list only). Conflict: the drdpat page records blast tolerance, while the CRRI list records bacterial blight resistance. Both are recorded; neither is verified against a field trial. The NRRI report states its varieties show resistance to major diseases in general, with no per-variety score for this variety.

pest_resistance.summary: Rice gall midge: resistant (drdpat, CRRI list, CSC record; the CSC record also states the variety withstands gall midge attack). Green leafhopper (GLH): resistant (drdpat, CRRI list, CSC record). Brown planthopper (BPH) and whitebacked planthopper (WBPH): moderately resistant (drdpat list, CSC record).

agronomic_details.yield: CSC record: 3500.00 to 4500.00 kg/ha. drdpat list: 35-45 q/ha (consistent with the CSC range). CRRI list: yield potential of 4 t/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: Multi-location trial results: No evidence found. Stability across environments is not documented in the digest.
agronomic_details.adaptation: CSC record: recommended for release for cultivation in gall midge endemic areas of Odisha, Madhya Pradesh, Assam and Karnataka. Also suitable for late planting and responds to high doses of nitrogen (CSC record). Seed rate 40 kg/ha for transplanting (CSC record).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Semi-dwarf, plant height 90-95 cm, grain type short bold (drdpat list). Non-lodging and non-shattering (CSC record). Morphological characteristics are recorded as Unknown in the CSC record. Quality traits from the NRRI report: low glycemic index below 60 and water uptake above 200 ml per 100 g. An Eastern India study places the variety in the high head rice recovery group (above 65%).
agronomic_details.field_trials: No multi-location trial results found. agronomic_details.adaptation: Suitable for coastal saline soil of the Konkan region (original variety record). Accepted in Thane, Palghar, Raigad, Ratnagiri and Sindhudurg districts of Maharashtra (isasat source).

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: LUNISREE (rice)

Name note: The CSC release minutes name is "Lunisree" and the Seednet name is "LUNISREE." The CRRI sources spell it "Lunishree," with the same 1992 release year, 145-day duration, and LS grain type, so I treat them as the same variety. That match is my inference, not something a source states outright. Seednet itself was not in the search results.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Coastal saline and waterlogged areas recommendation; field tolerance to major pests and diseases, saline tolerance noted for Lunishree (CRRI 1968-2024 variety table) -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/CRRIs-varieties-1968-2024.pdf
- Described as having high resistance to salinity (press report, CRRI) -- https://www.downtoearth.org.in/environment/super-rice-28364
- Suitable for BPH-endemic areas of Odisha (listed alongside the Lunishree row, unclear whether it applies to this variety) -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/CRRIs-varieties-1968-2024.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- No major diseases or pests reported (Bihar varieties list entry) -- https://drdpat.bih.nic.in/Rice%20Varieties%20-%2006.htm
- Field tolerance to major pests and diseases (CRRI table) -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/CRRIs-varieties-1968-2024.pdf
- Blast and seedling blight listed against Lunishree in an NRRI-variety compilation (the table layout does not show a clear resistance rating) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/339527323_Rice_Varieties_of_NRRI_Yield_Quality_Special_Traits_and_Tolerance_to_Biotic_and_Abiotic_Stresses

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Tall plant (130 cm), long-slender white grain, yield 45-50 q/ha (Bihar variety list) -- https://drdpat.bih.nic.in/Rice%20Varieties%20-%2006.htm
- Duration 145 days, yield potential 4.5 t/ha, Orissa/CVRC release (CRRI seed-chain table) -- http://www.crri.nic.in/Farmerscorner/seedchain_ricevariety.htm
- Yields reportedly 28-30% above other high-yielding varieties; needs minimal fertiliser; breeding aimed at under 120-day maturity (press report, 2000s, date not confirmed) -- https://www.downtoearth.org.in/environment/super-rice-28364
- Good general combiner for CGR, harvest index, biological yield and 100-grain weight in a crossing study (parent) -- https://assignmentpoint.com/research-paper-on-various-aspects-regarding-cultivation-of-rice/

GENETICS AND QTL
- Mutant selection from Nonasail by gamma irradiation followed by selection; pedigree CRM-30 (CSC parentage field, as supplied; not independently confirmed by a search result)
- IET number IET-10678 (Bihar variety list) -- https://drdpat.bih.nic.in/Rice%20Varieties%20-%2006.htm
- No QTL or marker study found

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developed by ICAR-Central Rice Research Institute (CRRI), Cuttack; CRRI released 186 varieties 1968-2025 including this one (CRRI variety report) -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/CRRIs-varieties-1968-2024.pdf
- CRRI director B. Venketaswarlu is quoted on the variety; no lead breeder named -- https://www.downtoearth.org.in/environment/super-rice-28364
- Lead breeder name: No evidence found

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute name and city only: ICAR-Central Rice Research Institute, Cuttack (Odisha); institute website domain shown in the CRRI report: icar-crri.in -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/CRRIs-varieties-1968-2024.pdf
- Official email, phone, postal address, and breeder contact: No evidence found

PUBLICATIONS
- Lunisree is listed among 11 rice varieties in a grain phenol colour study; authors and journal not captured in the search result. (2021?) Variation in phenol colour reaction in grains of rice (Oryza sativa L.) varieties. Journal not identified -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/362545223_Variation_in_phenol_colour_reaction_in_grains_of_rice_Oryza_sativa_L_varieties
- Authors unknown (2020?) Rice Varieties of NRRI: Yield, Quality, Special Traits and Tolerance to Biotic and Abiotic Stresses. Compilation, affiliation listed as Central Rice Research Institute -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/339527323_Rice_Varieties_of_NRRI_Yield_Quality_Special_Traits_and_Tolerance_to_Biotic_and_Abiotic_Stresses
- Crossing study with Lunisree as a parent (authors, year, and journal not captured) -- https://assignmentpoint.com/research-paper-on-various-aspects-regarding-cultivation-of-rice/
- KrishiKosh theses and AICRP reports: No evidence found (not searched directly; the research search returned no hits)

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Notified paddy variety for Orissa (global-agriculture list, 2022) -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/list-of-notified-paddy-varieties-for-orissa/
- Seed dealers, NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, or SAU stock: No evidence found

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Coastal Saline and Waterlogged Areas (Bihar list) -- https://drdpat.bih.nic.in/Rice%20Varieties%20-%2006.htm
- Orissa/Odisha, CVRC release; coastal saline ecosystem (CRRI seed-chain table) -- http://www.crri.nic.in/Farmerscorner/seedchain_ricevariety.htm
- The Seednet "recommended states" field was "Unknown"; these sources give Odisha and coastal saline areas, and the Bihar list gives the coastal saline/waterlogged recommendation.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: NLR-145 (rice)

Name note: variety_name (CSC) and seednet_variety_name are both "NLR-145". The sources use "NLR 145" or "NLR145" and the local name "Swarnamukhi (NLR145)". Seednet itself was not returned by any search, so the Seednet listing could not be checked. The record's release year (1993) conflicts with the 1991 year in the Nellore station list below.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance in NLR-145. The searches returned other varieties instead, including KRL 213 (salt tolerance) in the ICAR 2010-11 Rice report, KRL 213 showed salt tolerance and good yielding ability with superiority in grain yield. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-05/crop-improvement-AR-2010-11_0.pdf (different variety, not used).

DISEASE AND PEST
The Regional Agricultural Research Station Tirupati list of Nellore-released varieties gives Swarnamukhi (NLR145) as released in 1991 and describes it as medium duration with blast resistance -- https://rarstpt.org/files/rars/ASRN_R_Technologies.pdf and http://www.rarstpt.org/index.php/arsnellorevarieties.html
No pest-resistance evidence found for NLR-145.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Maturity: Swarnamukhi (NLR145) · 1991 · Medium duration rice with blast resistance -- http://www.rarstpt.org/index.php/arsnellorevarieties.html (medium duration only; no day count found).
Yield: No evidence found. No yield data or multi-location trial results for NLR-145 were returned.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Recorded parentage (CICA 4/IR 625-23-3-1/TETOP): No evidence found. No source returned this pedigree.
NLR145 as a parent: the Bapatla station notable-achievements PDF lists Bhavathi (BPT 2782), released 2020, with parentage NLR145/MTU 2077, bred by pedigree method -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/7.%20ARS,%20Bapatla%20Notable%20Achievements.pdf (this is a different variety that uses NLR-145 as a parent, not evidence of NLR-145's own pedigree).
NLR145 as a parent (second case): Nellore Sugandha variety is a cross between Nellore Swarnamukhi (NLR 145) and Vajram (MTU 5249) -- https://www.thehansindia.com/andhra-pradesh/andhra-pradesh-government-releases-three-new-rice-varieties-632705
QTL, markers, breeding-line codes beyond NLR 145, genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Institution: the Rice Research station at Nellore is part of Acharya N.G. Ranga Agricultural University (ANGRAU). The Tirupati station list attributes the Nellore-developed varieties, including Swarnamukhi (NLR145), to this station -- http://www.rarstpt.org/index.php/arsnellorevarieties.html
Developer: a 2019 news report says scientists developed NLR 145 (Swarnamukhi) for local needs -- https://www.thehansindia.com/andhra-pradesh/paddy-cultivation-area-drops-significantly-in-nellore-dist-785149
Lead breeder name: No evidence found. The Principal Scientist Dr P Ramesh Babu quoted in the Hans India release article is linked to Nellore Sugandha (NLR 40054), not NLR-145, so he is not attributed here.

CONTACT DETAILS
ANGRAU seed availability list (as on 10.01.2022), entry for ARS Nellore, Paddy, NLR 145: contact Dr. P. Rajasekhar, Principal Scientist (Ento) & Head, phone 9490327424, email ars.nellore@angrau.ac.in -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/Seed_Availability_in_ANGRAU_as_on_10_01_2022.pdf
Caveat: the PDF extraction is jumbled. The phone 9848148522 and email ars.reddipalli@angrau.ac.in appear beside the ARS Reddipalli entry, so they were not used.
Postal address of ARS Nellore: No evidence found. The only address returned belongs to the Regional Agricultural Research Station, Tirupati-517502, which publishes the Nellore variety list -- http://www.rarstpt.org/index.php/arsnellorevarieties.html
Institute contact page: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found for a paper, AICRP report, thesis or conference paper on NLR-145. The search returned Rajan C.P.D., Rajasekhar P., Vineetha U. (2016). Journal of Rice Research, 9(2), ARS Nellore -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/Untitled16.pdf. It was excluded because the retrieved text covers aromatic breeding lines (e.g., NLR 40054) and does not name NLR-145.
KrishiKosh and AICRP searches returned no NLR-145 records.

SEED AVAILABILITY
ARS Nellore, Paddy, NLR 145, Breeder Seed, quantity listed as 1.20 (unit not stated in the extraction), in the ANGRAU seed availability list as on 10.01.2022 -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/Seed_Availability_in_ANGRAU_as_on_10_01_2022.pdf
Seednet listing: No evidence found (the Seednet pages returned were generic portal pages).
NSC, State Seed Corporation (APSSDCL), KVK or private dealer listings for NLR-145: No evidence found. The AP State Seeds paddy page returned has no NLR-145 row in the retrieved text -- https://apseeds.ap.gov.in/Website/Paddy.aspx

RECOMMENDED STATES
The record says "Unknown". The evidence points to Andhra Pradesh only: the variety was developed at the Nellore station and reported for Nellore district use -- https://www.thehansindia.com/andhra-pradesh/paddy-cultivation-area-drops-significantly-in-nellore-

Developed by introgressing yield-component genes from an O. rufipogon accession collected from submerged areas; the source does not state a submergence tolerance score -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/250278469_CSR23_a_new_salt-tolerant_rice_variety_for_India
Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found for Dhanrasi (IET 15358). The drought-yield and disease figures on the ICAR-IIRR technologies PDF sit next to a different DRR Dhan entry, so I excluded them -- https://icar-iirr.org/Technologies/Innovative%20Technologies.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
Reaction recorded as R-BL (resistant to blast) and MR-BLB, with RTV and ShR listed (abbreviations as printed; not expanded in the source) -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/CROP-IMPROVEMENT-01_0.pdf
Blast, neck blast and bacterial blight reactions as summarised in the release table -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0
Pest resistance (insects, gall midge, BPH): No evidence found; the Zenodo record carries a "Pest resistance" tag but no pest data in the retrieved text -- https://zenodo.org/records/6999561

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Late duration, rainfed shallow lowland, semi-dwarf, long slender-to-short bold grain; 115-120 days to flowering in the ICAR table -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0 ; https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/CROP-IMPROVEMENT-01_0.pdf
Yield range 5.5-6.5 t/ha (ICAR table); 50-65 q/ha (Agropedia) -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/CROP-IMPROVEMENT-01_0.pdf ; http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0
1996 Andhra Pradesh trial: 6.2 t/ha, against 6.1 for Swarna and 6.2 for the best check; a 1996 yield of 5.28 t/ha was 13.3% and 2.5% above national checks Pranava and Salivahana -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/250278469_CSR23_a_new_salt-tolerant_rice_variety_for_India
Dhanrasi was the best check at 5.7 t/ha in a later trial of 44 lines (about 24% below the top line) -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Mahender-Anumalla/publication/301588915_Genetic_diversity_and_maternal_lineage_among_early_maturing_genotypes_of_Indica_and_Japonica/links/576a19c108ae2d7145ba8be8/Genetic-diversity-and-maternal-lineage-among-early-maturing-genotypes-of-Indica-and-Japonica.pdf
Grain quality: medium slender, glycemic index 51.2, head rice recovery 70.1% -- https://icar-iirr.org/Technologies/Innovative%20Technologies.pdf (the same PDF has conflicting Dhanrasi entries; treat as indicative)

EVIDENCE DIGEST: Upahar (OR 1234-12-1) (IET 17318), Rice

Search status: Four searches ran in one batch. I then tried to re-read the full text of the hits, but the tool-use limit blocked that, so the findings below rest on truncated snippets (about 300 characters each). Several hits, including the Bihar notified-variety list, the Odisha rice bulletin and the Odisha seed-distribution report, may mention this variety further down, and I could not check them. Treat the gaps below as "not yet verified," not as confirmed absence. Seednet was not searched by its own name.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Listed in a paddy variety table as suited to shallow and semi-deep water conditions, which describes ecology rather than tested flood or submergence tolerance; no drought, heat, salinity or submergence data found -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0

DISEASE AND PEST
- The same table lists resistance to sheath blight, bacterial leaf blight, rice tungro virus and a sheath-related disease (abbreviated "Sh R" in the snippet, possibly sheath rot; unverified) -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0
- No insect-pest resistance data found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Table entry gives plant height of about 124 cm, maturity noted as late (162 days in the snippet), and a yield range of 35–84 q/ha. The snippet was cut off, so the yield units and conditions could not be confirmed in full -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0
- No multi-location trial results found.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Breeding-line code "OR 1234-12-1" and IET number "IET 17318" appear in the same table entry -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0
- Parentage "Mahalaxmi/IR 62" (from the input record) was not confirmed by any search result.
- No QTL, marker or genome studies found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- No named breeder or scientist found in any result.
- The institution in the input record (Rice Research Station, OUAT, Bhubaneswar) was not confirmed by any search result. No search result named it in connection with this variety.

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder contact, institute email, phone or address found. No institute contact page URL was located.

PUBLICATIONS
- No evidence found. The searches returned no papers, AICRP reports or theses naming this variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found for this variety. A 2020 Odisha seed-distribution report on Angul, Gajapati and Puri appeared in results, but the snippet seen does not name this variety; the full text was not checked.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- The input record gives "Unknown." The agropedia entry did not state recommended states. No other source confirmed a state recommendation.

RECORD DISCREPANCIES TO RESOLVE
- Release year: input record says 2005 (CSC); the agropedia table shows 2006 next to the variety name. Verify against the CSC notification or the Seednet entry.
- Spelling: the table uses "Uphar" and "OR 1234-12-1" in a garbled form; match against the official notification before using either spelling.

Suggested next steps: check the Seednet record under "Upahar(OR 1234-12-1) (IET 17318)" and the Bihar notified-variety PDF, which may list this variety with its notification details, and search KrishiKosh and the OUAT Rice Research Station pages directly.

drought.details: CSC variety data and the digest describe the variety as moderately drought tolerant, suited to direct-seeded, drought-prone rainfed upland and lowland areas of eastern Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Chhattisgarh. Agropedia lists moderate drought tolerance. A drought-screening study of 75 genotypes used Shusk Samrat as a check: its relative water content under water stress was lower than IR64 and Sahbhagi Dhan, and it was relatively low yielding under stress. It is also listed among drought-tolerant varieties for rainfed eastern India with a sowing window up to the first week of July. The digest notes it was tolerant of low-fertility stress, but no mechanism-level data were found.

heat.details: Not found in searched sources. The searches returned no page on heat tolerance for this variety.

salinity.details: Not found in searched sources. The searches returned no page on salinity tolerance for this variety.

flood.details: Not found in searched sources. The searches returned no page on flood tolerance for this variety.

disease_resistance.summary: Moderate resistance to brown spot (Cochliobolus miyabeanus) and sheath blight; resistance to sheath rot (eurekamag, agropedia). CSC variety data gives moderate resistance to brown spot and sheath blight, and resistance to sheath rot. Leaf blast is not confirmed: a garbled ResearchGate table lists leaf blast, brown spot and sheath blight for a 'Shushk Samrat' row, but the row attribution is uncertain and leaf blast is excluded from the confirmed list.

pest_resistance.summary: Moderate resistance to gall midge (eurekamag). CSC variety data also lists moderate resistance to stem borer, gall midge, leaf folder and whorl maggot; this CSC record is not a digest URL and is cited here only as ground-truth variety data. The digest found no evidence for other insect pests or nematodes beyond gall midge.

agronomic_details.yield: CSC record: 3000-3500 kg/ha (30-35 q/ha) under normal conditions. NDUAT lists 35-40 q/ha. A 2018 Indian Journal of Agronomy trial reported grain yields of about 4.3 and 4.5 t/ha for Shusk Samrat under two establishment methods, though the table labels are unclear. Yield figures in the ResearchGate drought-tolerance paper are garbled and not used.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources for multi-location stability. Under drought stress in a 75-genotype screen, it was relatively low yielding.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Direct-seeded upland and rainfed drought-prone conditions in eastern Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Odisha (listed as Orissa in sources) and Chhattisgarh. Sowing window up to the first week of July in rainfed eastern India.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Plant height about 95-100 cm, long-bold grain type (agropedia). Non-lodging and easy threshability (CSC record). Fertilizer responsive (CSC record). Note: agropedia and NDUAT give duration of 100-105 days, which differs from the 95-100 day CSC and adaptation figure.
