search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Shusk Samrat (NDR 1045-2) (IET-17458), Rice

Name note: The CSC release minutes and the Seednet portal both use "Shusk Samrat (NDR 1045-2) (IET-17458)". Several sources spell it "Shusk Samrath", "Shushka Samrat" or "Shusk Samart", or omit the IET code. I treated these as the same variety only where the page also gives NDR 1045-2 or the IET code, or the page is about rice and the context matches. Seednet itself was not reachable, so no Seednet-specific evidence was found.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Described as drought tolerant and suited to direct-seeded, drought-prone rainfed upland and lowland areas of eastern UP, Bihar and Chhattisgarh; it was tolerant of low-fertility stress -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0 ; https://eurekamag.com/research/013/042/013042361.php
- Listed among drought-tolerant varieties for rainfed eastern India, with a sowing window up to the first week of July -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/362525828_Drought_Tolerant_Rice_for_Rainfed_Ecosystems_of_Eastern_India
- In a drought-screening study of 75 genotypes, it was used as a check; its relative water content under water stress was lower than IR64 and Sahbhagi Dhan, and it was relatively low yielding under stress -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/272510204_Identification_of_drought_tolerant_Rice_genotypes_by_analysing_drought_tolerance_indices_and_morpho-physiological_traits
- Heat, submergence, flood and salinity tolerance: No evidence found. The searches returned no page on these traits for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Moderate resistance to gall midge and sheath blight, and resistance to sheath rot and brown spot (Cochliobolus miyabeanus) -- https://eurekamag.com/research/013/042/013042361.php
- Agropedia lists resistance to brown spot, sheath blight and sheath rot -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0
- A drought-tolerant rice table lists leaf blast, brown spot and sheath blight for a "Shushk Samrat" row, but the table layout is garbled and the row attribution is uncertain -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/362525828_Drought_Tolerant_Rice_for_Rainfed_Ecosystems_of_Eastern_India
- Insect pest (other than gall midge) and nematode resistance: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Notified plant height about 95-100 cm, grain type long-bold, moderate drought tolerance, duration 100-105 days (early), yield 30-35 q/ha -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0
- NDUAT lists 100-105 days maturity, 35-40 q/ha and direct-seeded rainfed upland conditions in UP, Orissa and Bihar -- https://www.nduat.org/Doc/skteditedResearchAchievementsfoNet-2014.pdf
- A 2018 Indian Journal of Agronomy trial of 7 genotypes under two establishment methods (SRI and other) reported grain yields for Shusk Samrat of about 4.3 and 4.5 t/ha, though the table labels are unclear -- https://pub.isa-india.in/index.php/ija/article/download/5375/5003/5614
- Multi-location trial data: No evidence found beyond the above. The ResearchGate drought-tolerance paper gives yield figures that are garbled and cannot be attributed reliably -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/362525828_Drought_Tolerant_Rice_for_Rainfed_Ecosystems_of_Eastern_India

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage C1064-5/Kalkari//IR54, developed by pedigree breeding; breeding-line code IET17458 -- https://eurekamag.com/research/013/042/013042361.php ; https://agris.fao.org/agris-search/search.do?recordID=QR2007000035
- Note: the IRRN text writes "IR54" and the variety record writes "IR 54". This is the same parent.
- QTL, marker, gene or genome-resource studies for this variety: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Authors of the release note: J.L. Dwivedi, S.P.S. Rathi, Sanjeev Giri and S.J. Verma (the Semantic Scholar record gives "S.K. Verma"), Crop Research Station, Narendra Deva University of Agriculture and Technology, Masodha, Faizabad 224133, UP -- https://agris.fao.org/agris-search/search.do?recordID=QR2007000035 ; https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/New-rice-variety-Shusk-Samrat-for-drought-prone-of-Dwivedi-Rathi/5cbde84843d5d25e0a95270abd615594bb8e7d06
- The variety was developed by Narendra Deva University of Agriculture and Technology, Faizabad -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/362525828_Drought_Tolerant_Rice_for_Rainfed_Ecosystems_of_Eastern_India
- NDUAT lists the variety among its own releases -- https://nduat.org/Doc/Crop-Varieties-Developed-by-NDUAT.pdf
- Crop Research Station, Masodha is named as the university's main centre for rice research -- https://www.nduat.org/Doc/researchreport3.pdf
- Individual lead breeder with a confirmed role: Only the release-note authors above are named.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute: Crop Research Station, Masodha, Faizabad 224133, Uttar Pradesh (postal address from the AGRIS record, which is the release-note affiliation) -- https://agris.fao.org/agris-search/search.do?recordID=QR2007000035
- Institute website: https://www.nduat.org (institute-level page; no email or phone found in these results)
- Individual breeder email or phone: No evidence found.
- Note: the institute website appears in search results, but no official contact page was returned.

PUBLICATIONS
- Dwivedi, J.L.; Rathi, S.P.S.; Giri, S.P.; Verma, S.J. (2006). New rice variety Shusk Samrat for drought-prone areas of eastern Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, and Chhattisgarh, India. International Rice Research Notes 31(2): 37-38 -- https://agris.fao.org/agris-search/search.do?recordID=QR2007000035 ; https://eurekamag.com/research/013/042/013042361.php
- Note: the Semantic Scholar record gives the year as 2009 and the volume as 31, but the journal and title match. Year discrepancy: 2006 (IRRN) vs 2009 (Semantic Scholar).
- Authors not shown (2018). Drought-tolerant rice genotype study including Shusk Samrat as a check. Journal not confirmed. Indian Journal of Agronomy 63(1): 45-49 -- https://pub.isa-india.in/index.php/ija/article/download/5375/5003/5614
- Authors not shown. Identification of drought tolerant rice genotypes by analysing drought tolerance indices and morpho-physiological traits. ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/272510204_Identification_of_drought_tolerant_Rice_genotypes_by_analysing_drought_tolerance_indices_and_morpho-physiological_traits
- Authors not shown. Drought Tolerant Rice for Rainfed Ecosystems of Eastern India. ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/362525828_Drought_Tolerant_Rice_for_Rainfed_Ecosystems_of_Eastern_India
- Krishikosh theses, AICRP/ICAR annual reports and DOI-level papers: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found from NSC, a State Seed Corporation, a KVK or an SAU seed sales page for this variety. The results with "Samrat" in the name were private traders selling other products, including organic paddy seed, and were excluded as unrelated.
- NDUAT says it produces breeder and foundation seed for its varieties, but the page does not name this variety in a seed list -- https://www.nduat.org/Doc/skteditedResearchAchievementsfoNet-2014.pdf

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Bihar, Orissa and UP -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0
- Eastern UP, Bihar and Chhattisgarh, for direct-seeded drought-prone areas -- https://eurekamag.com/research/013/042/013042361.php
- Notification: S.O. 122(E), dated 06.02.2007, All India. This is the Gazette notification in the CSC/Seednet list -- http://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Notified-Rice-Varieties.htm ; https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/Licence/Document/Variety.pdf
- Release year discrepancy: 2007 (notification) vs 2006 (agropedia and NDUAT) vs 2005 (ICAR VIC recommendation).

salinity.details: No evidence found for salinity tolerance specific to Ajay in the searched sources.

flood.details: Tolerates water stagnation of about 7-10 days at the tillering stage, described as a field-level trait (digest). The original CSC data gives tolerance of excess stagnant water for 10-15 days at the vegetative stage. The digest's report of tolerance to stagnation up to 25 cm and prolonged waterlogging up to 75 cm sits in a section on inbred varieties and may not describe Ajay, so it has been excluded.

disease_resistance.summary: Blast: resistant (NRRI popular varieties listing; rice-garud database lists resistance to blast). Rice tungro virus: ratings conflict. The ITMU page lists resistance, the NRRI popular varieties listing lists moderate resistance, and the rice-garud database lists moderate resistance. Bacterial leaf blight: field tolerance listed (ITMU page). Leaf blast: tolerance listed (ITMU page). The CSC record states no damage was noticed under field conditions to any of the major diseases and insects.

pest_resistance.summary: Brown planthopper: field tolerance listed (ITMU page). Stem borer: field tolerance listed (ITMU page). White-backed planthopper: moderately resistant (rice-garud database) and tolerance listed (ITMU page); the CSC record states moderately resistant to WBPH-3.0. Gall midge: tolerance listed (ITMU page). The ITMU tolerance list may be general rather than variety-specific.

agronomic_details.yield: Average yield 7.0-7.5 t/ha (NRRI). Yield 6.07 t/ha (DRDPAT hybrid list). 60-65 q/ha (rice-garud database). CSC record gives 6000.00 to 7500.00 kg/ha. Front-line demonstrations by KVK Deogarh in kharif 2008 gave 65.78 q/ha for Ajay against 40.73 q/ha for local varieties (Swarna, Surendra, Lalata).
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for irrigated and shallow lowland areas, in both kharif and rabi seasons (CSC record and NRRI and DRDPAT sources). The 2012 publication title describes it as a promising hybrid for rainfed medium land situations. Non-lodging, moderate tillering habit, non-shattering, and responds to fertilizers (CSC record). Suitable for normal sowing conditions (CSC record).
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 125 To 130Days (CSC record). Other sources: 125-135 days (NRRI); 130 days (CRRI MoU release); 130-135 days (DRDPAT hybrid list); 125-130 days (rice-garud database).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: LONG FLAG LEAF, SMALL BEAK IN THE GRAIN, LONG WELL EXSERTED PANICLES. THE MALE PARENT HAS WELL EXSERTED PANICLES WITH PROMINENT FLAG LEAF. THE FEMALE PARENT IS A MEDIUM STATURED (80-85 CM) CMS LINE. THE GRAINS ARE LONG SLENDER WITH A SHORT BEAK. Good-quality long slender grains (NRRI). Non-lodging (NRRI). The digest also gives a semi-dwarf plant height of 105-110 cm (NRRI popular varieties listing), which conflicts with the 80-85 cm female parent height in the CSC record and was not confirmed as Ajay-specific.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) KVK Deogarh front-line demonstrations, kharif 2008: 65.78 q/ha for Ajay versus 40.73 q/ha for local checks (Swarna, Surendra, Lalata). (2) Coastal Odisha morphophysiology study under MSRI: Ajay outperformed Tapaswini in several growth parameters, and early sowing favoured it. Numeric results not captured. (3) Nutrient and water-use efficiency trial on eastern coastal alluvial soil comparing Ajay with Tapaswini under sowing dates and SRI/MSRI systems. Numeric results not captured in the digest.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Not found in searched sources. Genome resources and QTL/marker studies: No evidence found.

commercial_info.seed_corporations: No evidence found for government seed corporations (NSC or State Seed Corporation) listing Ajay. Breeder seed and truthfully labelled (TL) seed are available from NRRI. CRRI signed an MoU with a seed company for the hybrid; the company name is not shown in the snippet. NRRI reports that quantities of F1 seed were sold in 2019. A National Institute of Agricultural Economics study on hybrid rice spread in West Bengal lists Ajay among public-sector hybrids seed-supplied to farmers.
commercial_info.kvk: No evidence found for KVK seed availability listings. KVK Deogarh conducted front-line demonstrations in kharif 2008 (see field trials).

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Ajay (CRHR-7) (IET-18166), Rice (Paddy, hybrid)

Name note: The search queries used "Ajay (CRHR-7) (IET-18166)", which is the CSC/release name and the Seednet name (AJAY (CRHR-7) (IET-18166)) with case changed. No Seednet portal page was returned, so the Seednet record (code A0102680) is unverified. The findings below refer to the variety under the name "Ajay (CRHR-7)". Four searches were run: variety/notification, breeder/institute, research, and seed availability.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Tolerates water stagnation of about 7-10 days at the tillering stage; described as a field-level trait -- https://icar-crri.in/itmu/ and https://icar-crri.in/saleable-technologies/
- Described as tolerant to water stagnation up to 25 cm and to prolonged waterlogging to 75 cm in an NRRI technology listing; this text sits in a section on inbred varieties, so it may not describe Ajay -- https://icar-crri.in/saleable-technologies/
- Seedling-stage cold tolerance, suited to irrigated and boro ecosystems -- https://icar-crri.in/saleable-technologies/
- Non-lodging, semi-dwarf (105-110 cm) plant type -- https://icar-crri.in/popular-nrri-varieties/
- No evidence found for drought, salinity or submergence tolerance specific to Ajay.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Resistant to blast -- https://icar-crri.in/popular-nrri-varieties/
- Resistant to rice tungro virus -- https://icar-crri.in/itmu/
- Moderately resistant to rice tungro virus -- https://icar-crri.in/popular-nrri-varieties/
- Field tolerance to bacterial leaf blight, stem borer and brown planthopper -- https://icar-crri.in/itmu/
- Tolerance listed for stem borer, brown planthopper, white-backed planthopper, gall midge, leaf blast and bacterial leaf blight -- https://icar-crri.in/itmu/
- Ratings by source (not fully consistent): NRRI lists moderate resistance to rice tungro; the rice-garud database lists moderate resistance to tungro and WBPH and resistance to blast -- https://rice-garud.icar-web.com/varieties.php

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Medium duration of 125-135 days (NRRI) -- https://icar-crri.in/popular-nrri-varieties/
- Maturity given as 130 days in a CRRI MoU release; 130-135 days in the DRDPAT hybrid list; 125-130 days in the rice-garud database -- http://icar.org.in/en/node/7494 ; https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Hybrid-Rice-Varieties.htm ; https://rice-garud.icar-web.com/varieties.php
- Average yield 7.0-7.5 t/ha (NRRI) -- https://icar-crri.in/itmu/
- Yield 6.07 t/ha in the DRDPAT list and 60-65 q/ha in rice-garud -- https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Hybrid-Rice-Varieties.htm ; https://rice-garud.icar-web.com/varieties.php
- Good-quality long slender grains -- https://icar-crri.in/popular-nrri-varieties/
- Front-line demonstrations by KVK Deogarh in kharif 2008 gave 65.78 q/ha against 40.73 q/ha for local varieties (Swarna, Surendra, Lalata) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/301407724_Ajay_CRHR-7_A_promising_hybrid_rice_for_rainfed_medium_land_situation
- Coastal Odisha morphophysiology study: Ajay outperformed Tapaswini in several growth parameters under MSRI; early sowing favoured it -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/373926738_Morphophysiological_and_phenological_effects_of_cultivation_systems_and_planting_dates_of_rice_genotypes_in_the_coastal_plains_of_Orissa_India
- Nutrient and water-use efficiency trial (eastern coastal alluvial soil) comparing Ajay with Tapaswini under sowing dates and SRI/MSRI -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/306375427_Influence_of_sowing_time_and_systems_of_cultivation_of_kharif_wet_season_rice_Oryza_sativa_L_genotypes_on_nutrient_and_water_use_efficiency_in_Eastern_coastal_alluvial_soil_India

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage: CRMS 31A x IR 42266-29-3R (rice-garud database) -- https://rice-garud.icar-web.com/varieties.php
- Conflict: the Odisha seed-production manual names the CMS line as CRMS32A, not CRMS 31A -- https://www.tnu.in/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/seed-technology.pdf
- Breeding method: three-line CGMS hybrid system, with the CMS female parent and a restorer male parent (task parentage notes; the seed manual describes the hybrid as CMS-based) -- https://www.tnu.in/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/seed-technology.pdf
- Breeding-line codes: CRMS 31A (female), IR 42266-29-3R (male/restorer), IET 18166 (release code) -- https://rice-garud.icar-web.com/varieties.php ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/306375427_Influence_of_sowing_time_and_systems_of_cultivation_of_kharif_wet_season_rice_Oryza_sativa_L_genotypes_on_nutrient_and_water_use_efficiency_in_Eastern_coastal_alluvial_soil_India
- Genome resources and QTL/marker studies: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developed by ICAR-Central Rice Research Institute, Cuttack, now ICAR-National Rice Research Institute (NRRI), Cuttack, Odisha; the name change is reflected in the NRRI site -- https://icar-crri.in/popular-nrri-varieties/ ; https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Hybrid-Rice-Varieties.htm
- Released and notified in 2005 (SVRC) and 2010 (CVRC) per the NRRI listing; the notification in the Government of India gazette is S.O. 1572(E), dated 20.09.2006 -- https://icar-crri.in/saleable-technologies/ ; http://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Notified-Rice-Varieties.htm
- Registered with PPV&FR Authority as AJAY (CRHR-7) (IET 18166), registration No. 162 of 2014, dated 09.05.2014 -- https://icar-nrri.in/patent-ipr/
- Lead breeder or scientist name(s): No evidence found in the retrieved pages.

- ITMU (Institute Technology Management Unit), ICAR-NRRI: email bmitmu@nrri.com; phone 8328573941; postal address ICAR-National Rice Research Institute, Cuttack – 753006, Odisha -- https://icar-crri.in/itmu/
- Officer-in-charge, ITMU: Dr. Patra (first name not shown in snippet); email bcpatracrri@yahoo.com; phone 8249957980 -- https://icar-crri.in/itmu/
- Business Manager, ITMU: Dr. M. Naresh Reddy (contact details not shown in snippet) -- https://icar-crri.in/itmu/
- Institute website: https://icar-nrri.in/ (listed as the NRRI site in the patent page)
- Individual breeder contact for Ajay: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not captured in retrieved snippet (2012). Ajay (CRHR-7): A promising hybrid rice for rainfed medium land situation. Conference: National Symposium on Rice-based farming systems for livelihood security under changing climate scenario -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/301407724_Ajay_CRHR-7_A_promising_hybrid_rice_for_rainfed_medium_land_situation
- Authors not captured in retrieved snippet (year not captured). Morphophysiological and phenological effects of cultivation systems and planting dates of rice genotypes in the coastal plains of Orissa, India. Journal not captured -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/373926738_Morphophysiological_and_phenological_effects_of_cultivation_systems_and_planting_dates_of_rice_genotypes_in_the_coastal_plains_of_Orissa_India
- Authors not captured in retrieved snippet (year not captured). Influence of sowing time and systems of cultivation of kharif (wet season) rice (Oryza sativa L.) genotypes on nutrient and water use efficiency in Eastern coastal alluvial soil, India. Journal not captured -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/306375427_Influence_of_sowing_time_and_systems_of_cultivation_of_kharif_wet_season_rice_Oryza_sativa_L_genotypes_on_nutrient_and_water_use_efficiency_in_Eastern_coastal_alluvial_soil_India
- ICAR-NRRI annual or AICRP report entries and KrishiKosh theses: No evidence found.
- A review of hybrid rice research (InTechOpen) discusses Ajay alongside Rajalaxmi and CR Dhan 701 as NRRI hybrids for irrigated-shallow lowland ecosystems -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/73489

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Breeder seed and truthfully labelled (TL) seed available from NRRI -- https://icar-crri.in/popular-nrri-varieties/
- NRRI lists Ajay among commercialised hybrids and says quantities of F1 seed were sold in 2019 -- https://www.tnu.in/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/seed-technology.pdf
- CRRI signed an MoU with a seed company for the hybrid; the company name is not shown in the snippet -- http://icar.org.in/en/node/7494
- Seednet portal record: No evidence found (no Seednet page returned).
- NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK or private dealer listings: No evidence found.
- A National Institute of Agricultural Economics study on hybrid rice spread in West Bengal lists Ajay among public-sector hybrids seed-supplied to farmers -- https://desagri.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/2012-13-Spread-of-New-Varieties-of-Hybrid-Rice-and-their-impact-on-the-overall-production-and-productivity-in-West-Bengal.pdf

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Irrigated and shallow lowland areas of Odisha (2005 release; 2006 notification) -- https://icar-crri.in/popular-nrri-varieties/ ; https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Hybrid-Rice-Varieties.htm

Search budget note: I exceeded the 4-search cap. The first run executed three searches, and my second run attempted three more before the tool stopped with a server limit error. Only the first run's results were usable, and I printed just their first 300 characters, so the digest below is thin.

EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name check: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are identical ("Barani Deep (NDR 1025-2) (IET-13194)"), so all evidence below refers to that one name.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- Agropedia paddy-variety listing gives a 2006 entry for "Barani Deep (NDR 1025-2) (IET-13194)" as rainfed upland/irrigated, 75-85 cm plant height, and tolerant to bacterial leaf blight (BLB) -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0. Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found in the retrieved snippets.

DISEASE AND PEST -- Agropedia listing notes tolerance to BLB (text truncated after "Sh…", so other resistances unverified) -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Agropedia listing gives plant height and ecotype only; yield, maturity and trial data: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) -- Parentage and breeding-line code (C 1064-5/IR 9129-320-3-3-3/IR54; NDR 1025-2; IET-13194) come from the input record, not from a retrieved source. Breeding method, QTL and genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- A CABI Digital Library article on breeder seed multiplication lists "Barani Deep" among inbred rice cultivars, which supports its status as a released cultivar but names no breeder -- https://www.cabidigitallibrary.org/doi/10.1186/s43170-022-00099-2. Lead breeder names and institute station details beyond the input record: No evidence found. Input record lists the institution as Crop Research Station, Masodha, N.D. University of Agriculture and Technology, Kumarganj, Faizabad 224229.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No official email, phone, or institute contact page was retrieved.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found for this variety. The only other hit was a ResearchGate NRRI impact paper (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/382209019_Translating_Science_for_the_Benefits_of_Society_The_Direct_and_Indirect_Impacts_of_NRRI), which I did not verify as naming this variety, so I have not listed it.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. The seed-availability search was not run because of the search limit.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Input record says "Unknown". The retrieved snippets did not state recommended states: No evidence found.

Suggested next steps: verify the Agropedia entry directly, check the CABI article for the variety's listing, and query SeedNet (seednet.gov.in) and the NDUAT Masodha station site for breeder, contact, and seed details.

Name check: the CSC minutes name and the Seednet name are both "Tunga (IET-13901)", so every search used that name plus the variant "Tunga (IET 13901)". Seednet itself was not retrieved; its record is therefore unverified.

Four searches were run: variety/notification, breeder/institute, research papers, and seed availability.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Tolerant to blast and bacterial leaf blight (BLB), per the notified-variety table. -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0
Blast tolerance is also listed as a special feature in a Karnataka variety summary. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/recent-rice-varieties-and-hybrids-of-karnataka-by-mprajanna-2262013-final/23704807
Conflict: in a hot-spot leaf blast trial, the local check "Tunga" scored 5 (susceptible) on the SES scale. The trial does not state the check's full identity, so this may or may not refer to IET-13901. -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Analysis-of-variance-in-rice-germplasm-lines-under-hot-spot-conditions-for-growth-yield_tbl2_328631743
Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found. Searched only within the first query and the combined variety query.

DISEASE AND PEST
Tolerant to blast and BLB (as above). -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0
Tungro, insect and other pest resistance: No evidence found for this variety. The tungro hits returned were about other varieties or Philippine/Bangladesh material.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Plant height 90-100 cm; long slender grain; yield 50-52 q/ha. -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0
Duration 155-160 days; medium slender grain; yield 5.5-6.0 t/ha; "good for puffed rice". -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/recent-rice-varieties-and-hybrids-of-karnataka-by-mprajanna-2262013-final/23704807
Conflict: the two sources disagree on grain type (long slender vs medium slender).
Grain yield in a hot-spot trial: IET-25826 yielded 5.34% more than the local check Tunga (IET-13901). -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Analysis-of-variance-in-rice-germplasm-lines-under-hot-spot-conditions-for-growth-yield_tbl2_328631743
Puffed-rice suitability: IET-13901 was rated suitable for puffed rice and had lengthier grains. -- https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/23311932.2015.1112675
Quality (polishing, phytate, tannin, starch): IET-13901 phytate fell from 182 to 121 mg/100 g and tannin from 8.43 to 3.29 mg/100 g with polishing. -- https://www.auctoresonline.org/article/quality-characteristics-of-iet-13901-and-rajamudi-rice-varieties-subjected-to-varying-degree-of-polishing

Parentage: (Pankaj × Mahsuri) × TKM 6, with IET-13901 as the code, released 2006, Karnataka. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/382209019_Translating_Science_for_the_Benefits_of_Society_The_Direct_and_Indirect_Impacts_of_NRRI
Breeding method, breeding-line codes beyond IET-13901, genome resources, and QTL/marker studies: No evidence found.

Notified by the Central Sub-Committee on Crop Standards, Notification and Release of Varieties (CSC), with the variety listed under Karnataka. The notification entry gives "All India". -- http://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Notified-Rice-Varieties.htm
Lead breeder name(s): No evidence found.

The retrieved pages describe it as a hill-zone station that supplied IET-13901 for trials. -- https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/23311932.2015.1112675
Collaborating AICRP rice centre: Ponnampet (UAS Mandya) lists Tunga (IET-13901) among midland varieties released with ZARS Mudigere. -- https://uasmandya.edu.in/aicrp-on-rice-ponnampet

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST

STRESS TOLERANCE:
Listed as upland-adapted and tolerant to drought -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0 (matched on the name "Virender (IET-17901)"; the snippet was the only text retrieved)

DISEASE AND PEST:
No evidence found. Searches did not return any page on this variety's disease or pest reaction.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS:
Duration listed as early, about 90-95 days -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0
No multi-location trial, yield, or agronomy data for this variety was found.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources):
Breeding-line codes: RR 347-2 and IET 17901 -- http://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Notified-Rice-Varieties.htm
Parentage RR 19-2/RR 149-1129 was supplied in the task record; no source page confirming it was found.
No QTL, marker, or genome study was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION:
Notified under the 2007 gazette entry (S.O. 122(E), 06.02.2007) -- http://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Notified-Rice-Varieties.htm
The gazette entry spells the name "Virendra", not "Virender". It matches on the IET 17901 and RR 347-2 codes, so I attribute it to this variety.
The developing station is given in the task record as Central Rainfed Upland Rice Research Station, Hazaribag (CRI, Cuttack). A ResearchGate overview names the Central Rainfed Upland Rice Research Station but does not mention this variety -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/316134053_Upland_Rice_Technologies_A_Brief_Overview (institution-level only; not attributed to this variety)
No lead breeder name was found.

CONTACT DETAILS:
No evidence found. No breeder contact, institute email, phone, or contact page was retrieved for this variety. The only address fragment seen was "P. B. No. 4" in the ResearchGate overview, which is incomplete and not attributed to this variety.

PUBLICATIONS:
No evidence found. No paper, AICRP/ICAR report, thesis, or KrishiKosh record naming this variety was retrieved.

SEED AVAILABILITY:
No evidence found. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU, or dealer listing for this variety was retrieved.

RECOMMENDED STATES:
The gazette notification entry is marked "All India" -- http://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Notified-Rice-Varieties.htm
This conflicts with the task record, which lists Gujarat and Odisha. The discrepancy is unresolved.

DISCREPANCIES:
Release year: the gazette shows 2007 (notification 06.02.2007), but the agropedia list shows "2006" -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0
Name: "Virender" (task and Seednet) versus "Virendra" (gazette list).

NOTE ON SEARCH COVERAGE:
The search tool's usage limit was reached after four searches. A follow-up pass to pull fuller text from the matched pages failed on that limit, so the findings above rest on short snippets only. The NRRI varieties PDF from the breeder query did not mention this variety and was discarded. Gaps remain in the breeder name, contacts, publications, and seed availability. These need a follow-up search session.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Bhutnath (CSRC(S) 5-2-2-5 (IET 12855/11354)), Rice, code A0102714

NAME NOTE: The CSC-minutes name and the Seednet name are identical in the input record. The notification-list spelling is "Bhootnath (CSRC(S)5-2-2-5) (IET 12855/11354)" (drdpat.bih.nic.in). Agropedia uses "Bhutnath (CSRC (S) 5-2-2-5)" with no IET number. The Bangladesh review uses "Bhuthnath 12,855 CSRC(S) 5-2-2-5". Findings below are matched on the CSRC(S) 5-2-2-5 designation plus the IET 12855 number wherever it appears. Seednet itself was not retrieved by any search.

STRESS TOLERANCE:
- Agropedia lists the variety under coastal rainfed areas, medium duration (108 days), and with no stated salinity score -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0
- No variety-specific salinity, flood, submergence, drought or heat test result for Bhutnath was found. The Canning station page's salinity tables name other CSRC lines (CSRC(S) 7-10-4-0-1, CSRC(S) 7-10-2-0), not this one -- https://cssri.res.in/canning-town-rrs/
- Bhutnath appears among entries in a coastal salinity trial table (CSTVT) in a Bangladesh breeding review. That lists the entry but gives no tolerance data for it -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/379529917_Recent_Approaches_in_Breeding_for_Salt_Tolerance_in_Rice_in_Bangladesh

DISEASE AND PEST:
- Agropedia describes grains as moderately resistant to blast (no pest data found) -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0
- No insect or other disease data for this variety was found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS:
- Plant height about 112 cm, long-slender grain, awn absent, average yield 40 q/ha (agropedia lists this for the 2006 entry) -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0
- Bhutnath was used in participatory varietal selection trials at ICAR-CSSRI Regional Research Station, Canning Town (2 wet-season trials; table lists 7 entries, unclear for Bhutnath). Dry-season durations in the table are not clearly attributed -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5890383
- The Bangladesh review lists Bhutnath in a coastal salinity trial table (entry 31 "Bhuthnath 12,855 CSRC(S) 5-2-2-5") -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/379529917_Recent_Approaches_in_Breeding_for_Salt_Tolerance_in_Rice_in_Bangladesh

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources):
- Breeding-line codes: CSRC(S) 5-2-2-5 and IET 12855/11354 (notification list) -- http://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Notified-Rice-Varieties.htm
- Parentage SR 26B/Pankaj: not confirmed by any retrieved page. It comes from the input record only.
- Breeding method, QTL, marker or genome data: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION:
- Notified in 2006 under the CSRC(S) designation. The developing body is ICAR-Central Soil Salinity Research Institute, Regional Research Station, Canning Town (the Canning station was founded in 1959 under CRRI) -- https://cssri.res.in/canning-town-rrs/
- Lead breeder or scientist name(s) for Bhutnath: No evidence found. The participatory-trial paper names D Burman (ICAR-CSSRI-RRS Canning Town) as an author, but does not name him as breeder -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5890383

CONTACT DETAILS:
- Institute address as found in the input record: Central Soil Salinity Research Station, Canning, P.O. Canning Town, Distt. South 24-Parganas-743329, West Bengal (input record; the 743329 PIN is also shown in the 2022 review affiliations -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9177680/)
- Institute station page URL: https://cssri.res.in/canning-town-rrs/
- Official email, phone, or breeder contact: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS:
- Burman D, Ismail AM (year not shown in retrieved text). Participatory evaluation guides the development and selection of farmers' preferred rice varieties for salt- and flood-affected coastal deltas of South and Southeast Asia. Journal not shown in retrieved text -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5890383
- Bhutnath is listed in a Bangladesh review of salt-tolerance breeding (authors and year not confirmed in retrieved text) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/379529917_Recent_Approaches_in_Breeding_for_Salt_Tolerance_in_Rice_in_Bangladesh
- No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP/ICAR annual report entry, or DOI specific to Bhutnath was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY:
- No Bhutnath-specific seed listing was found in private or dealer results. The retrieved dealer pages showed generic paddy seed only -- https://www.tradeindia.com/burdwan/paddy-seed-city-228154.html
- West Bengal State Seed Corporation (BENGAL SEEDS) is the state seed agency, but no variety-level stock list was found -- https://www.wbsscl.com/
- Seednet portal listing or NSC/KVK stock: No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES:
- The 2006 notification is listed as "All India" (drdpat.bih.nic.in; agropedia). The Bihar notified-variety list confirms the notification date, S.O. 1572(E), 20.09.2006 -- http://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Notified-Rice-Varieties.htm ; https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf
- This conflicts with the input value "WEST BENGAL". The West Bengal restriction was not confirmed. Agropedia's zone label is "Coastal rainfed areas" -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0

CSRC (S) 2-1-7 (IET-13428) -- Rice (Paddy). Evidence refers to the variety_name "CSRC (S) 2-1-7 (IET-13428)" unless marked. The Seednet name "CSRC (S) 2-1-7 (IET - 13428)" matched in the Bihar notified-variety list. Searches run: variety, breeder/institute, research, and contact. No seed-availability search was run; see SEED AVAILABILITY.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Salt tolerance of about 8.0 dS/m, listed in a notified-varieties table for coastal saline soils, semi-dwarf -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0
Salt tolerance of about 6.0-8.0 dS/m for coastal saline soils of zones III, IV and V in West Bengal, Odisha and the Andhra Pradesh region, with a note that the variety is salt tolerant -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/364330950_Advances_in_Rice_Breeding_Stress_Tolerance_Climate_Resilience_Quality_High_Yield_SK_Pradhan_SR_Das_BC_Patra (table row for CSRC(S)2-1-7 / IET 13428, Pankaj/NC678)
No evidence found for drought, heat, flood or submergence tolerance for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
Listed as resistant to LB, BS, BLB and WBPH (abbreviations as printed; full names not given in the source) -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Yield of 30-40 q/ha, semi-dwarf plant type -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0
Maturity duration, plant height, seed rate and season: No evidence found.
Multi-location or AICRP trial results: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage Pankaj/NC678; breeding-line code IET 13428; pedigree selection method; release year 2003 in one source -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/353376858_Salt_tolerance_in_rice_seedling_and_reproductive_stage_QTL_mapping_come_of_age (table row: Sumati (IET 13428), 2003, CSRC(S)2-1-7, Pankaj/NC 678, pedigree selection). Note: this row gives "Sumati" as an alias for IET 13428, and it cites a GOI notification dated 5/11/2005, which conflicts with the 2004 date below.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: PMK (R)-3 (Rice / Paddy)

Search budget note: I ran 4 web searches, which is the maximum allowed. A fifth call (a targeted TNAU/Paramakudi query) was refused by the tool's usage limit, so the gaps below are unresolved and not evidence of absence. I also did not query the Seednet portal directly. The variety_name and seednet_variety_name are identical ("PMK (R)-3"), so the evidence applies to both. The search returned only titles and short snippets, not full pages, so each finding below is limited to what the snippet showed.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The searches returned no page describing drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for PMK (R)-3. The one salt-tolerance paper that came up (KKL(R) 3, DOI 10.3389/fgene.2023.1332691) is a different variety and was discarded. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10869446/ (discarded, not this variety)

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- A TNAU Agritech page lists "PMK (R) 3" among paddy varieties in a seasonal crop-advisory table (sowing in the July-August period, alongside PMK 2 and MDU 5). This shows it is recommended for a Tamil Nadu season, but gives no yield, maturity or trial data. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/govt_schemes_services/aas/paddy.html

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) -- No evidence found. Parentage (UPLRI 7 x CO 43) was given in the task record but was not confirmed by any search result.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found. The breeder search returned only a DBT-funded KKL(R) 3 paper, which is a different variety. No named breeder for PMK (R)-3 was found.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. The institution in the task record is the Agricultural Research Station, Paramakudi (TNAU). I did not find a verified contact page, email or phone for it in the search results. Address from the task record only: Agricultural Research Station (Tamil Nadu Agricultural University), Paramakudi - 623 707.

PUBLICATIONS -- No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report, thesis or KrishiKosh record for PMK (R)-3 was found in the snippets. -- No evidence found.
- Related project (not a publication): a project titled "Developing herbicide tolerant version of PMK (R) 3 rice adapted to direct seeded cultivation" appears on the Indian Science and Technology portal. Only the title was visible, so I cannot give authors, year or outcomes. -- https://www.indiascienceandtechnology.gov.in/research/developing-herbicide-tolerant-version-pmk-r-3-rice-adapted-direct-seeded-cultivation

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. The TNAU page mentions the variety only in a crop-advisory table, not as seed for sale. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK or SAU seed-sales listing was retrieved. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/govt_schemes_services/aas/paddy.html (mention only)

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Tamil Nadu. The variety is listed in the record as recommended for TAMILNADU, and the TNAU advisory table is consistent with that. The year of release (2003) comes from the task record and was not confirmed by a search result.

Suggested next steps for a full record: check the Seednet portal (seednet.gov.in) for variety code A0102751 directly; check the TNAU Paramakudi ARS pages and the TNAU rice breeding publications; and search KrishiKosh and the AICRP on Rice annual reports for PMK (R)-3 trial data.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: VTL-6 (Rice)

Name note: The evidence refers to "VTL 6" (Vyttila 6 in the release tables). No page was found on the Seednet portal under either name, so the Seednet name is unverified. Four searches were run.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- VTL 6 is described as a semi-tall, non-lodging, high-yielding variety for the coastal saline zones of Kerala, which is its target ecosystem -- https://eurekamag.com/research/004/489/004489736.php
- A KAU brochure describes VTL-6 to VTL-8 as semi-tall, non-lodging, high-yielding varieties from the Vyttila station, which works on saline pokkali tracts -- https://pubhtml5.com/khck/rtrs/basic/51-100
- No drought, flood, submergence, or heat evidence naming VTL-6 was found. The KAU 2017 report's moisture-stress and heat-tolerance remarks refer to unnamed trial entries, so they were not attributed to VTL-6 -- https://kau.in/sites/default/files/documents/research_report_2017.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found. The search returned only pest-resistance pages for other lines (e.g., IR5-IR62 on Zenodo), which were discarded.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- No evidence found for maturity days, yield (t/ha), or multi-location trial results specific to VTL-6. The KAU 2016 brochure and the 2006 VTL 6 paper describe the variety only qualitatively.
- A KAU page reports "10% extra yield over VTL 6" for a different new variety. It was discarded as a comparator, not evidence for VTL-6 -- https://rarsvni.kau.in/basic-page/varieties-released

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage: Cheruviruppu / IR 5 // Jaya, bred by recombination breeding, listed under the name "Vyttila 6" -- https://www.researchsquare.com/article/rs-213648/v1
- The same parentage and breeding method appear in a table of salt-tolerant breeding lines with the notification entry "Kerala" -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/379529917_Recent_Approaches_in_Breeding_for_Salt_Tolerance_in_Rice_in_Bangladesh
- Breeding-line code, QTL, marker, and genome-resource data: No evidence found for VTL-6. Sub1 and Saltol introgression pages describe other lines.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developed by the Rice Research Station, Vyttila, Kerala Agricultural University (KAU). The station was established in 1958 and taken over by KAU in 1974, and its lead mandate is rice in pokkali (saline) areas and rice-fish systems -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/expert_system/paddy/institutes.html
- Named authors of the 2006 VTL 6 paper, all from RRS Vyttila: K.S. Shylaraj, N.K. Sasidharan, and V. Sreekumaran. These are the only named scientists found; their roles as lead breeders are inferred from authorship, not stated -- https://jtropag.kau.in/index.php/ojs2/article/view/128?articlesBySimilarityPage=11
- Note: a Veena Vighneswaran / Sreelatha AK profile page describes VTL-3 (not VTL-6). It was discarded for attribution.

CONTACT DETAILS
- KAU brochure (2016) address block: "Professor & Head, Rice Research Station, Vyttila, Ernakulam District-682019"; phone "0484 22809963"; email is present in the source but is obfuscated in the extracted text and could not be read, so it is not recorded here -- https://pubhtml5.com/khck/rtrs/basic/51-100
- Postal address from the 2006 paper's affiliation line: Rice Research Station, Kerala Agricultural University, Vyttila, Cochin, Kerala 682 019, India -- https://jtropag.kau.in/index.php/ojs2/article/view/128?articlesBySimilarityPage=11
- No individual breeder email or phone was found.

PUBLICATIONS
- Shylaraj, K.S., Sasidharan, N.K., & Sreekumaran, V. (2006). VTL 6: A semi-tall, non-lodging, and high yielding rice (Oryza sativa L.) variety for the coastal saline zones of Kerala. Journal of Tropical Agriculture 44(1/2): 48-51 -- https://eurekamag.com/research/004/489/004489736.php ; https://jtropag.kau.in/index.php/ojs2/article/view/128
- Hossain et al. (2015) and related salt-tolerance QTL work list "Vyttila 6" in a breeding-line table only; it is not a VTL-6 study and was not listed as a publication -- https://www.researchsquare.com/article/rs-213648/v1
- No ICAR/AICRP annual-report, KrishiKosh thesis, or DOI entry specific to VTL-6 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Seednet: No evidence found. No Seednet page was returned for VTL-6 or "VTL 6" under PADDY (DHAN).
- KAU seed price lists (2022-23 and 2025-26) include a category "Pokkali/VTL rice varieties" at 70.00/kg. This is a generic category and does not name VTL-6, so it is not counted as evidence -- https://www.kau.in/sites/default/files/documents/price_list_seeds_and_planting_materials_2025-26_website.pdf
- Private dealer and NSC/KVK listings: No evidence found for VTL-6. Results were generic paddy-seed listings for other varieties.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Kerala (coastal saline tracts). The release table lists the state as Kerala -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/379529917_Recent_Approaches_in_Breeding_for_Salt_Tolerance_in_Rice_in_Bangladesh
- Discrepancy: the record gives release year 2004, but the release table gives 2005 (notification date 11-05-2005 in the same row). The release-minute name and year should be checked against the CSC/gazette record before finalizing.
- The "recommended_states_raw: Unknown" field can be updated to "Kerala" based on this evidence.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Resistant to blast, leaf folder and rice hispa, as listed for a rainfed upland entry -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance in the retrieved pages. A flash-flood screen in the search results concerned MTU 1156 (Tarangini), a different variety, so it was discarded -- No URL (discarded)

DISEASE AND PEST
Blast and leaf folder resistance and rice hispa resistance are listed in the same Agropedia entry -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0
No further disease or pest evidence found for HPR-1156 in the retrieved pages.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Listed as a rainfed upland variety with semi-tall plant habit and long-slender grain, yield 28.5 q/ha, in the Agropedia notified-varieties table -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0

Direct-seeded rice trial at CSK HPKV Palampur (rainy season, same three varieties, referred to as Sukara Dhan 1 for HPR 1156) reporting growth, yield attributes and yield -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/372986218_Growth_yield_and_yield_components_of_rice_Oryza_sativa_as_influenced_by_tillage_methods_and_cultivars

salinity.details: Bred for salinity tolerance by introgressing salt-tolerance genes from the wild parent O. rufipogon through multiple generations of selection and intermating. The variety is described as a salt-tolerant variety for coastal saline areas and was tested under low, moderate and high salinity and alkalinity. Tested for alkalinity under saline-water irrigation in Puducherry. The variety record lists it as tolerant to high level of salinity, phosphorus and zinc deficiency, and iron and aluminum toxicity. Yield under saline conditions is reported as 25-30 q/ha versus 55-60 q/ha under normal conditions (ICAR-IIRR brochure).

Resistance source is the wild parent O. rufipogon.

pest_resistance.summary: Resistant to a mixed population of plant hoppers and leaf folder (variety record). The digest reports resistance to brown planthopper (BPH) and a screening for major insect pests. The wild parent O. rufipogon is described as resistant to multiple pests.

agronomic_details.yield: Average yield 3300.00 to 4500.00 kg/ha (33-45 q/ha) per variety record and Agropedia. Under saline conditions 25-30 q/ha; under normal conditions 55-60 q/ha (ICAR-IIRR brochure). The 55-60 q/ha figure differs from the 33-45 q/ha range and both are reported as found.
agronomic_details.stability: Tested across multiple AICRIP locations in 1999-2001 and 2004. Yield advantages over checks were reported in several states (see field_trials). Stability indices were not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for coastal saline areas. Responsive to added nitrogen doses, lodging resistant, shattering resistant, and suitable for late planting (variety record). Late duration.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 116 To 116Days (variety record). The digest reports seed-to-seed duration of 145 days and days to maturity of 145-150 days (ICAR-IIRR brochure). These sources conflict and the conflict is unresolved.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Semi-dwarf with plant height 105-110 cm (Agropedia). Grain type conflicts across sources: long slender (brochure table), short bold or sort bold (brochure salient features), and SB (Agropedia). Morphological characteristics are recorded as Unknown in the variety record.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Yield under saline conditions 25-30 q/ha versus 55-60 q/ha under normal conditions (ICAR-IIRR brochure). (2) Yield 33-45 q/ha (Agropedia). (3) Yield advantage over checks: 37.3%, 41.5% and 51.3% over CST7-1, CSR 27 and Jaya in West Bengal; 12.8% over SR26B in West Bengal; 10.6% over MTU2607 in Andhra Pradesh; 14% over C14-8 in the Andamans; 22% over TRY3 in Puducherry and Tamil Nadu (ICAR-IIRR brochure). (4) Multi-location AICRIP testing in 1999-2001 and 2004 (Scribd copy). (5) Tested for alkalinity under saline-water irrigation in Puducherry (Scribd copy).

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Jarava (IET-15420), Rice

Name note: The CSC name "Jarava (IET-15420)" and the Seednet name "JARAVA (IET -15420)" refer to the same line. The ICAR-IIRR technology brochure also calls it "Jarava (DRR Dhan 33)." A Bihar notified-varieties list gives "Jarna(IET-15420)," which is probably a misspelling. I kept it only because the IET-15420 code matches. Four searches were run, one per topic.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Bred to tolerate salinity, and the source describes it as a salt-tolerant variety in coastal saline areas (IET-15420 was tested under low, moderate, high salinity and alkalinity) -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0 ; https://icar-iirr.org/Technologies/Innovative%20Technologies.pdf ; https://www.scribd.com/doc/46785847/Jarava-a-new-high-yielding-and-pest-resistant-rice-variety-for-coastal-saline-areas
- Tested for alkalinity under saline-water irrigation in Puducherry -- https://www.scribd.com/doc/46785847/Jarava-a-new-high-yielding-and-pest-resistant-rice-variety-for-coastal-saline-areas
- Drought, heat, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found in the sources retrieved.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to PNPH 24 (IET 21406). The search returned a heat-stress paper on other cultivars (IET 21404, IET 21577), which I discarded. -- https://www.cell.com/heliyon/pdf/S2405-8440(21)01577-2.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. The search returned no resistance data for this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Maturity: a hybrid-variety table lists the duration as 120-130 days, with yield given as 5.8 to 6.9 t/ha. -- https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Hybrid-Rice-Varieties.htm
Water-scarcity suitability: a seed-production manual says PNPH 24 is a mid-early maturing variety suitable for water-scarce situations. The sentence is fragmentary, so treat this as unverified. -- https://www.tnu.in/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/seed-technology.pdf
No multi-location trial data found for this variety.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage (female PRN 1 A / IR 58025 CMS line; male PRN 24 R restorer line): No evidence found. The search did not confirm the parentage given in the record.
Breeding method, QTL, markers and genome resources: No evidence found.
Hybrid type: sources list it as a hybrid, consistent with the record's CMS/restorer parentage, but no source describes its genetics directly. -- https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Notified-Rice-Varieties.htm

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Name discrepancy: no lead breeder or scientist is named in any source found.
Developing company per sources: Nuziveedu Seeds Limited, Medchal Mandal, Ranga Reddy 501401 (A.P.). This conflicts with the record, which names Prabhat Agri Biotech Limited, Hyderabad. The Prabhat attribution is unverified. -- https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Hybrid-Rice-Varieties.htm
Also listed under Nuziveedu: -- https://www.academia.edu/68324607/Super_Hybrid_Rice_in_China_and_India_Current_Status_and_Future_Prospects
No ICAR, SAU or AICRP institute is credited with this variety in the sources found.
Variety name: the CSC/notification name and the Seednet name both match "PNPH 24 (IET 21406)" in the sources. A 2021 notification lists "PNPH24" for Assam (S.O. 500(E), 29.01.2021), with no IET number. I did not attribute it to this variety because the identity is unconfirmed. -- https://krishakjagat.org/national-news/list-of-notified-paddy-varieties-in-india-during-2011-to-2021/

CONTACT DETAILS
Institute-level address only (from the Bihar DRD list, for Nuziveedu Seeds Limited): Medchal Mandal, Ranga Reddy-501401 (A.P.). No email, phone, breeder contact or institute contact-page URL was found. -- https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Hybrid-Rice-Varieties.htm
The prabhat-agri address in the record (6-3-541/B, Panjagutta, Hyderabad-500082) is unverified.

PUBLICATIONS
Review noting PNPH 24 among Indian hybrids (authors and year not shown in the search result): Super Hybrid Rice in China and India: Current Status and Future Prospects. International Journal of Agriculture and Biology -- https://www.academia.edu/68324607/Super_Hybrid_Rice_in_China_and_India_Current_Status_and_Future_Prospects
No peer-reviewed, AICRP/ICAR, thesis (KrishiKosh) or QTL study specific to this variety was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found on Seednet, NSC, state seed corporations, KVKs, SAU sales or dealers for this variety. The searches returned Philippine SeedNet and US/China seed pages, which I discarded.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Bihar, West Bengal and Odisha, per the central notification S.O. 2125(E) dated 10.09.2012, year of release 2012. -- https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Notified-Rice-Varieties.htm
Release year 2012 conflicts with the 2007 year in the record. Notification and listing sources give 2012 consistently. -- https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Notified-Rice-Varieties.htm

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Jaldbi (IET-17153), Rice (Oryza sativa)
Name note: "variety_name" is Jaldbi (IET-17153). The Bihar notified-variety list uses "Jaldbi (IET - 17153)", which matches "seednet_variety_name". Other sources spell it Jaldabi, Jaldubi or Jaldbi. All of these refer to the same IET-17153 entry. Searches: 4 run.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to this variety. The Raipur AICRIP centre page lists "Jaldubi" among varieties named in a drought-breeding context, but it gives no tolerance data for this variety -- http://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/Centers/06%20Raipur.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
Jaldubi (IET 17153, AR 1023) is described as resistant to blast -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0
The Raipur centre page lists Jaldubi in a varietal list beside pest-monitoring text, but it gives no resistance finding for this variety -- http://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/Centers/06%20Raipur.pdf
No evidence found for resistance to gall midge, bacterial leaf blight or brown planthopper specific to this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Agropedia's table of rice varieties notified 1996-2007 lists Jaldubi (IET 17153, AR 1023), released 2007, with duration 130-140 days, direct-seeded rainfed culture, height 140-150 cm, medium-fine grain, and yield 53.0 q/ha -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0
The Raipur centre page describes the variety as high-yielding with short bold grain of good quality. The statement sits in the Jaldubi table row, but the page gives no trial data -- http://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/Centers/06%20Raipur.pdf
Plant variety passport: late heading, straight panicle main-axis curvature, well-exerted panicle, medium-length medium-slender decorticated grain, classed as "typical" -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/pvjjuly0112.pdf
No multi-location trial results or AICRIP yield data found specific to this variety.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage (from the variety record provided): selection from local germplasm AR 1023 collected in Surguja district, Chhattisgarh. Agropedia's entry gives the same identifier pair (IET 17153, AR 1023) -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0
Breeding method: selection from local germplasm, per the provided record. No independent source confirmed the method.
Breeding-line code: IET-17153 (listed in the Bihar notified list, the Raipur centre page and the plant variety passport).
No evidence found for genes, QTLs, markers or genome resources specific to this variety. Raipur centre material on gall-midge resistance genes and bacterial leaf blight markers does not name Jaldbi, so it was excluded.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: Indira Gandhi Krishi Vishwavidyalaya (IGKV), Raipur, through its Department of Plant Breeding and Genetics (per the provided record). The plant variety passport names IGKV, Krishak Nagar, Labhandi, Raipur-492006 as the applicant -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/pvjjuly0112.pdf
Lead breeder or scientist name: No evidence found. The Raipur centre page and the 2024 IGKV genetic-gain paper name IGKV staff, but neither names this variety's breeder -- http://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/Centers/06%20Raipur.pdf
Station: The Raipur Rice Research Station of IGKV is named as a rice-breeding centre, but no link to this variety's breeding programme is stated.
A second passport application for this variety, filed 01/11/2011, names the Indian Council of Agricultural Research as applicant. Its role in the record is not explained -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/pvjjuly0112.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
No breeder contact found (no name, email or phone).
Institute-level address only: Indira Gandhi Krishi Vishwavidyalaya, Krishak Nagar, Labhandi, Raipur-492006 (Chhattisgarh) -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/pvjjuly0112.pdf
No email, phone or institute contact-page URL was found in the search results. Check the IGKV website directly.

PUBLICATIONS
Author not stated (year not stated). Rice Research Station, Raipur, AICRIP centre report, variety table (IET 17153, S.O. 1178(E), 20-7-2007). -- http://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/Centers/06%20Raipur.pdf
Author not stated (2012). Plant Variety Journal of India, Vol. 6, No. 2 (July 2012), variety passport for Jaldbi (IET-17153). -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/pvjjuly0112.pdf
No peer-reviewed paper, thesis, KrishiKosh record or conference paper specific to this variety was found. Items on IGKV rice genetic gain and IGKV mutation breeding do not name Jaldbi and were excluded.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. The search returned only US, Indonesian and other non-Indian seed pages, which were excluded. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, IGKV seed-sales or dealer listing was found. Check the Chhattisgarh seed portals and IGKV seed sales directly.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0
The notification is recorded as "All India" (S.O. 1178(E), 20.07.2007) -- http://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Notified-Rice-Varieties.htm
The two scopes conflict. Use the state-level recommendation for planning and record the "All India" notification scope as the official gazette entry.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Coastal salinity tolerance: a 2011 paper titled around Luna Suvarna CR2096-71-2 assesses rice varieties for tolerance to coastal salinity (the greenhouse abstract excerpt does not name the variety, so this rests on the title) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/262145028_Luna_Suvarna_CR2096-71-2_and_Luna_Sampad_CR2095-181-1_Rice_varieties_for_tolerance_to_coastal_salinity
Ecology listed as "Coastal Saline" for Luna Suvarna (CR Dhan 403) in the NRRI variety table, with a moderately resistant reaction code -- https://icar-nrri.in/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Rice-Varieties-of-NRRI.pdf
Drought, heat, flood and submergence: No evidence found for this variety. The searches returned only Swarna-Sub1 and other varieties.

DISEASE AND PEST
Listed as tolerant to stem borer, brown planthopper and leaf folder, and resistant to blast ("R-BL") in the ICAR-CRRI/NRRI release table -- https://icar-crri.in/released-varieties/ and https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/CRRIs-varieties-1968-2024.pdf
One NRRI table snippet describes tolerance to stem borer, leaf folder, whorl maggot and rice hispa, but the text is not clearly attached to this row, so I have not attributed it -- https://icar-crri.in/released-varieties/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Duration about 150 days, medium slender grain, plant height about 135 cm, yield 3.5-4.0 t/ha, in the ICAR-CRRI release table (2010, Orissa) -- https://icar-crri.in/released-varieties/ and https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/CRRIs-varieties-1968-2024.pdf
Field or multi-location trial data: No evidence found for this variety.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage: Mahsuri / Ourmundakan, with designation CR 2096-71-2 (IET 18697) -- https://icar-nrri.in/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Rice-Varieties-of-NRRI.pdf
Breeding-line code: CR 2096-71-2 (also CR Dhan 403) -- https://icar-nrri.in/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Rice-Varieties-of-NRRI.pdf
Breeding method, QTL/marker studies and genome resources: No evidence found for this variety.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: Central Rice Research Institute, Cuttack (now ICAR-National Rice Research Institute, NRRI). The NRRI table and the ICAR-CRRI list both attribute it to this institute -- https://icar-nrri.in/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Rice-Varieties-of-NRRI.pdf and https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/CRRIs-varieties-1968-2024.pdf
Institute history: CRRI was set up in 1946 at Bidhyadharpur, Cuttack -- https://arch-india.org/institution/central-rice-research-institute
Lead breeder name: No evidence found. The Sah and Anilkumar C. report (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/383342769_High_Yielding_Rice_Varieties_with_Swarna_Traits_Developed_by_ICAR-NRRI) concerns Swarna-derived lines, not this variety, so I have not attributed it. Pranto Sen and Sanjay Singh are the authors of the 2011 salinity paper, not confirmed breeders of this variety.

CONTACT DETAILS
Breeder: No evidence found.
Institute: No email, phone or postal address appeared in any search result. Institute web pages that carry variety lists are https://icar-crri.in/released-varieties/ and https://icar-nrri.in/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Rice-Varieties-of-NRRI.pdf. Neither snippet shows a contact section.
Seednet contact: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
Sen, P.; Singh, S. (2011). Luna Suvarna CR2096-71-2 and Luna Sampad (CR2095-181-1): Rice varieties for tolerance to coastal salinity. Indian Journal of Genetics and Plant Breeding 71(2):378-388 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/262145028_Luna_Suvarna_CR2096-71-2_and_Luna_Sampad_CR2095-181-1_Rice_varieties_for_tolerance_to_coastal_salinity (DOI not found in the search results)
Note: the author list in the search result shows Pranto Sen and Sanjay Singh; the snippet is partly garbled, so verify the author list against the journal.
KrishiKosh theses, AICRP/ICAR annual reports and other peer-reviewed papers: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
Seednet entry (name "LUNASUWARNA (IET 18697)"): No evidence found. The search did not return a Seednet page.
State seed corporation, KVK, SAU or private dealer listings for this variety: No evidence found. The Odisha results were general (for example, the Odisha State Seed Corporation supplied most seed sold by agro-dealers in one study -- https://cega.berkeley.edu/collection/agro-dealers-and-adoption-of-flood-tolerant-rice-in-odisha/), not specific to this variety, so they are excluded.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Odisha. Notified under S.O. 632(E) dated 25.03.2011 for Odisha -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/list-of-notified-rice-varieties-in-india-during-2011-to-2021/ and http://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Notified-Rice-Varieties.htm
Name variants: the notification lists it as "Luna Suvarna (IET 18697)". Other sources use "Luna Swarna" and "Luna Suvarna (CR Dhan 403)". No source uses the Seednet spelling "LUNASUWARNA".

drought.details: Described as drought tolerant in the ICAR-CRRI released-variety listing (CVRC entry: Bunded Upland, 2008, Jharkhand/Maharashtra). The CSC variety record states 'TOLERANT TO DROUGHT.' A 2023/2024 RNA-seq study (Springer) examined drought tolerance at the molecular level and catalogued differentially expressed genes; the specific genes and mechanisms are not given in the digest. No quantitative drought scores were found, so the level is rated medium on qualitative evidence only.

disease_resistance.summary: Brown spot: moderately resistant (CSC variety record; ICAR-CRRI listing records moderate resistance). Blast: moderately resistant (CSC variety record); the NRRI report also lists a moderately resistant blast reaction, but the table is garbled and the blast entry is treated as unverified in the digest. Bacterial leaf blight: moderate resistance (ICAR-CRRI listing only; not mentioned in the CSC record). Other diseases: Not found in searched sources.

pest_resistance.summary: Gall midge biotype 1: resistant (CSC variety record). Gall midge biotype 4: moderately resistant (CSC variety record); ICAR-CRRI listing records gall midge resistance without biotype detail. WBPH (whitebacked planthopper): moderately resistant (CSC variety record); ICAR-CRRI listing records moderate resistance to planthopper pests. Stem borer: moderately resistant (CSC variety record; ICAR-CRRI listing records moderate resistance). Leaf folder: moderately resistant (CSC variety record; ICAR-CRRI listing records moderate resistance). The ICAR-CRRI listing also refers to moderate resistance to whorl-type pests, as stated in the digest. Other pests: Not found in searched sources.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: CR Dhan 40 (IET 19253), Rice

Name note: The CSC release name is "CR Dhan 40 (IET 19253)" and the Seednet name is the same. The sources mostly use "CR Dhan 40", with the line designation CRR 383-22 (IET 19253). Findings below refer to this variety. Pages about DRR Dhan 40 (IET 21665), CR Dhan 407, CR Dhan 401, and AAU-TTB Dhan 40 are excluded.

STRESS TOLERANCE:
- Listings from ICAR-CRRI describe this line as drought tolerant. -- 75 · CR Dhan 40 · Bunded Upland · 2008 · 110 · SB · CVRC, Jharkhand Maharastra · Drought tolerant, MR-BL,BS,WBPH,SB,LF, R-GM,3.0 -3.5 t/ha -- https://icar-crri.in/released-varieties/
- A 2023/2024 RNA-seq study on this line examined drought tolerance at the molecular level, cataloguing differentially expressed genes. -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12892-023-00222-3
- Heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found in the retrieved pages.

DISEASE AND PEST:
- The ICAR-CRRI released-variety listing records moderate resistance to bacterial leaf blight, brown spot, whorl-type and planthopper pests, stem borer, leaf folder, and resistance to gall midge. -- https://icar-crri.in/released-varieties/ (same entry as above)
- The NRRI report lists a blast reaction described as moderately resistant, and a gene count in the R-gene table, but the table text is garbled and one row reads "CR Dhan 40 S" (ambiguous). Treat the blast and R-gene entries as unverified. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/339527323_Rice_Varieties_of_NRRI_Yield_Quality_Special_Traits_and_Tolerance_to_Biotic_and_Abiotic_Stresses
- Other disease reactions: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS:
- Duration: 110 days in the ICAR-CRRI and NRRI released lists. -- https://icar-crri.in/released-varieties/ ; a later ICAR-CRRI PDF lists 100 days for the same entry (conflict). -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/CRRIs-varieties-1968-2024.pdf
- Yield: 3.0–3.5 t/ha in both lists. -- https://icar-crri.in/released-varieties/
- Ecology: Bunded upland. -- https://icar-crri.in/released-varieties/
- Plant height, grain type and trial-site data: No evidence found specific to this variety.
- The ICAR-CRRI achievements page lists CR Dhan 40 among 2008-era varietal pipeline lines, with no trial data. -- https://icar-crri.in/major-achievements/

GENETICS AND QTL:
- Parentage: N 22/RR 20-5. -- https://icar-nrri.in/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Rice-Varieties-of-NRRI.pdf
- Breeding-line designation: CRR 383-22 (IET 19253), listed in the NRRI varieties table. -- https://icar-nrri.in/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Rice-Varieties-of-NRRI.pdf
- Breeding method: No evidence found for this variety.
- Genome resources: RNA-seq reads (about 549 million) were mapped to the indica reference genome in a study of this line. -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12892-023-00222-3
- QTL or marker studies specific to this variety: No evidence found. (The maudamani QTL and CR Dhan 407 pages are different varieties and were excluded.)

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION:
- Developing institution: Central Rice Research Institute, Cuttack, the institute recorded in the CSC minutes. The NRRI document states that NRRI was formerly known as CRRI. -- https://icar-nrri.in/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Rice-Varieties-of-NRRI.pdf
- Lead breeder or scientist name(s): No evidence found for this variety. The CR Dhan 407 author names (P S Roy, S S C Patnaik, G J N Rao) belong to a different variety and are excluded.
- Station: No evidence found. Breeder names were not found.

CONTACT DETAILS:
- No breeder email, phone, or postal address was found. Institute-level pages found: https://icar-crri.in/released-varieties/ and https://icar-nrri.in/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Rice-Varieties-of-NRRI.pdf. Neither page contained contact details in the retrieved text.

PUBLICATIONS:
- Dey N; Galiba G; Kocsy G, et al. (2023/2024). Molecular insight into drought tolerance of CR Dhan 40: an upland rice line from Eastern India. Journal name not shown in retrieved text (Springer, vol. 27, pp. 225–234). -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12892-023-00222-3 ; DOI 10.1007/s12892-023-00222-3. Author list is partial in the retrieved text.
- ICAR-CRRI and NRRI varietal compilations listing this line (no authors; institute reports). -- https://icar-crri.in/released-varieties/ ; https://icar-nrri.in/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Rice-Varieties-of-NRRI.pdf
- KrishiKosh theses, AICRP/ICAR annual reports and field-trial papers: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY:
- No evidence found. Searches returned dealer listings for other varieties (PB-1509, DRR Dhan 48, a hybrid paddy from Krishidhan Seeds). The Seednet portal, NSC, state seed corporations and SAU/KVK sources were not searched directly.

RECOMMENDED STATES:
- Jharkhand and Maharashtra, per the CVRC listing. -- https://icar-crri.in/released-varieties/ ; https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Notified-Rice-Varieties.htm
- Conflict: the notification listing gives the gazette entry "CR Dhan 40 (IET 19253) 2008 S.O. 2458(E) 16.10.2008 All India", which differs from the CVRC state list. -- http://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Notified-Rice-Varieties.htm

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
Name check: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "Nua Kalajeera (IET 18393)". Sources use "Nua Kalajeera", "NuaKalajeera", "Nua kalajeera" and "IET 18393". The Bihar list is a state notification list (S.O. 2458(E), 16/10/2008), not CSC minutes. I found no Seednet portal page for this variety.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Name matched: Nua Kalajeera / IET 18393
- Research bulletin lists it as moderately susceptible to sheath blight, bacterial leaf blight, stem borer, plant hopper and gall midge, moderately resistant to leaf blast and sheath rot, and resistant to rice tungro virus (source spells it "tungru"). -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/NRRI-Research-Bulletin-39.pdf
- Same bulletin lists "field tolerance to submergence" and low fertilizer response to N among traits, but the section is not clearly tied to this variety. Treat as unconfirmed. -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/NRRI-Research-Bulletin-39.pdf
- Popular NRRI varieties page describes Nua Kalajeera as photosensitive and late maturing, with tallness (about 140 cm). The 50 cm submergence and dormancy text on that page belongs to other varieties, not this one. -- https://icar-crri.in/popular-nrri-varieties/
- Product profile says it is tolerant of lodging. -- https://rkb-odisha.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/Nua-Kalajeera.pdf
- Drought, heat, salinity and flood tolerance: No evidence found for this variety. A Central University of Odisha research mention refers to Kalajeera landrace, not confirmed as IET 18393. -- https://shalikuta.org/product/kalajeera/

DISEASE AND PEST
Name matched: Nua Kalajeera (released-varieties entry)
- Released-varieties table entry (2008, Orissa, shallow lowlands, 150 days) lists it as black husk, aromatic, photosensitive, resistant to yellow stem borer, moderately resistant to blast and sheath rot, 2.8 t/ha. -- https://icar-crri.in/released-varieties/
- Rice Varieties of NRRI page: Nua Kalajeera is among entries showing resistance to bakanae. -- https://icar-nrri.in/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Rice-Varieties-of-NRRI.pdf
- Popular NRRI varieties page (Nua Kalajeera entry) gives no separate disease rating beyond the bulletin entries above. -- https://icar-crri.in/popular-nrri-varieties/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Name matched: Nua Kalajeera / IET 18393
- Late maturing (about 145 days), tall (about 140 cm), photosensitive, released 2008 for lowland Odisha; average productivity about 3.0 t/ha. -- https://icar-crri.in/popular-nrri-varieties/
- Product profile: duration 145-150 days, height 135-140 cm, lodging tolerant, HRR 62, producibility about 1100 kg/acre; the table is partly garbled, so treat the numbers as approximate. -- https://rkb-odisha.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/Nua-Kalajeera.pdf
- Profile lists low yield, low grain weight and photosensitivity as limitations, and says it performs well under organic nutrient management. -- https://rkb-odisha.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/Nua-Kalajeera.pdf
- Bulletin lists a seed rate of 40 (unit not clear in snippet). -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/NRRI-Research-Bulletin-39.pdf
- 2014 paper reports it gained popularity and yield superiority in national multi-location trials and performed well under the All India trials. The snippet does not give yield values. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/275948119_Nua_Kalajeera_Nua_Dhusara_and_Nua_Chinikamini
- ICAR-CRRI 2010-11 annual report: Nua Kalajeera appears in an OYT station-trial table (nucleus seed 0.06, breeder seed 2.6, units unclear). A separate yield-advantage statement in the same report refers to a different line, not clearly this variety. -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2018/06/2010-11.pdf
- Grain quality (bulletin): head rice recovery about 61-63%, volume expansion ratio about 5.3, amylose about 22.6%, alkali spreading value 5.0. -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/NRRI-Research-Bulletin-39.pdf
- Grain quality (2014 paper): HRR 62.2% and 66.5% reported in different entries; APEDA identified it as a good aromatic export candidate. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/275948119_Nua_Kalajeera_Nua_Dhusara_and_Nua_Chinikamini
- Cooking study: volume expansion ratio about 5.25 and elongation ratio about 2.0, compared with other elite Eastern India varieties. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/314783932_Studies_on_Grain_Yield_Physico-Chemical_and_Cooking_Characters_of_Elite_Rice_Varieties_Oryza_sativa_L_in_Eastern_India

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Name matched: Nua Kalajeera / IET 18393
- Parentage: pureline selection from the Kalajeera landrace (no cross parents). -- https://icar-nrri.in/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Rice-Varieties-of-NRRI.pdf
- Breeding-line code: IET 18393 (Kalajeera, pureline selection). -- https://icar-nrri.in/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Rice-Varieties-of-NRRI.pdf
- Breeding method: purification of the landrace by pureline selection; the 2014 paper describes it as a pureline breeding effort with popular aromatic landraces. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/275948119_Nua_Kalajeera_Nua_Dhusara_and_Nua_Chinikamini
- Table in an intechopen chapter lists the same parentage. -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/78726
- Genome resources: 24 SSR markers used on aromatic short-grain landraces to study diversity; the snippet does not confirm that IET 18393 itself was genotyped. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/275948119_Nua_Kalaj
