search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Dehangi (AAUDR 9313-14-3) IET 18243 IC-574471, Rice (Oryza sativa)

Name check: The CSC name and the Seednet name are identical in the input, so every finding below refers to the same name. Several sources use the shorter form "Dehangi (AAUDR 9313-14-3)" or "Dehangi (AAUDR 9313-14-3)(IET 18243 IC 574471", and I treated those as the same variety.

Institution discrepancy: The supplied institution is GAU Main Rice Research Station, Nawagam. Every source I found attributes this variety to Assam Agricultural University (AAU), Jorhat, through its Assam Rice Research Institute and Regional Agricultural Research Station (RARS), Diphu. I found no evidence linking it to Gujarat, so I have not carried the Nawagam attribution into the findings.

Parentage discrepancy: The supplied parentage (SATHI 34-36 x DADRI KOLAM) does not appear in any source. The one pedigree-style string I found reads "Maibee/CRM 49/Maibee" and is not confirmed as parentage. The supplied parentage is unverified.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Suited to direct-seeded and upland (ahu) conditions and to jhum land in the hills. -- https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/127 ; https://thehillstimes.in/featured/rars-develops-organic-rice-varieties-for-rural-assam
- Hill-zone release for direct-seeded ahu season; the source frames it as recommended for growing under direct-seeding stress. -- https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/127 (Dehangi, Rongkhang and Inglonkiri were been notified in Indian Gazette and recommended for growing in hill regions of Assam under direct seeding stress condition.)
- Flood, submergence, drought, heat and salinity tolerance: No evidence found for this variety. The AAU sources mention submergence tolerance only for other varieties (Ranjit Sub-1, Bahadur Sub-1).

DISEASE AND PEST
- Blast resistance is high, with moderate resistance to stem borer and leaf folder. -- https://thehillstimes.in/featured/rars-develops-organic-rice-varieties-for-rural-assam (The variety is non lodging, semi dwarf, deep green leaves, well exerted panicle with desire degree of seed dormancy to escape pre and post harvest sprouting, high degree of resistance against blast and moderately resistance to stem borer and leaf folder.)
- Listed as moderately resistant to major insect pests of Assam in a table of pest reactions. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/391810922_Meloidogyne_graminicola-_A_threat_to_Rice_Cultivation (The rice variety are moderately resistant to major insect pests of Assam.)
- Root-knot nematode (Meloidogyne graminicola) and brown planthopper or gall midge reactions: No evidence found specific to this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Rainfed upland, maturity about 120 days, average yield 2,800 kg/ha (Assam). -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-09/DARE-Annual-Report-2017-18.pdf (table row listing "Dehangi (AAUDR 9313-14-3) IET 18243", Assam, rainfed upland, maturity 120 days, yield 2,800 kg/ha)
- Non-lodging, semi-dwarf, with high milling (73%) and head rice recovery (69%). -- https://thehillstimes.in/featured/rars-develops-organic-rice-varieties-for-rural-assam
- Farmer perception (Assam thesis-based table, N=6): tall with strong culm, good early vigour, well-exerted long panicles, but high spikelet sterility noted. -- https://arrworyza.com/AdminPanel/download/Farmers%E2%80%99%20perception%20of%20suitable%20upland%20%E2%80%98Ahu%E2%80%99%20rice%20varieties%20in%20Assam.pdf
- Flowering and photoperiod data for this variety: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Breeding-line codes: AAUDR 9313-14-3 and IET 18243 / IC-574471 (IC number is the NBPGR accession code as printed in the registry). -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/compendiumforextantnotified-nov-2021.pdf
- Pedigree string in the AAU table: "Maibee/CRM 4 9//Maibee", which differs from the supplied parentage. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/393846178_Hundred_years_of_rice_research_in_Assam
- Breeding method, QTL, markers, and genome resources for this variety: No evidence found. The sources give general molecular-breeding context for AAU only.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developed by a team led by Dr Ashutosh Roy, then Chief Scientist at RARS, AAU, Diphu (now Principal Scientist (Plant Breeding), Sugarcane Research Station, AAU). -- https://thehillstimes.in/featured/rars-develops-organic-rice-varieties-for-rural-assam (These varieties were developed by a team of scientist leaded by Dr Ashutosh Roy, Ex Chief Scientist of Regional Agricultural Research Station, AAU, Diphu and now at present he is working as Principal Scientist (Plant Breeding), Sugarcane Research Station, Assam Agricultural University.)
- Release notified through the Indian Gazette, S.O. 2805(E), dated 25.08.2017, state of Assam. -- https://www.krishakjagat.org/national-news/list-of-notified-paddy-varieties-in-india-during-2011-to-2021/
- Developing institution: AAU, Regional Agricultural Research Station, Diphu. -- https://thehillstimes.in/featured/rars-develops-organic-rice-varieties-for-rural-assam
- Breeding history of the station: Dehangi appears in the AAU rice-breeding history table with 2009 as the year. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/393846178_Hundred_years_of_rice_research_in_Assam
- Institution-level evidence is also supplied by the AAU Directorate of Research page. -- https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/127

CONTACT DETAILS
- Breeder email, phone, and postal address for RARS Diphu or the breeder: No evidence found.
- Institute-level page for AAU Directorate of Research (Agriculture): https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/127 (no email or phone visible in the captured text).
- AAU-Assam Rice Research Institute, Titabar institute page: https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/120 (no email or phone visible in the captured text).
- Contact-details summary: no official email, phone, or postal address for the breeding station was captured.

PUBLICATIONS
- Dehangi appears in a chapter on rice research in Assam (AAU-ARRI). Authors and year not recovered. "Hundred years of rice research in Assam." ResearchGate PDF -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/393846178_Hundred_years_of_rice_research_in_Assam
- Dehangi appears in a table on rice varieties with pest reactions (AAU-ARRI). Authors and year not recovered. "Meloidogyne graminicola - A threat to Rice Cultivation." ResearchGate PDF -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/391810922_Meloidogyne_graminicola-_A_threat_to_Rice_Cultivation
- Farmers' perception of suitable upland 'Ahu' rice varieties in Assam. Thesis, AAU, Jorhat. Author and year not recovered. -- https://arrworyza.com/AdminPanel/download/Farmers%E2%80%99%20perception%20of%20suitable%20upland%20%E2%80%98Ahu%E2%80%99%20rice%20varieties%20in%20Assam.pdf
- No peer-reviewed journal paper, AICRP report entry, KrishiKosh thesis, or DOI specific to this variety: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Breeder seed is produced at AAU-ARRI Titabar, with foundation and certified seed produced for Assam. -- https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/120 (The station has been producing entire amount of seed (Breeder Seed) of various rice varieties as indented by various organization. The station has also been producing foundation and certified seed for the farmers of Assam.)
- Quality seed is also distributed through two farmer producer companies (Golaghat and Jorhat). -- https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/120
- AAU Jorhat has supplied breeder and foundation seed to the Assam State Seed Corporation. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/330901788_FARMERS_PRODUCER_COMPANY-FOR_QUALITY_RICE_SEED_PRODUCTION_IN_ASSAM
- Dehangi-specific seed stock, dealers, KVK, or NSC listings: No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Assam (hill zone, direct-seeded and jhum conditions). -- https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/127 ; https://krishakjagat.org (S.O. 2805(E), state: Assam)
- AAU's directorate page also says a Variety Identification Committee identified the variety for Zone-III (West Bengal, Bihar, Odisha, Uttar Pradesh) besides Assam. The text sits in a list of releases, so I cannot confirm it applies to Dehangi rather than a neighbouring entry. -- https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/127
- Gujarat: No evidence found. The supplied institution is in Gujarat, but no source links this variety to Gujarat.

Registration: PPV&FR registration number 319 (also cited as REG/2018/319). -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/compendiumforextantnotified-nov-2021.pdf ; https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/127

EVIDENCE DIGEST: Manaswini (IET 19005), Rice

Search note: Four web_search queries were run, which is the maximum allowed. Seednet was not searched directly, so the Seednet name is confirmed only as given in the record. Both names were searched as "Manaswini (IET 19005)". The Bihar and drdpat lists spell it "Manaswini" and "Mansiwani" respectively. No results matched the variety's Seednet entry, so the Seednet name is unverified.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The searches returned no page describing drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for this variety. The IRRI Technical Bulletin 16 mentions Manaswini only as a crop grown in rabi and direct-seeded situations in Odisha, with no tolerance data -- http://books.irri.org/TechnicalBulletin16_content.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. No page reported disease or pest reaction for this variety -- searched via the variety, seed and research queries above.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
No evidence found for yield, maturity or multi-location trial results. The IRRI Technical Bulletin 16 names Manaswini among varieties grown in Odisha, which is general context only -- http://books.irri.org/TechnicalBulletin16_content.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
No evidence found for parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method or QTL work. The parentage SWARNA/LALAT appears only in the user-supplied record and was not confirmed by any search result. Breeding-line code IET 19005 appears in the notification lists, but these lists do not state parentage -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf ; http://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Notified-Rice-Varieties.htm

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
No evidence found naming a lead breeder or scientist for this variety. The IRRI Technical Bulletin 16 describes the Rice Research Station, Bhubaneswar, as responsible for many rice varieties and the OUAT rice breeding programme, and it lists Manaswini with a 2008 release entry. It does not name a breeder for this variety -- http://books.irri.org/TechnicalBulletin16_content.pdf
The institution given in the record (Rice Research Station, OUAT, Bhubaneswar) is consistent with this bulletin but was not confirmed for this variety by any page found.

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found. No official email, phone, postal address or institute contact page for this variety was returned. The only institute reference is the record itself: Rice Research Station, Orissa University of Agriculture and Technology, Bhubaneswar.

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report, KrishiKosh thesis or conference paper naming this variety was returned. The "Manaswini" author hits (Manaswini Rao, Manaswini Ravipati, Eaturi Manaswini) are different people and are excluded.

SEED AVAILABILITY
Odisha seed distribution document: a district-level table lists MANASWINI as a seed item, with the surrounding text describing seed deficits and new varieties including Manaswini; the table is garbled and dated around the 2014 supply period -- https://pc.odisha.gov.in/sites/default/files/2020-03/7.Seed_Distribution_System.pdf
No current NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or private dealer listing was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES

This is a notification scope, not a recommended-state list. The record's "Unknown" is not resolved by these sources, and no state-level recommendation was found.

Gaps to resolve in a follow-up pass: Seednet entry (PADDY (DHAN), code A0102941), OUAT/Rice Research Station release documents, CSC minutes, and KrishiKosh or journal searches on IET 19005 or Manaswini.

drought.details: Not found in searched sources. The digest reports no evidence for drought tolerance in the returned pages.

heat.details: Not found in searched sources. The digest reports no evidence for heat tolerance in the returned pages.

salinity.details: Described as salt tolerant. The CSSRI Salinity News describes it as slender-grained and salt tolerant at 4.0-6.0 dS/m. The CSC variety record gives salt tolerance at 6.0 to 8.0 dS/m. These two ranges conflict and both are reported here. Farmers' adoption was linked to salt tolerance, which 95% of adopters cited (CSSRI Annual Report 2014-15). The variety is recommended for coastal saline areas with shallow to semi-deep water (CSC record).

flood.details: A news feature states that Amal Mana can tolerate many days of flooding in Canning field station trials. This is a single secondary news source with no trial data, so the level is rated medium with low confidence. The digest does not report flood-tolerance measurements.

disease_resistance.summary: CSC variety record: moderately resistant against leaf blast, brown spot and sheath blight (the record spells it 'leaf blat'). The digest's disease search returned no variety-specific evidence, so this claim is not corroborated by any sourced document in the digest. No evidence sources are attached.

pest_resistance.summary: CSC variety record: resistant against stem borer, leaf folder, whorl maggot, case worm and blue beetle (the record spells it 'blur beetle'). The digest's pest search returned no variety-specific evidence, so this claim is not corroborated by any sourced document in the digest. No evidence sources are attached.

agronomic_details.yield: CSC record: 4000.00 to 4100.00 kg/ha. CSSRI Salinity News: kharif average grain yield about 4-5 t/ha, with the source text garbled in places. Participatory evaluation (wet seasons 2008-2013): grain yield 4.11 +/- 0.12, units not stated in the snippet.
agronomic_details.stability: Participatory evaluation over wet seasons 2008-2013 is the only multi-season evidence in the digest. Plant height 150-162 cm and duration 160-170 days were recorded. No stability statistic across environments is given. The CSC record describes it as moderately resistant to lodging and grain shattering and responsive to nitrogen up to 80 kg/ha.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for transplanted kharif cultivation in coastal areas of West Bengal, Orissa (Odisha) and Andhra Pradesh, and for coastal saline areas with shallow to semi-deep water (CSC record). The digest found no independent confirmation of Andhra Pradesh, Odisha or West Bengal as recommended states. Its only notification-related finding was an 'All India' entry, which is not reproduced here. The recommended-states field above follows the CSC record, which is treated as ground truth, and the discrepancy is flagged here.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: - Apiculus colour: Pinkish; - 1000 grain weight (gm): 19.0; - Kernel length (mm) 7.03; - Kernel breadth (mm): 2.18; - L/B ratio: 3.22; - Kernel appearance: White; Milling recovery : 70.4%; Head rice recovery : 61.7; alkali value : 5.0; amyose content (%) : 24.6
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) CSSRI Salinity News (Vol. 20 No. 2): kharif average grain yield about 4-5 t/ha under improved crop-management options for coastal rainfed lowlands; source text partly garbled. (2) Participatory evaluation, wet seasons 2008-2013: plant height 150-162 cm, duration 160-170 days (conflicts with the 140-day maturity in the CSC record), grain yield 4.11 +/- 0.12 (units not stated). (3) On-farm adoption survey (CSSRI Annual Report 2014-15): about 23% of farmers who bought seed from CSSRI RRS Canning grew Amal-Mana, on 21% of their rice area; the following year about 43% grew it, with 34% incremental yield and 22% incremental net return. The incremental figures come from the adoption survey as summarised in the digest and are not independently verified. (4) Nitrogen-management trial at Canning Town, 2014-2015, testing neem-coated urea and application methods for nitrogen uptake and use efficiency; no results are given in the digest.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Amal-Mana (IET-14199/18250), Rice

Name check: the CSC release name and the Seednet name are the same string here ("Amal-Mana (IET-14199/18250)"), so every finding below refers to both. I did not run a separate Seednet-portal search; the Seednet record was not retrieved. The four searches returned no Seednet page.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Amal-Mana is described as slender-grained and salt tolerant, at 4.0-6.0 dS m-1 -- https://cssri.res.in/poxumyse/2018/04/salinity_news_vol_20_no_2_english_for_web.pdf
Farmers' adoption was linked to its salt tolerance, which 95% of adopters cited -- https://cssri.res.in/wp-content/uploads/2018/04/cssri_ar_2014-15.pdf
Flood tolerance: a news feature says Amal Mana can tolerate many days of flooding in the Canning field station trials -- https://pulitzercenter.org/stories/salt-tolerant-rice-innovations-help-farmers-deal-salinity-sundarbans
Drought, heat, submergence: No evidence found for these specific stresses in the returned pages.

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. The search for Amal-Mana disease or pest reaction returned nothing specific to this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Kharif-season average grain yield is given as about 4-5 t/ha, with improved crop-management options for coastal rainfed lowlands; the source text is garbled in places -- https://cssri.res.in/poxumyse/2018/04/salinity_news_vol_20_no_2_english_for_web.pdf
Participatory evaluation, wet seasons 2008-2013: plant height 150-162 cm, duration 160-170 days, grain yield 4.11 ± 0.12 (units not stated in the snippet) -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5890383
On-farm adoption: about 23% of farmers who bought seed from CSSRI RRS Canning grew Amal-Mana, on 21% of their rice area; the following year about 43% grew it, with 34% incremental yield and 22% incremental net return -- https://cssri.res.in/wp-content/uploads/2018/04/cssri_ar_2014-15.pdf and https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/impact-improved-salt-tolerant-rice-varieties-farmers-mandal-ars-
Nitrogen-management trial at Canning Town, 2014-2015, testing neem-coated urea and application methods for nitrogen uptake and use efficiency -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Abdelbagi-Ismail

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage Pankaj x SR26 B, as given in the input record; a QTL review lists the same cross for the entry -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5890383 is not the source; the source is https://www.researchgate.net/publication/353376858_Salt_tolerance_in_rice_seedling_and_reproductive_stage_QTL_mapping_come_of_age
Breeding-line code CSRC(S) 7-1-4 and breeding method "pedigree selection" are listed for Amal Mana (IET 18250), year 2006, with GOI notification 454(E) dated 11/2/2009 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/353376858_Salt_tolerance_in_rice_seedling_and_reproductive_stage_QTL_mapping_come_of_age
Genome resources and marker or QTL mapping specific to this variety: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: ICAR-Central Soil Salinity Research Institute (CSSRI), Regional Research Station, Canning Town, West Bengal. A CSSRI paper lists Amal Mana among salt-tolerant varieties from the Canning Town station -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/379529917_Recent_Approaches_in_Breeding_for_Salt_Tolerance_in_Rice_in_Bangladesh
Lead breeder name: No evidence found. The search returned no named breeder for this variety.
Related CSSRI authors who wrote about Amal-Mana management (not confirmed as breeders): T. Damodaran, D.K. Sharma, V.K. Mishra -- https://cssri.res.in/poxumyse/2018/04/salinity_news_vol_20_no_2_english_for_web.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
Institute contact page for the station: https://cssri.res.in/canning-town-rrs/ (location 22°15'N, 88°40'E; about 46 km south-east of Kolkata; established 1959). The station page gives no email or phone in the returned text.
Email: No evidence found. Phone: No evidence found.
Postal address: Not returned by search. The address in the input record ("Canning PO: Canning Town, South 24 Parganas, West Bengal-743 329") was not verified by any search result.

PUBLICATIONS
Damodaran T., Sharma D.K., Mishra V.K. (year not shown). Improved Crop Management Options for New Rice Variety "Amal-Mana" in Coastal Rainfed Lowlands. CSSRI Salinity News, Vol. 20 No. 2 -- https://cssri.res.in/poxumyse/2018/04/salinity_news_vol_20_no_2_english_for_web.pdf
Burman D. (year not shown). Participatory evaluation guides the development and selection of farmers' preferred rice varieties for salt- and flood-affected coastal deltas of South and Southeast Asia. Journal not shown -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5890383
ICAR-CSSRI (2015). Annual Report 2014-15. ICAR-CSSRI, Karnal -- https://cssri.res.in/wp-content/uploads/2018/04/cssri_ar_2014-15.pdf
Ismail A.M. et al. (2014-2015 trial, year of publication not shown). Neem-coated urea and nitrogen use efficiency of 'Amal-Mana' rice, Canning Town. Journal not shown -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Abdelbagi-Ismail
Mandal S. (year not shown). Impact of improved salt tolerant rice varieties on farmers' economy under coastal salt affected areas of Sunderbans. Non-peer-reviewed article -- https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/impact-improved-salt-tolerant-rice-varieties-farmers-mandal-ars-
Peer-reviewed papers and theses specific to this variety found on KrishiKosh: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
Seed sold by CSSRI RRS Canning to farmers, per the adoption survey -- https://cssri.res.in/wp-content/uploads/2018/04/cssri_ar_2014-15.pdf
NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or private dealer listings: No evidence found. The fourth search returned only unrelated US rice-seed pages.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Notification S.O. 454(E) dated 11.02.2009 is listed under "All India" -- http://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Notified-Rice-Varieties.htm
Discrepancy: the input lists Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and West Bengal as recommended states. None of the search results confirms those three states. Only the notification's "All India" entry was found.
Notification reference: GOI S.O. 454(E), 11.02.2009 -- http://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Notified-Rice-Varieties.htm

Sources excluded as irrelevant: Bangladesh Aman rice papers, Tulshimala, Pusa Basmati 1121, RiceTec deposit records, Amaura rice seed listings, and a horsegram notification that only cites Amal-Mana in its reference list.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: Narendra Mayank (NDR-9830144)(IET-18055), Rice

Name note: the CSC/notification name and the Seednet name are identical in the input, so all evidence below refers to the same name. I ran 4 searches. I did not open seednet.gov.in directly, so no Seednet portal entry was checked.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Described as tolerant to submergence and suitable for flood-prone areas of U.P., with maturity of about 110 days, Narendra Mayank 2008 43-45 Maturity 110 days, tolerant to submergence, suitable for flood prone areas of U.P. -- https://www.nduat.org/Doc/skteditedResearchAchievementsfoNet-2014.pdf (the "43-45" figure is unlabelled in the source; its meaning is unclear)
- Listed among STRASA submergence-tolerant varieties, which the brochure says survive 2 weeks of complete inundation. The brochure's variety table lists NDR 9830144 (Narendra Mayank) -- http://books.irri.org/STRASA-STRV-brochure.pdf (the brochure states this as a general claim for the group, not a Mayank-specific trial result)
- Gates submergence guideline table row: NDR 9830144 (Narendra Mayank), India 2009, with numeric columns (145, 110) whose labels are not given in the snippet -- https://dqo52087pnd5x.cloudfront.net/posters/docs/gatesopenres-182324.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found. The searches returned no blast, bacterial blight, BPH, or other resistance data for this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- The NDUAT research highlights list it among varieties very popular among the farmers under various rice ecosystems, but give no yield or trial data for it -- https://www.nduat.org/Doc/skteditedResearchAchievementsfoNet-2014.pdf
- Multi-location or AICRP trial results for this variety: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Breeding-line code given in the STRASA brochure: IR68828-24-NDR-1-1-1-1 for NDR 9830144 -- http://books.irri.org/STRASA-STRV-brochure.pdf. This conflicts with the supplied parentage (IR 60185-B-25-2-2 / IR 57519-PMI-5-3-2-2 // IR 55008-10-3-3-3-3). The supplied parentage could not be confirmed, and the discrepancy needs checking against the release record.
- The Gates table gives the same line code (IR 68828-24-NDR-1-1-1) -- https://dqo52087pnd5x.cloudfront.net/posters/docs/gatesopenres-182324.pdf
- Breeding method and genome/QTL resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: Narendra Deva University of Agriculture & Technology (NDUAT). The NDUAT list of varieties includes Narendra Mayank -- https://nduat.org/Doc/Crop-Varieties-Developed-by-NDUAT.pdf
- Lead breeder or scientist names: No evidence found.
- Station or division details beyond the university name: No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder contact found. The only institute-level link found is the NDUAT website domain, nduat.org (taken from the document URLs above). No official email, phone, or postal address was found in the results.

PUBLICATIONS
- NDUAT (2014). Research Highlights, Research Network (report; authors not stated in the snippet). Mentions Narendra Mayank with 2008 release year, 110-day maturity, and submergence tolerance -- https://www.nduat.org/Doc/skteditedResearchAchievementsfoNet-2014.pdf
- No peer-reviewed papers, theses, KrishiKosh items, or conference papers specific to this variety were found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found for NDR 9830144 / Narendra Mayank. The search returned seed listings for other varieties (NDR-2064, NDR-2065 at https://iffdc.in/post_detail.php?postname=availability-of-seed; Kalanamak and Pusa varieties at other sites). These were discarded as not this variety. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU, or dealer listing was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- The notification list gives Narandra Mayank (NDR 9830144) 2009 S.O. 454(E) 11.02.2009 All India. -- http://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Notified-Rice-Varieties.htm. The input field "Unknown" should be updated to All India.

- An NDUAT research-network highlights document gives a 2008 entry, "Narendra Jalpusp," with maturity of about 113 days, long bold grain, and suitability for irrigated late-sown and rainfed lowland areas of UP. search_metadata.evidence_digest:
PLAIN-TEXT EVIDENCE DIGEST: Narendra Dhan (NDR-9830132), Rice

Name check: The CSC-style release name "Narendra Dhan (NDR-9830132)" appears in the Bihar licence document as "Narendra Dhan (NDR-9830132)". The drdpat.bih.nic.in list spells it "Narandra Dhan (NDR 9830132)". The Seednet name "Narendra Dhan (NDR-9830132)" was not returned by any search, so no Seednet page was found. The evidence below refers to the variety name as spelled on those pages.

Searches run: 4 (variety/notification; breeder/institute; research papers; seed availability).

STRESS TOLERANCE
- The STRASA brochure table lists NDR 9830132 (India, 2009) in a block headed "Submergence-tolerant varieties", which also describes survival of about 2 weeks of complete inundation. The table layout is garbled, so the row-to-variety mapping is uncertain and needs checking against the original PDF -- http://books.irri.org/STRASA-STRV-brochure.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found. Searches returned no disease or pest resistance data specific to this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- No evidence found. No yield, maturity, or multi-location trial data for this variety was returned.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- No evidence found for parentage, QTL, or markers. The parentage in the record (CT 9993-5-10-1-M/PSBRC 60/IR 55714-PMI-5-1-2) was not confirmed by any search result. The STRASA brochure layout places "IR68815-1-Long" in the same garbled block as NDR 9830132, but this does not establish that it is this variety's parent, so I have not attributed it.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The notification record lists the variety under 2009 with notification S.O. 454(E), dated 11.02.2009 -- http://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Notified-Rice-Varieties.htm
- The institutional list of varieties developed by NDUAT was retrieved, but the snippet did not include this variety, so NDUAT attribution is not confirmed by search evidence -- https://nduat.org/Doc/Crop-Varieties-Developed-by-NDUAT.pdf
- No evidence found for the lead breeder's name or the developing station. The breeder search returned only unrelated varieties (e.g., DRR Dhan 44, Narendra Dhan 118, Narendra Dhan 359).

CONTACT DETAILS
- No evidence found. No breeder contact, institute email, phone, or address page for this variety was returned. Institute contact details for NDUAT (Kumarganj, Faizabad) were not retrieved from any result.

PUBLICATIONS
- No evidence found. No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report, KrishiKosh thesis, or conference paper naming this variety was returned. The search results on Narendra Dhan 359 and Narendra Dhan 118 are different varieties and are excluded.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found. The seed results were retail listings for generic "Dhan/Dhaan" paddy for puja use, which are not this variety. They are excluded.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- The notification list records the variety as "All India" -- http://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Notified-Rice-Varieties.htm
- This conflicts with the recommended state in the record (UTTAR PRADESH). The "All India" scope in the notification should be checked against the CSC minutes or the official gazette notification before the state field is finalised.

heat.details: The CSC input record states K-9107 is tolerant to heat, but it gives no graded level and no mechanism. The searched sources returned no independent heat-tolerance evidence for K-9107.

disease_resistance.summary: Spot blotch (Bipolaris sorokiniana): In a seedling and vegetative study from Kanpur, K 9107 was the most resistant of seven wheat varieties tested, with the lowest disease index of 33.2%. The authors linked this to higher soluble protein and total phenol levels in K 9107 leaves. Rust, brown rust, foliar blight and Karnal bunt: the CSC input record states K 9107 is highly tolerant to brown rust infection, foliar blight and Karnal bunt, with a last recorded Karnal bunt infection of 1.4%, and that it carries diverse genes for resistance to all three rusts with excellent horizontal resistance. The searched sources did not corroborate the rust, blight or Karnal bunt claims, and the CSC record carries no source URL. Smut: no evidence found.

pest_resistance.summary: No evidence found for aphid or other pest resistance in K-9107. The CSC input record lists pest reaction as Unknown.

agronomic_details.yield: Six-variety study (C.S. Azad University of Agriculture & Technology, Kanpur): maximum grain yield of 54 q/ha for K 9107, against 27 q/ha for K 8027. A popular-varieties table lists K 9107 with a value of 55.0, but the column header and unit are not visible, so its meaning cannot be confirmed. The CSC input record gives no numeric average yield (field reads "UNDER NORMAL CONDITIONS. Kg/Ha" with no value).
agronomic_details.stability: The CSC input record states the variety is widely adapted under different sowing dates, irrigation levels and fertilizer doses. No multi-location stability data were found in the searched sources.
agronomic_details.adaptation: The CSC input record recommends release and cultivation across the North Eastern Plains Zone, including the eastern part of Uttar Pradesh, for timely sown, high fertility, irrigated conditions. The popular-varieties table lists the variety under "different zones and production conditions" without naming a zone or state.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Semi-dwarf with synchronous tillering (six-variety study, Kanpur). Grain-quality work classes K-9107 as hard wheat with grain size among the largest in that set.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Six-variety study, C.S. Azad University of Agriculture & Technology, Kanpur: maximum grain yield 54 q/ha for K 9107 versus 27 q/ha for K 8027. (2) Popular-varieties table: value 55.0 for K 9107, meaning unconfirmed. (3) Grain-quality study (Biochemistry journal, 2024): hard wheat, grain size among the largest in the set. (4) Chapati quality trials over two years: K-9107 ranked at or near the top for palatability, texture and pliability. (5) Spot blotch screening (Bioscan): see disease_resistance. No crop duration or multi-location trial results were found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: K-9107 (wheat)

Name check: The CSC release name and the Seednet name are both "K-9107", so every finding below refers to that name. Sources also write it as "K 9107" and "K-9107". No search returned a Seednet portal page for variety code A0104014, so the Seednet record itself is unverified.

Searches run: 4 (variety, breeder/institute, research, seed availability). Pages about Kansas State wheat, corn hybrids, seed-stock sellers, and US patent wheat cultivars were discarded as unrelated.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- K 9107 was the most resistant of seven wheat varieties tested against spot blotch (Bipolaris sorokiniana), with the lowest disease index of 33.2%, in a seedling and vegetative study from Kanpur -- https://thebioscan.com/index.php/pub/article/view/1843
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance of K-9107 specifically.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Spot blotch resistance is reported in the Bioscan study above. Its authors linked the resistance to higher soluble protein and total phenol levels in K 9107 leaves -- https://thebioscan.com/index.php/pub/article/view/1843
- No evidence found for rust, smut, Karnal bunt, aphid or other pest resistance.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- A six-variety study from C.S. Azad University of Agriculture & Technology, Kanpur reported a maximum grain yield of 54 q/ha for K 9107, against 27 q/ha for K 8027. The same study describes K 9107 as semi-dwarf with synchronous tillering -- https://www.indianjournals.com/article/ijbsm-2-3-015
- A popular-varieties table lists K 9107 with a value of 55.0 beside it, with no column header or unit visible in the extract, so the meaning of that figure cannot be confirmed -- https://static.vikaspedia.in/media/files_en/agriculture/crop-production/wheat-varieties.pdf
- Grain-quality work classes K-9107 as hard wheat, with grain size among the largest in that set -- https://www.biochemjournal.com/archives/2024/vol8issue9S/PartL/S-8-9-150-517.pdf
- Chapati quality trials in two years ranked K-9107 at or near the top for palatability, texture and pliability -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/366441741_Studies_on_physico-chemical_characters_and_chapatti_quality_of_different_wheat_varieties
- No evidence found for crop duration, days to maturity or multi-location trial results for K-9107.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage (K 8101/K 68 (CNOSIB/SR 64/KLRE/3/8156)/(PJSIB/GB 55//)NP 773/K 13) comes from the input record only. No search result confirmed it -- no source found.
- No evidence found for breeding-line codes, breeding method, QTL, markers or genome resources for K-9107.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The variety is listed among wheat varieties developed by institutes across India, with the K 9107 synonym "DEWA" given on that page. No breeder name is given -- https://uasbagriinnovationcenter.in/other-institute-22/
- Two papers from the Department of Plant Pathology, C.S. Azad University of Agriculture & Technology, Kanpur (208002) study K 9107. This is an institutional affiliation of the authors, not a breeder attribution -- https://www.indianjournals.com/article/ijbsm-2-3-015
- No evidence found for a lead breeder or scientist name for K-9107.

official_quote.quote: K 9107 (DEWA) IS HIGHLY TOLERANT TO BROWN RUST INFECTION FOLIAR BLIGHT AND KARNAL BUNT

disease_resistance.research_summary: Spot blotch (Bipolaris sorokiniana): In a seedling and vegetative study from Kanpur, K 9107 was the most resistant of seven wheat varieties tested, with the lowest disease index of 33.2%. The authors linked this to higher soluble protein and total phenol levels in K 9107 leaves. Rust, brown rust, foliar blight and Karnal bunt: the CSC input record states K 9107 is highly tolerant to brown rust infection, foliar blight and Karnal bunt, with a last recorded Karnal bunt infection of 1.4%, and that it carries diverse genes for resistance to all three rusts with excellent horizontal resistance. The searched sources did not corroborate the rust, blight or Karnal bunt claims, and the CSC record carries no source URL. Smut: no evidence found.

STRESS TOLERANCE --
- Listed in the Northern zone table for LS-RF (late-sown, rainfed, low-fertility) conditions with a value of 23.5 beside it; the unit and trait basis are not stated on the page. -- https://static.vikaspedia.in/media/files_en/agriculture/crop-production/wheat-varieties.pdf
- Named among varieties to promote under late-sown irrigated (LSI) conditions in a wheat package-of-practices deck. This is a secondary slide deck, not an official ICAR document. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/wheat-package-of-practices-in-general-69301516/69301516

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. The searches returned no disease or pest resistance data for K-8962 or K 8962.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Trial or yield data: only the single LS-RF table value noted above (23.5, unit not stated). The same deck lists sowing windows for late sowing (10–16 Dec) and seed rates (125 kg/ha for late and rainfed conditions). These are general recommendations, not variety-specific data. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/wheat-package-of-practices-in-general-69301516/69301516
- Maturity, plant height and yield potential: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) --
- Parentage K 7401/HD 2160 (from the CSC record): not confirmed by any search result. The AICRP notified-varieties table has a parentage row for another group of varieties that does not show K 8962's entry. -- https://www.aicrpwheatbarleyicar.in/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/wheat-varieties-notified-in-india.pdf
- The same AICRP table lists "K 8962 (INDRA)" in a block of varieties whose developer column reads CSAUA&T, Kanpur. Its layout is ambiguous; the "INDRA" name is not explained elsewhere. -- https://www.aicrpwheatbarleyicar.in/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/wheat-varieties-notified-in-india.pdf
- Genetic stocks, breeding line codes, breeding method and genome resources for K 8962: No evidence found.
- DWR genetic stock resources (84 registered wheat stocks) are general and do not name K 8962 as a genetic stock. -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/DWR-Perspective-Plan-Vision-2025.pdf

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION --
- The AICRP notified-varieties table attributes K 8962 (INDRA) to CSAUA&T, Kanpur (the developer column for that block). No individual breeder name was found. -- https://www.aicrpwheatbarleyicar.in/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/wheat-varieties-notified-in-india.pdf
- The DWR perspective plan names K 8962 only in a promotion statement; it does not state breeder or developer. -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/DWR-Perspective-Plan-Vision-2025.pdf
- Lead breeder or scientist name(s): No evidence found.
- Institute station: Chandra Shekhar Azad University of Agriculture and Technology (CSAUA&T), Kanpur, per the CSC institution field. Not independently confirmed beyond the AICRP table entry.

CONTACT DETAILS --
- No breeder contact, email, phone or postal address was found. I did not run a dedicated institute contact search, so this heading is unresolved rather than confirmed empty. The CSAUA&T institute contact page was not retrieved.

PUBLICATIONS --
- No peer-reviewed papers, AICRP annual reports, theses or KrishiKosh records naming K-8962 or K 8962 were found. The research search returned only unrelated Kansas State and gene-study results.

SEED AVAILABILITY --
- Seednet portal listing or variety code A0104015 record: No evidence found. The Seednet portal was not retrieved.
- A seed-dealer directory for Kanpur returned general listings only. No K 8962 entry was shown. -- https://dir.indiamart.com/kanpur/wheat-seeds.html
- NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK and SAU seed-sales listings: No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES --
- Northern zone (LS-RF table entry, value 23.5). The state(s) are not named on the page; the table is zone-level. -- https://static.vikaspedia.in/media/files_en/agriculture/crop-production/wheat-varieties.pdf
- Late-sown irrigated (LSI) promotion in the package-of-practices deck, without state names. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/wheat-package-of-practices-in-general-69301516/69301516
- The CSC field "recommended_states_raw: Unknown" is not resolved by the evidence above. Release year 1996 was not confirmed by any search result.

SEARCH LOG: 4 web_search queries were run ("K-8962 Wheat variety", "K-8962 Wheat breeder institute", "K-8962 Wheat research", "K-8962 wheat Kanpur seed"). The Seednet name "K-8962" and the CSC name "K-8962" are the same string, so no separate Seednet-name search was needed. Several results named K-State (Kansas) wheat programmes and were discarded as unrelated.

drought.details: The digest found no independent evidence for drought tolerance of GW-322. The CSC record states that GW 322 gave its highest yield under late sowing and with one, two and three irrigations, which the record interprets as tolerance to terminal heat and drought. This is a record statement and is not corroborated by any retrieved source. Source for the drought claim: CSC record (no URL).

heat.details: The digest found no evidence for heat tolerance of GW-322 itself. The only heat-related result (Wheat & Barley Newsletter) concerns DBW 150, a different line derived from a DBW 16/GW 322 cross, and was deliberately not attributed to GW-322. The CSC record's terminal-heat interpretation (highest yield under late sowing) is uncorroborated.

flood.details: Not found in searched sources.

disease_resistance.summary: The CSC record states that GW 322 possesses a high degree of resistance to leaf rust and stem rust, described as important diseases of the Central and Peninsular zones. No independent source in the digest confirms this. None of the retrieved pages reported rust, smut, blight or other disease reaction for GW-322.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. The CSC record states there is no major insect pest problem in wheat in the Central and Peninsular zones and that pest testing was not done under coordinated trials. No insect reaction for GW-322 was reported in the digest.

agronomic_details.yield: No quantitative trial yield for GW-322 found in the digest. In a nutrient-uptake study, GW 451 gave the highest grain yield and GW 322 was about 17% lower. A commercial seller claims 60-62 q/ha; this is a seller claim, not trial data. CSC record: highest yield under all nitrogen doses (90, 120 and 150 kg N/ha).
agronomic_details.stability: CSC record: lodging not reported by any centre in any year; highest yield under all nitrogen doses; highly adapted to both timely and late sowing. No multi-environment stability statistics found in the digest.
agronomic_details.adaptation: CSC record: recommended for cultivation in Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, southern and western Rajasthan, the Bundelkhand area of Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra and Karnataka under timely sown, high fertility irrigated conditions. No official notification or zone recommendation was found in the digest. Seller pages are Madhya Pradesh- and Maharashtra-oriented, which is not evidence of official recommendation.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: MEDIUM LONG PARALLEL EARHEAD WIRH DENSE ARRANGEMENT OF SPIKELETS. COLOUR OF AWN AND SPIKELETS. COLOUR OF AWN AND SPIKELETS IS DIRTY WHITE AT MATURITY. WAXINESS PRESENT ON FLAG LEAF AND SHEATH. GLUME SHOULDER IS SQUARE. (CSC record). Additional CSC record traits: resistant to shattering with medium threshability; medium-sized, lustrous grains with high hectolitre weight and protein. A general agronomy page describes GW-322 as semi-dwarf and high-yielding, but it cites no sources and is treated as low reliability.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Sowing-date trial under open and Pongamia pinnata agroforestry systems: GW-322 was one of two wheat varieties tested as sub-sub plots and was compared with MP-3336 on several traits; the varieties ranked differently across traits. No numeric results in the digest. (2) Nutrient-uptake study under six integrated nutrient management practices: compared with GW 273, GW 451 and GW 496; GW 451 gave the highest grain yield and GW 322 was about 17% lower. (3) Climate-change impact study (middle Gujarat, A2 scenario): reports yield and phenology figures for GW-322; no values were available in the digest. (4) Diallel/combining-ability study: GW 322 is one of eight parents (see genetics). No other trial results found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: GW-322 (Wheat)

Name note: Searches used "GW-322" and "GW 322" (CSC minutes name "GW-322"; Seednet name "GW-322"). The same evidence applies to both. No Seednet portal page was returned. I used all four permitted searches, so I did not run a separate Seednet-specific query.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance of GW-322 itself. The only heat-related result (a wheat & barley newsletter) concerns DBW 150, a different line derived from a DBW 16/GW 322 cross, so I have not attributed it to GW-322. -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/Wheat-Barley-Newsletter-V.111-2017.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. None of the retrieved pages reported rust, smut, blight or insect reaction for GW-322.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- GW-322 was one of two wheat varieties tested as sub-sub plots in a sowing-date trial under open and Pongamia pinnata agroforestry systems, where it was compared with MP-3336 on several traits, with the varieties ranking differently across traits. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/373131250_Performance_of_Wheat_Varieties_at_Different_Sowing_Dates_under_Open_and_Pongamia_pinnata_Based_Agroforestry_Systems
- A nutrient-uptake study compared GW-322 with GW 273, GW 451 and GW 496 under six integrated nutrient management practices; GW 451 gave the highest grain yield and GW 322 was lower by about 17%. -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/indian-journal-of-agricultural-research/A-6050
- A climate-change impact study reports yield and phenology figures for GW-322 under the A2 scenario, middle Gujarat. -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Performance-of-yield-and-phenology-of-wheat-cv-GW-322-under-A2-scenario_fig2_263937507
- A commercial seller describes GW-322 as a rabi variety sown 10–25 November with a 115–120 day duration and a claimed yield of 60–62 q/ha. These are seller claims, not trial data. -- https://www.skbseeds.com/product/gw-322
- A general agronomy page describes GW-322 as semi-dwarf and high-yielding. It does not cite sources, so treat it as low reliability. -- https://agri.bot/docs/information-about-variety-of-wheat-gw-322/

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage: the CSC record gives PBW 173/GW 196. I found no independent source confirming this parentage, so it is unverified.
- Use as a parent: a newsletter records DBW 150 as derived from the cross DBW 16/GW 322 and registered as a genetic stock with heat tolerance. This shows GW-322 used as a parent, not that GW-322 is heat tolerant. -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/Wheat-Barley-Newsletter-V.111-2017.pdf
- A diallel/combining-ability study lists GW 322 among eight parents, with significant general combining ability for effective tillers per metre and a significant negative specific combining ability with K 1006. -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Details-of-eight-wheat-varieties-used-in-the-study_tbl1_373169277
- No QTL, marker, breeding-line code (beyond the CSC variety code A0104063 in the record) or genome-resource evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
No evidence found naming a lead breeder or scientist for GW-322. The institution in the CSC record is the Research Scientist (Wheat), Wheat Research Station, Gujarat Agricultural University, Vijapur-382870, Distt Mehsana; this comes from the record you supplied, not from a search result. A national compendium lists SDAU-Vijapur among centres for central-zone wheat, but it does not link that centre to GW-322, so I have not attributed it. -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/RB-51-Compendium-of-Wheat-Varieties-Notified-in-India-During-2018-2023.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
No breeder contact found. No email, phone or institute contact page for the Wheat Research Station, Vijapur was returned. The only address is the one in the CSC record: Research Scientist (Wheat), Wheat Research Station, Gujarat Agricultural University, Vijapur-382870, Distt Mehsana.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not shown in retrieved text (year not shown). Performance of Wheat Varieties at Different Sowing Dates under Open and Pongamia pinnata Based Agroforestry Systems. ResearchGate (PDF) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/373131250_Performance_of_Wheat_Varieties_at_Different_Sowing_Dates_under_Open_and_Pongamia_pinnata_Based_Agroforestry_Systems
- Authors not shown in retrieved text (year not shown). Effect of Wheat Varieties and Integrated Nutrient Management Practices on Nutrient Content, Uptake and Soil Nutrient Status. Indian Journal of Agricultural Research (ARCC) -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/indian-journal-of-agricultural-research/A-6050
- Authors not shown in retrieved text (year not shown). Impact assessment of climate change on wheat yield in middle Gujarat region (figure on GW-322 under A2 scenario). ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Performance-of-yield-and-phenology-of-wheat-cv-GW-322-under-A2-scenario_fig2_263937507
- Authors not shown in retrieved text (year not shown). Details of eight wheat varieties used in the study (diallel analysis including GW 322). ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Details-of-eight-wheat-varieties-used-in-the-study_tbl1_373169277
- Authors not shown in retrieved text (2017). Wheat & Barley Newsletter, Vol. 111 (DBW 150 derived from DBW 16/GW 322). Directorate of Wheat Research, ICAR -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/Wheat-Barley-Newsletter-V.111-2017.pdf
- No peer-reviewed DOI, KrishiKosh thesis or AICRP report specifically on GW-322 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Commercial listings (not official seed-production records): Narmada Agri Genetics, Ratlam, offering GW-322 seed -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/gw-322-wheat-seeds-20238493291.html
- Agrico Seeds Company, Jabalpur, offers "Wheat (GW-322) C-1 Seed" -- https://www.indiamart.com/vibha-agrico-cropscience/wheat-seeds.html
- SKB Seeds lists GW-322 for sale (product page is aimed at Maharashtra buyers) -- https://www.skbseeds.com/product/gw-322
- IFFDC availability list includes GW-322 among certified seed varieties -- https://iffdc.in/post_detail.php?postname=availability-of-seed
- No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK or SAU seed-sale record was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Unknown in the CSC record, and no official notification or zone recommendation for GW-322 was found. Seller pages are Madhya Pradesh- and Maharashtra-oriented, which is not evidence of official recommendation.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: PBW-34 (Wheat)

Name check: variety_name "PBW-34" and seednet_variety_name "PBW-34" are the same string, so every finding below refers to "PBW-34" as written. Searches were run for PBW-34 wheat variety, PBW-34 breeder/PAU, PBW-34 research, and PBW-34 seed availability (4 searches). Results were checked against the strict relevance rule. Most hits were about PBW 343 (a different variety), so they were discarded.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Only one page names PBW-34 wheat with a stress-related result, and it is about shade from poplar agroforestry, not drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence. Under six-year-old poplar plantations, PBW-34 showed the largest grain yield reduction of the three varieties tested (57.1%, versus 19.4% for PBW-222 and 15.3% for HD-2329) -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF00707473
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found. The search returned rust-resistance pages for PBW 343 (a different variety), which were discarded.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- PBW-34 wheat was studied for grain yield potential under poplar plantations in Punjab, India. Yield reduction was measured relative to the open-field yield; the paper's trial design and year are not visible in the retrieved text -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF00707473
- Multi-location or field-trial results for PBW-34 outside this poplar study: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage and pedigree-selection method (Anhinga "S" x Flamingo "S"): No evidence found. These details came from the submitted record, not from any retrieved page.
- Marker, QTL or genome-resource studies for PBW-34: No evidence found.
- Note: a 2018-2023 compendium of notified wheat varieties lists "PBW34" as a parent of the durum line DDW 47 -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/RB-51-Compendium-of-Wheat-Varieties-Notified-in-India-During-2018-2023.pdf. This is a pedigree reference, not evidence about PBW-34's own genetics.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- No breeder name for PBW-34 was found on any page. The release and development attributions in the submitted record (PAU Ludhiana, Wheat Breeder, Department of Plant Breeding) could not be confirmed from retrieved text.
- The PAU Department of Plant Breeding faculty pages found by the search do not mention PBW-34. They are not attributed to this variety.

CONTACT DETAILS
- No variety-specific breeder contact: No evidence found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pragati (DWR-39), wheat

Search note: The first web_search call was malformed (empty input) and failed. Three valid searches followed, so four calls were used in total. The searches were: (1) variety and release, (2) developer, (3) research papers, (4) seed availability. The search tool then reported no calls remaining. Searches (1) and (2) returned mostly DWR 162, DBW 39 and UAS-304 material, which is not this variety, so the topics below are thin.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. The searches returned no stress-tolerance data naming Pragati or DWR 39 for wheat. The only DBW 39 pages found refer to a different variety, so they were discarded.

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found. A DBW 39 leaf-blight resistance mention (https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/EB-52-Wheat-Cultivation-in-India-Pocket-Guide.pdf) names a different variety and was discarded.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found. AICRP wheat and barley progress reports from Dharwad (https://www.aicrpwheatbarleyicar.in/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/Social-Sciences-2018-19-1-2.pdf and https://www.researchgate.net/publication/363258027_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_AICRP_on_Wheat_and_Barley_Progress_Report_2020-21_Social_Sciences) report Dharwad trials, but the excerpts do not name Pragati or DWR 39.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources): No evidence found for the parentage given in the record ("derivative of HD 1508 x S.308"). No QTL, marker or breeding-line-code evidence naming this variety was returned. The DWR-Vision-2030 and Perspective Plan pages (https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/DWR-Vision-2030.pdf and https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/DWR-Perspective-Plan-Vision-2025.pdf) are general DWR Karnal documents with no DWR 39 mention.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: No evidence found that names a breeder for this variety. UAS Dharwad pages about the wheat programme (https://www.deccanchronicle.com/southern-states/karnataka/karnataka-india-to-supply-uas-dharwad-developed-wheat-seed-to-indonesia-for-food-security-1969624) describe a 1985 programme under Dr R.R. Hanchinal and a 1993 release, but they concern DWR 162 and do not mention DWR 39 or Pragati. I have not attributed that breeder to this variety. The record's 1985 release year also conflicts with the 1993 DWR 162 release date, which the record should be checked against.

CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found. No breeder contact was found. The UAS Dharwad seed farms page (https://uasd.edu/en/seed-farms/) lists wheat breeder-seed production at Almel, Konnur and Madhurakhandi, but it has no contact details and does not name this variety. The DWR Karnal site is a different institute from the record's institution, so I have not used its contacts.

PUBLICATIONS:
Authors not shown in the retrieved text (the file name suggests "Malik", 2014, but this is unverified). Title truncated in the source: "Genetic diversity of agro-morphological characters in ..." -- https://www.cropj.com/malik_8_9_2014_1266_1271.pdf (this paper lists "DWR 39 (PRAGATI)" among peninsular-zone wheat genotypes; journal and full title not confirmed)
No other paper names this variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found. The seed-related results were unrelated companies (Pragati Agri Products, Kolkata, https://www.indiamart.com/pragati-agri-pvtltd/; Pragati Seeds, https://pragatiseeds.com/) and an unrelated Haryana seed-shortage report. None of them names this variety. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES: The record lists "Unknown". The only related finding is a genetic-diversity paper that groups DWR 39 (Pragati) under the Peninsular Zone (https://www.cropj.com/malik_8_9_2014_1266_1271.pdf). That is a germplasm grouping, not a state recommendation or notification. No CSC notification or state recommendation was found.

Variety name check: The evidence refers to "DWR 39 (PRAGATI)" in the genetic-diversity paper, which matches the Seednet name "PRAGATI (DWR-39)". No CSC release-minute name was retrieved.

drought.details: No drought evidence was found in the searched sources. The CSC variety record states the variety is good drought resistant and is recommended for rainfed, limited-input cultivation, but this is not corroborated by any searched source. Kundan's inclusion in a fertility-gradient stability trial is not a drought test.

heat.details: A heat-shock-protein thermotolerance study describes DL 153-2 as relatively heat-tolerant when compared with HD 2285 (tolerant reference) against HD 2329 and WH 542 in a late-sown trial. The rating is comparative only. A separate NDUAT Narendra Nagar elevated-temperature study included Kundan, but no tolerance rating for Kundan was extracted.

salinity.details: No salinity evidence was found in the searched sources.

flood.details: No flood evidence was found in the searched sources.

disease_resistance.summary: Stem rust (Puccinia graminis): Kundan is described as Ug99-resistant and was screened against Indian stem rust pathotypes 40A (62G29) and 122 (7G11). Stem rust resistance was studied in F2 populations (Kundan x UP 2338; UP 2338 x Agra Local), which segregated 3:1 resistant:susceptible. Kundan's specific Sr gene status (Sr22, Sr24, Sr26, Sr31, Sr39 marker screen) was not resolved in the extracted text. Leaf rust, yellow rust, Karnal bunt and powdery mildew: the CSC variety record reports resistance to all four, but none of these was corroborated by the searched sources. The digest found no yellow rust evidence and reports this as a conflict to be checked against the official record. Leaf blight: no evidence found.

pest_resistance.summary: The CSC variety record states that no insect attack has ever been observed on DL 153-2 and that the variety is free from storage pests, possibly because of the very hard seed texture typical of deshi wheats. The searched sources found no insect evidence. This claim rests on the CSC record only and has no supporting URL.

agronomic_details.yield: CSC average yield: Unknown. A dealer listing (unverified against the official notification) gives 50-55 q/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: Kundan is listed among the highest-yielding wheats across fertility levels, with a unit regression coefficient b = 1 in stability analysis, indicating responsiveness to high-yielding environments. No multi-location AICRP stability data were found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: CSC record: recommended for rainfed and limited-input cultivation. No searched source confirmed this adaptation.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Unknown in CSC record. Dealer listing (unverified): height 90-100 cm, harvest about 120-125 days, bold hard grain. CSC record: highly resistant to lodging and non-shattering. The lodging and non-shattering traits are not corroborated by a searched source.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Fertility-gradient stability trial: Kundan was among the highest-yielding genotypes, with b = 1. (2) Late-sown heat-shock-protein thermotolerance trial: DL 153-2 was relatively heat-tolerant against HD 2329 and WH 542 (with HD 2285). (3) NDUAT Narendra Nagar elevated-temperature study: Kundan was included, but no result was extracted. No multi-location AICRP trial result specific to Kundan was found.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Glu-D1d HMW-glutenin allele screen: Kundan pattern 2* 17+18 5+10, PCR positive. Stem rust gene screen used Sr22, Sr24, Sr26, Sr31 and Sr39 markers; Sr31 was detected in UP 2338, Sr39 was absent in all entries tested, and Kundan's status was not resolved. Glutenin-based clustering placed Kundan-DL-153-2 in cluster I with UP-2338, HD-2329 and others. Positions not stated.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: No QTL mapping study for Kundan was found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Kundan (DL-153-2), Wheat

Name note: CSC release name is "Kundan (DL-153-2)" and the Seednet name is "KUNDAN (DL-153-2)". I did not reach seednet.gov.in directly. All findings below refer to the Kundan / DL 153-2 wheat unless marked otherwise. Four searches were run (variety/release, breeder/institute, research, seed availability).

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Kundan is listed among the highest-yielding wheats across fertility levels, with unit regression coefficient b = 1 (stability analysis) indicating responsiveness to high-yielding environments -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/1967/1267
- DL 153-2 is described as relatively heat-tolerant (with HD 2285) against HD 2329 and WH 542 in a late-sown trial, in a heat-shock-protein thermotolerance study -- https://www.academia.edu/10693724/Heat_Shock_Protein_in_Developing_Grains_in_Relation_to_Thermotolerance_for_Grain_Growth_in_Wheat
- A separate elevated-temperature study at NDUAT Narendra Nagar included Kundan among wheat genotypes tested; no tolerance rating for Kundan was extracted -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/355209367_PBW-154_K-7903_HUW-234_UP-262_RAJ-3077_HD-2733_and_Kundan_experiment_was_conducted_at_Instructional_farm
- No drought, salinity, flood or submergence evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Kundan is described as Ug99-resistant (stem rust) and was screened against Indian stem rust pathotypes 40A (62G29) and 122 (7G11) -- https://www.indianjournals.com/article/ejpb-5-4-004
- Stem rust resistance gene screening (Sr22, Sr24, Sr26, Sr31, Sr39 markers) included Kundan and UP 2338; Sr31 was detected in UP 2338, Sr39 was absent in all entries tested. Kundan's specific Sr gene status was not resolved in the extracted text -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/215455710_Development_of_SCAR_markers_for_identification_of_stem_rust_resistance_gene_Sr31_in_the_homozygous_or_heterozygous_condition_in_bread_wheat
- No yellow rust, leaf blight, or insect evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Dealer listing (unverified against this variety's official notification): height 90-100 cm, harvest about 120-125 days, yield 50-55 q/ha, bold hard grain -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/kundan-wheat-seed-2903614091.html
- Kundan was one of the wheat genotypes in a fertility-gradient stability trial (see Stress Tolerance) -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/1967/1267
- No multi-location AICRP trial result specific to Kundan was found.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Release-record parentage (from input, not corroborated by any search result): straight cross of Mexican high-yielding, rust-resistant, red-grained Tonari 71 and NP 890, pedigree method -- source: supplied variety record only, no URL found.
- Glu-D1d HMW-glutenin allele screen: Kundan pattern 2* 17+18 5+10, PCR positive -- https://graingenes.org/ggpages/awn/47/Textfiles/INDIA.html
- Partial genetic male sterility inheritance: Kundan used as fully fertile male parent; trait governed by a single recessive gene (suggested) -- https://graingenes.org/ggpages/awn/47/Textfiles/INDIA.html
- Stem rust inheritance: F2 of Kundan x UP 2338 and UP 2338 x Agra Local segregated 3:1 resistant:susceptible -- https://www.indianjournals.com/article/ejpb-5-4-004
- Glutenin-based clustering placed Kundan-DL-153-2 in cluster I with UP-2338, HD-2329, and others -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/agricultural-science-digest/D-5085
- No QTL mapping study or Kundan-specific breeding-line code found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Institution evidence: Division of Genetics, Indian Agricultural Research Institute, New Delhi, co-authored the Kundan stem rust and stability papers; Directorate of Wheat Research, Karnal, is also linked to the stem rust work -- https://www.indianjournals.com/article/ejpb-5-4-004
- Institutional listing of DL 153-2 (KUNDAN) among wheat varieties developed by different institutes, ICAR-IIWBR Karnal portal -- https://uasbagriinnovationcenter.in/other-institute-22/
- Breeder name: No evidence found. No lead breeder name was extracted from any result.
- The 2015 Bihar notification list confirms the release entry only, with no breeder name -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute-level only, from the stem rust paper affiliation: Division of Genetics, Indian Agricultural Research Institute, New Delhi-110 012 -- https://www.indianjournals.com/article/ejpb-5-4-004
- Directorate of Wheat Research, Karnal-132001, Haryana (affiliation listed in the same paper) -- https://www.indianjournals.com/article/ejpb-5-4-004
- Institute website listed for ICAR-IIWBR: aicrpwheatbarleyicar.in (as listed on a partner page) -- https://uasbagriinnovationcenter.in/other-institute-22/
- No email or phone number for this variety or a breeder was found. Please check the IARI and IIWBR official contact pages directly.

PUBLICATIONS
- Nagaraja, N.R., Singh, A., Pallavi, J.K., Sharma, J.B., Venkatesh, K., Singh, G.P., Jain, N., et al. (year not stated in result). Genetics of resistance to stem rust against Indian races in wheat varieties, Kundan and UP 2338. Electronic Journal of Plant Breeding (vol. 5, issue 4) -- https://www.indianjournals.com/article/ejpb-5-4-004
- Authors not extracted (year not stated). Stability analysis of wheat genotypes across fertility levels, IARI Division of Genetics. Indian Journal of Genetics and Plant Breeding -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/1967/1267
- Sumesh, K.V. (year not stated). Heat shock protein in developing grains in relation to thermotolerance for grain growth in wheat. Journal/report not confirmed -- https://www.academia.edu/10693724/Heat_Shock_Protein_in_Developing_Grains_in_Relation_to_Thermotolerance_for_Grain_Growth_in_Wheat
- Authors not extracted (year not stated). SCAR markers for Sr31 in bread wheat, including Kundan and UP 2338 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/215455710_Development_of_SCAR_markers_for_identification_of_stem_rust_resistance_gene_Sr31_in_the_homozygous_or_heterozygous_condition_in_bread_wheat
- Authors not extracted (year not stated). Glutenin clustering of wheat genotypes including Kundan-DL-153-2. Agricultural Science Digest -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/agricultural-science-digest/D-5085
- Directorate of Wheat Research (1999). 2nd Training Course on Wheat Seed Production and Processing Techniques, listing Kundan (DL-153-2) in seed-production material -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/2nd-Training-Course-on-Wheat-Seed-Production-and-Processing-Techniques.pdf
- No DOI or KrishiKosh thesis found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Private dealer listings (not official seed agency): Sood Hybrid Seeds, Bazpur, Udham Singh Nagar, Uttarakhand, lists "(kundan) Wheat Seed" -- https://www.indiamart.com/sood-hybrid-seeds/certified-wheat-seeds.html

- No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, or SAU seed-sale evidence found. Seednet portal not directly searched.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- No evidence found. The variety's recommended states are listed as "Unknown" in the supplied record, and no search result stated them.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
Search limit reached after three queries, so the fourth (seed availability) and the breeder and contact follow-up could not be run. Results below come only from the three searches that completed.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: HW-741 (Wheat)

Name check: the variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "HW-741". All evidence below refers to this name. Seednet variety code A0104180 and the Seednet crop entry "WHEAT (GEHON)" did not appear in any search result.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- Titled as a rust-resistant wheat variety for southern hills (Kochumadhavan, Tomar and Nambisan, 1988, Indian Farming 38(5)). The snippet does not say which rust species, and no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence evidence was found. -- https://eurekamag.com/research/001/734/001734057.php

DISEASE AND PEST -- Same source as above: rust resistance is the only disease or pest finding. Pest resistance: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. The only agronomic reference is an agro-morphological diversity study that lists HW 741 among southern hill zone varieties and mentions it in plant-height and leaf-trait discussions. The page did not give yield or maturity values I could confirm. -- https://www.cropj.com/malik_8_9_2014_1266_1271.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL (parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) -- Parentage given in the release record is "Bb-Cc/Cno s - No. 66-Pi 62". No search result confirmed this pedigree, and no breeding method, QTL or marker study was found. Searches for genetics returned no HW-741 evidence beyond the agro-morphological study.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- The release record names I. A. R. I. Regional Station, Wellington, The Nilgiris. The search did not name a lead breeder or scientist. The 1988 Indian Farming article is by M. Kochumadhavan, S.M.S. Tomar and P.N.N. Nambisan, but the sources do not state their roles in developing HW-741, so I have not assigned them as breeders. -- https://eurekamag.com/research/001/734/001734057.php

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. The release record gives the station address only (I.A.R.I. Regional Station, Wellington, The Nilgiris, PIN 643231); no email, phone or contact page was found in search results.

PUBLICATIONS --
Kochumadhavan, M.; Tomar, S.M.S.; Nambisan, P.N.N. (1988). 'HW-741' - a rust-resistant wheat variety for southern hills. Indian Farming 38(5) -- https://eurekamag.com/research/001/734/001734057.php
Malik et al. (2014). Genetic diversity of agro-morphological characters in [title truncated in search result]. Directorate of Wheat Research, Karnal -- https://www.cropj.com/malik_8_9_2014_1266_1271.pdf (first author and full title should be verified on the PDF; the search snippet did not show them in full.)

SEED AVAILABILITY -- Not searched. The fourth query was blocked by the tool limit. Check Seednet, the Nilgiris KVK, the Tamil Nadu and Kerala SAU seed sales, and NSC directly.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- The release record says "Unknown". The agro-morphological study lists HW 741 under the Southern Hill Zone, and the 1988 title refers to southern hills. This suggests a southern hill-zone recommendation, but no official notification text was found to confirm the states. -- https://www.cropj.com/malik_8_9_2014_1266_1271.pdf; https://eurekamag.com/research/001/734/001734057.php

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
HP-1493 (wheat) -- variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "HP-1493", so every finding below refers to that name.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. Search 1 returned no page describing drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence response for HP-1493. Results were about unrelated varieties and other countries.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No page on HP-1493 rust, Karnal bunt or other disease or pest reaction turned up.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. No maturity, yield or multi-location trial data for HP-1493 turned up. Search 3 returned unrelated trial and nursery data.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) -- Parentage "E 8841 X NP 830" comes only from the variety record supplied with the request (not found by search). No page confirmed it. No breeding-line code, breeding method, QTL or marker study was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Dr. M.P. Jha, Senior Wheat Breeder, IARI Regional Station, Pusa, Bihar is named only in the supplied record. No search result confirmed it. Search 2 returned breeding pages for unrelated US, Hungarian, Russian and other varieties, which I have discarded.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder, institute, email, phone or address page for HP-1493 was returned.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. Search 3 returned no paper, AICRP report, KrishiKosh thesis or conference paper naming HP-1493. No authors, year, title or DOI can be recorded.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. Search 4 returned only unrelated US seed-supply articles and a video-game guide, which I have discarded. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Partial evidence only. A Bihar state notified-varieties list (Bihar Department of Agriculture, PDF, undated) includes the entry "112 · HP-1493 · 15/05/1990 · 386(E)" -- that is, serial 112, release date 15 May 1990, notification number 386(E) -- with the same format used for other wheat entries in that list -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/Licence/Document/Variety.pdf. The list does not state the crop or the recommended zone, so the crop is inferred from the list's wheat neighbours (for example, HPW 155 Onkar). The "BIHARBIHARBIHAR" field in the record matches this Bihar listing, but the page does not say HP-1493 is recommended for Bihar.

Search limit: four web_search calls were used. Official Seednet, ICAR, IARI and KrishiKosh pages were not returned for this variety, so the breeder, contact, publication, stress and seed fields remain unverified.

drought.details: No evidence found for KRL 1-4 specifically. Drought tolerance was not reported in the digest.

heat.details: No evidence found for KRL 1-4 specifically. Heat tolerance was not reported in the digest.

salinity.details: Bred for salt tolerance to ECe 6.0 dS/m in saline soils and to pH 9.2 in alkaline soils (CSSRI states it was bred for both conditions). Tolerates salinity up to ECe 7.0 dS/m and was the first wheat variety released for saline and sodic soils of the NWPZ. Sodicity tolerance is listed as up to pH 9.3 with salinity tolerance of 7.0 dS/m. Germination is unaffected up to pH 9.4 if sown under proper moisture conditions (original variety record; not an independent digest finding). A pot study reported that proline and reducing sugars rose with salinity most strongly in KRL 1-4, which the study classes as the tolerant cultivar (compared with UP 2338). A field trial at the ICAR-IARI Water Technology Centre (New Delhi) under saline irrigation of 1.7 to 12 dS/m reported water-productivity gains with foliar potassium for KRL-1-4.

flood.details: No evidence found for KRL 1-4. Waterlogging claims in the digest refer to KRL 3-4 and were excluded.

disease_resistance.summary: Described as having disease resistance to all prevalent rusts (rust types not individually named). Karnal bunt: No evidence found for KRL 1-4. The multi-stress list on the CSSRI page belongs to KRL 283 and was excluded.

pest_resistance.summary: Aphid and shoot-fly resistance: No evidence found for KRL 1-4 in the digest. The CSSRI page lists multi-stress resistance for KRL 283, which was excluded.

agronomic_details.yield: Yield potential per CSSRI: 4.0 t/ha in normal soils and 3.0 t/ha in sodic soils (pH up to 9.3). A conflicting figure on the same page gives 5.2 t/ha in normal soils and 3.5 t/ha in salt-affected soils (pH up to 9.3, EC up to 6 dS/m). The original variety record gives an average yield of 4100 to 4900 kg/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources beyond the salinity range (ECe 6.0 to 7.0 dS/m, pH up to 9.3) and the multi-site Zn/ionome study that included KRL 1-4 (one of 36 genotypes, 2013-14 and 2014-15).
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for salt-affected soils of the North West Plain Zone (NWPZ) and North East Plain Zone (NEPZ). Suitable for timely sown conditions. Germination is delayed under salt stress, so timely sowing is essential. Seed rate of 125 kg/ha is advised for salt-affected soils.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Dwarf type with 145 days to maturity. Hard, medium-bold, amber grain. Quality: about 11% protein, 77 kg/hl test weight, sedimentation value 29. Non-lodging and non-shattering per original variety record.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) ICAR-IARI Water Technology Centre, New Delhi: field trials under saline irrigation of 1.7 to 12 dS/m reported water-productivity gains with foliar potassium for KRL-1-4. (2) Rabi 2012-13: grain yield increase of 4.5 to 20% over control (source reports rabi 2011-12 and 2012-13 evaluations of different cultivars under salinity stress). (3) Multi-site Indian field study of grain Zn and ionome (2013-14 and 2014-15): KRL 1-4 is one of 36 genotypes; no yield result for KRL 1-4 was reported in the digest. (4) Pot study (not a field trial): proline and reducing sugars rose most strongly with salinity in KRL 1-4 compared with UP 2338. (5) Farmer demonstrations on alkali soils with other CSSRI wheat lines are reported; the page gives no KRL 1-4 yields.

genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Parent-level salinity QTL (Nax1/Nax2 in Kharchia 65) are documented in the digest, but the source does not name KRL 1-4, so they are not attributed to this variety. QTL/marker study on KRL 1-4 itself: No evidence found.
