salinity.details: Bred for salt tolerance to ECe 6.0 dS/m in saline soils and to pH 9.2 in alkaline soils (CSSRI states it was bred for both conditions). Tolerates salinity up to ECe 7.0 dS/m and was the first wheat variety released for saline and sodic soils of the NWPZ. Sodicity tolerance is listed as up to pH 9.3 with salinity tolerance of 7.0 dS/m. Germination is unaffected up to pH 9.4 if sown under proper moisture conditions (original variety record; not an independent digest finding). A pot study reported that proline and reducing sugars rose with salinity most strongly in KRL 1-4, which the study classes as the tolerant cultivar (compared with UP 2338). A field trial at the ICAR-IARI Water Technology Centre (New Delhi) under saline irrigation of 1.7 to 12 dS/m reported water-productivity gains with foliar potassium for KRL-1-4.

genetics_and_qtl.parentage_and_pedigree: Kharchia 65 x WL 711. Kharchia 65 is described as the most salt-tolerant wheat variety from Rajasthan, derived from Kharchia Local x EG 953. WL 711 is described as a well-adapted, high-yielding Punjab variety derived from (S. 308 x Chris) x Kalyan Sona. A review also gives the cross as Kharchia 65 and WL 711 and calls it promising for northern India. The review states that all Indian salt-tolerant cultivars, including KRL 1-4, are progeny of Kharchia 65.
genetics_and_qtl.breeding_line_designations: Named as KRL 1-4 (CSSRI naming; the Seednet name KRL-1-4 is treated as the same variety). Variety code A0104209 was not verified against Seednet, as no Seednet search was run. No IET/AICRP entry codes found.
genetics_and_qtl.breeding_method: Pedigree selection. Improved from Kharchia 65 for amber grain, dwarf habit, lodging resistance and yield.

agronomic_performance.yield: Yield potential per CSSRI: 4.0 t/ha in normal soils and 3.0 t/ha in sodic soils (pH up to 9.3). A conflicting figure on the same page gives 5.2 t/ha in normal soils and 3.5 t/ha in salt-affected soils (pH up to 9.3, EC up to 6 dS/m). The original variety record gives an average yield of 4100 to 4900 kg/ha.
agronomic_performance.stability: Not found in searched sources beyond the salinity range (ECe 6.0 to 7.0 dS/m, pH up to 9.3) and the multi-site Zn/ionome study that included KRL 1-4 (one of 36 genotypes, 2013-14 and 2014-15).
agronomic_performance.adaptation: Recommended for salt-affected soils of the North West Plain Zone (NWPZ) and North East Plain Zone (NEPZ). Suitable for timely sown conditions. Germination is delayed under salt stress, so timely sowing is essential. Seed rate of 125 kg/ha is advised for salt-affected soils.
agronomic_performance.plant_characteristics: Dwarf type with 145 days to maturity. Hard, medium-bold, amber grain. Quality: about 11% protein, 77 kg/hl test weight, sedimentation value 29. Non-lodging and non-shattering per original variety record.
agronomic_performance.field_trials: (1) ICAR-IARI Water Technology Centre, New Delhi: field trials under saline irrigation of 1.7 to 12 dS/m reported water-productivity gains with foliar potassium for KRL-1-4. (2) Rabi 2012-13: grain yield increase of 4.5 to 20% over control (source reports rabi 2011-12 and 2012-13 evaluations of different cultivars under salinity stress). (3) Multi-site Indian field study of grain Zn and ionome (2013-14 and 2014-15): KRL 1-4 is one of 36 genotypes; no yield result for KRL 1-4 was reported in the digest. (4) Pot study (not a field trial): proline and reducing sugars rose most strongly with salinity in KRL 1-4 compared with UP 2338. (5) Farmer demonstrations on alkali soils with other CSSRI wheat lines are reported; the page gives no KRL 1-4 yields.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: KRL-1-4 (Wheat)

Name check: The CSSRI pages write the name as "KRL 1-4" or "KRL 1–4". The Seednet name "KRL-1-4" is the same variety. I ran no search against the Seednet portal itself, so no Seednet listing, variety code (A0104209), or Seednet-specific detail was retrieved. All evidence below refers to KRL 1-4 under the CSSRI naming. The KRL 3-4, KRL 19, KRL 210, KRL 213, KRL 283 and KRL 99 pages were excluded because they name other lines.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Bred for salt tolerance to ECe 6.0 dS/m in saline soils and to pH 9.2 in alkaline soils; the Division says this variety was bred for both conditions. -- https://cssri.res.in/varieties-developed/
- Tolerates salinity up to ECe 7.0 dS/m, and was the first wheat variety released for saline and sodic soils of the NWPZ. -- https://cssri.res.in/varieties-developed/
- Sodicity tolerance is listed as up to pH 9.3 with salinity tolerance of 7.0 dS/m. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/335146803_SALINITY_TOLERANCE_IN_WHEAT
- A pot study found proline and reducing sugars rose with salinity most strongly in KRL 1-4, which it classes as the tolerant cultivar (compared with UP 2338). -- https://www.vegetosindia.org/journal/vegetos/article.php?id=6434
- Field trials at the ICAR-IARI Water Technology Centre (New Delhi) under saline irrigation of 1.7 to 12 dS/m reported water-productivity gains with foliar potassium for KRL-1-4. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/324237969_Evaluation_of_different_wheat_cultivars_under_salinity_stress
- Waterlogging, drought and heat tolerance: No evidence found for KRL 1-4 specifically. The waterlogging claims found refer to KRL 3-4 and were excluded.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Described as having disease resistance to all prevalent rusts and as lodging-resistant. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/257650699_tolerant_crop_varieties_developed_at_CSSRI_Karnal_India_a_success_story
- Karnal bunt, aphid, shoot-fly resistance: No evidence found for KRL 1-4. (The multi-stress list on the CSSRI page is for KRL 283.) -- https://cssri.res.in/varieties-developed/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Dwarf type with 145 days to maturity; hard, medium-bold, amber grain. -- https://cssri.res.in/varieties-developed/
- Yield potential: 4.0 t/ha in normal soils and 3.0 t/ha in sodic soils (pH up to 9.3). -- https://cssri.res.in/varieties-developed/
- A conflicting figure on the same CSSRI page gives 5.2 t/ha in normal soils and 3.5 t/ha in salt-affected soils (pH up to 9.3, EC up to 6 dS/m). -- https://cssri.res.in/varieties-developed/
- Quality: about 11% protein, 77 kg/hl test weight, sedimentation value 29. -- https://cssri.res.in/varieties-developed/
- Grain yield increase of 4.5 to 20% over control in rabi 2012-13. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/324237969_Evaluation_of_different_wheat_cultivars_under_salinity_stress
- Grain Zn/ionome study: KRL 1-4 is one of 36 genotypes in a multi-site Indian field study (2013-14 and 2014-15). -- https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0192026
- Farmer demonstrations on alkali soils (with other CSSRI wheat lines) are reported by the Institute, but the page does not give KRL 1-4 yields. -- https://cssri.res.in/technology-evaluation-and-transfer/

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage: Kharchia 65 x WL 711 (matches the record). A review states the cross was Kharchia 65 and WL 711, and calls it promising for northern India. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/354652937_Salinity_Stress_in_Wheat_Effects_Mechanisms_and_Management_Strategies
- All Indian salt-tolerant cultivars, including KRL 1-4, are described as progeny of Kharchia 65. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/354652937_Salinity_Stress_in_Wheat_Effects_Mechanisms_and_Management_Strategies
- Breeding method: pedigree selection. Improved from Kharchia 65 for amber grain, dwarf habit, lodging resistance and yield. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/257650699_tolerant_crop_varieties_developed_at_CSSRI_Karnal_India_a_success_story
- Parent-level salinity QTL (Nax1/Nax2 in Kharchia 65) are documented, but the source page does not name KRL 1-4, so it is not attributed here. QTL/marker study on KRL 1-4 itself: No evidence found.
- Genome resources: No evidence found for KRL 1-4 specifically.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developed by ICAR-Central Soil Salinity Research Institute (CSSRI), Karnal, and released through the Central Sub-Committee on Crop Standards, Notification and Release of Varieties in 1990. -- https://cssri.res.in/crop-improvement/
- Named breeder(s): No evidence found. The CSSRI pages name the Division and Institute but no individual breeder for KRL 1-4.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Central Soil Salinity Research Institute, Zarifa Farm, Kachawa Road, Karnal – 132001 (India); phones 91-184-2290501 and 91-184-2291156; email director.cssri@icar.gov.in. -- https://cssri.res.in/highlights/
- A second CSSRI page gives the same address and phones, with email cssridirector@gmail.com. This is a non-ICAR address and should be verified before use. -- https://cssri.res.in/technology-evaluation-and-transfer/
- Breeder-level contact: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- Vegetos (2024). Investigating biochemical changes and protein profile of salt-tolerant and salt-sensitive wheat cultivars in response to salinity stress. Vegetos -- https://www.vegetosindia.org/journal/vegetos/article.php?id=6434 ; DOI 10.1007/s42535-024-00991-4 (authors not shown in retrieved text)
- Authors not retrieved (n.d.). Tolerant crop varieties developed at CSSRI Karnal, India: a success story. ResearchGate/CSSRI report -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/257650699_tolerant_crop_varieties_developed_at_CSSRI_Karnal_India_a_success_story (authors and year not shown in retrieved text)
- Authors not retrieved (2021/2022). Quantitative Dissection of Salt Tolerance for Sustainable Wheat Production in Sodic Agro-Ecosystems through Farmers' Participatory Approach: An Indian Experience. Sustainability 13(6):3378 -- https://www.mdpi.com/2071-1050/13/6/3378 ; DOI not retrieved
- Authors not retrieved (2018). Salinity tolerance in wheat (review). ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/335146803_SALINITY_TOLERANCE_IN_WHEAT
- Authors not retrieved (2018). Evaluation of different wheat cultivars under salinity stress (rabi 2011-12 and 2012-13). ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/324237969_Evaluation_of_different_wheat_cultivars_under_salinity_stress
- Authors not retrieved (2017). Variation in grain Zn concentration, and the grain ionome, in field-grown Indian wheat. PLOS ONE -- https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0192026 ; DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0192026
- KrishiKosh theses, AICRP/ICAR annual reports: No evidence found (not reached in the four searches).

SEED AVAILABILITY
- CSSRI produced about 15.1 t of breeder seed and 108.1 t of certified seed of KRL 1-4 and KRL 19 over ten years (combined figure, not split by variety). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/257650699_tolerant_crop_varieties_developed_at_CSSRI_Karnal_India_a_success_story
- Breeder and truth-labelled seed of salt-tolerant wheat is distributed to national and state agencies and farmers; the page gives combined totals for all salt-tolerant wheat, not KRL 1-4 alone. -- https://cssri.res.in/crop-improvement/
- NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or private dealer listings: No evidence found (searched once; no seed-agency page returned).

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Recommended for salt-affected soils of the NWPZ and NEPZ. -- https://cssri.res.in/varieties-developed/
- NWPZ states listed for KRL1-4: Punjab, Haryana, western Uttar Pradesh and northern Rajasthan; NEP

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Amrita (HI 1500), Wheat

Name check: Searches used "Amrita (HI 1500)" and "HI 1500" (the variety_name). The Seednet name (also "Amrita (HI 1500)") and code A0104233 never appeared in any result, so no evidence under the Seednet name was found. Pages below refer to HI 1500 / Amrita, which matches the variety. Some pages write the name as "Amrta" or "HI-1500", and the sources are not all consistent. Release year 2003 and the recommended-state list are not confirmed by an official notification.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- A commercial seed-information page describes HI 1500 as a drought-tolerant, high-yielding wheat suited to central India, with reduced performance under low irrigation. -- https://www.kisaanhelpline.com/variety/wheat-amrta-hi-1500 (commercial site, not verified against an official source)
- A review of heat- and water-efficient varieties lists Amrita (HI 1500) among high-yielding central-Indian wheats with heat tolerance and water-use efficiency, but does not give trial data for this variety specifically. -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Adaptability-of-durum-wheat-variety-HI-8759-to-changes-in-agronomic-conditions_tbl1_342231273
- A Wheat Cultivation in India guide and a special-features guide both place HI 1500 in the timely-sown, rainfed or restricted-irrigation group, where it was grouped with varieties yielding about 35 q/ha under restricted irrigation versus 15-20 q/ha rainfed. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/301204375_Wheat_A_guide_on_special_features_of_varieties_for_different_production_conditions_in_India
- A drought-adaptation morphological study from Pantnagar includes an HI 1500 row in its data table, but the columns are not labelled in the snippet, so no drought score can be read from it. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/322632219_Morphological_Characterization_for_Identification_of_Drought_Adapted_Genotypes_in_Wheat_Triticum_aestivum_L_under_Drought_Stress

DISEASE AND PEST
- Central-zone Sharbati newsletter reports Amrita (HI 1500) as valued for good yield and resistance to stem and leaf rust. -- https://graingenes.org/ggpages/awn/66/AWNVOL66.pdf
- Leaf-rust resistance is attributed to gene Lr24, which the study postulated in HI 1500 from multi-pathotype tests and then validated genetically; the paper reports HI 1500 resistant to all Indian leaf-rust pathotypes tested. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/280082991_Validation_of_Lr24_in_some_released_bread_wheat_varieties_and_its_implications_in_leaf_rust_resistance_breeding_and_deployment_in_central_India
- An IARI Wellington rust-gene list names HI 1500 (Amrita) among released varieties carrying Lr24/Sr24. -- https://iari.res.in/files/Publication/Nilgiri_Wheat_News/Nilgiri_Wheat_News_02012023.pdf
- No evidence found for stripe rust, Karnal bunt, spot blotch or insect resistance specific to this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- A seed-information page gives 135-140 days maturity, 45-50 q/ha yield under favourable conditions, timely sowing in mid-October to mid-November, and 40 kg/acre seed rate. -- https://www.kisaanhelpline.com/variety/wheat-amrta-hi-1500 (commercial, unverified)
- A Madhya Pradesh package-of-practices blog lists HI-1500 (Amrita) as an early-sown rainfed option sown 20 October to 30 October, and as an early-sown 1-2 irrigation option sown 20 October to 10 November. -- https://digitalkheti.blogspot.com/2016/11/cultivation-of-wheat-package-of.html
- A Krishisewa extension page lists HI 1500 (Amrita) under timely-sown restricted irrigation (20 October to 10 November, 1-2 irrigations). -- https://krishisewa.com/crop-cultivation/improved-wheat-cultivation-practices-in-central-india/
- IARI Regional Station Indore frontline demonstrations in 2013-14 included HI 1500 on 16.35 ha, but the snippet names the location as IARI Regional Station, Kalimpong, which conflicts with Indore. -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/IARI-News/Newsletter_October-December-2014.pdf
- No evidence found for multi-location yield-trial tables specific to HI 1500, other than the AICRP-linked rows in the IIWBR trial result below.
- An AICRP-era trial table (IIWBR-linked 2008 paper) lists HI 1500 as entry G14 with yield figures, but the table is not readable in the snippet. -- https://journals.ansfoundation.org/index.php/jans/article/download/662/618/1202

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage: HW 2002*2 // STREMPALLI / PNC 5 (Lr24 study, ResearchGate; also the Indian-genotype SSR pedigree paper, and the drought table row). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/280082991_Validation_of_Lr24_in_some_released_bread_wheat_varieties_and_its_implications_in_leaf_rust_resistance_breeding_and_deployment_in_central_India ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/263554325_Genotypic_characterization_of_elite_Indian_wheat_genotypes_using_molecular_markers_and_their_pedigree_analysis
- Gene: Lr24 (postulated, then validated by crossing HI 1500 with Agra Local). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/280082991_Validation_of_Lr24_in_some_released_bread_wheat_varieties_and_its_implications_in_leaf_rust_resistance_breeding_and_deployment_in_central_India
- Genotyping: HI 1500 is one of 48 elite lines in a molecular-marker pedigree and genetic-similarity study, with coefficient-of-parentage values reported for the set. Marker-level results for HI 1500 are not in the snippet. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/263554325_Genotypic_characterization_of_elite_Indian_wheat_genotypes_using_molecular_markers_and_their_pedigree_analysis
- Breeding method: No evidence found for the cross-and-selection history beyond the parentage string.
- Breeding-line code: No evidence found for an IARI breeding-line code for HI 1500 beyond "HI 1500".
- Genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The IARI Regional Station at Indore is listed as having released after 2000 varieties including Amrita (HI 1500), and it is the station that developed the HI series. -- https://www.iari.res.in/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=301&Itemid=735
- The AICRP notified-varieties list names HI 1500 (AMRITA) in a column of released varieties, but the snippet does not show which developing station is in its cell. -- https://www.aicrpwheatbarleyicar.in/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/wheat-varieties-notified-in-india.pdf
- Lead breeder name: No evidence found. The name Y.M. Upadhyaya appears in an Indore newsletter only as a memorial-lecture figure and is not linked to HI 1500, so it is not attributed here. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348432282_IARI_Indore_Madhya_Bharat_Wheat_News_Vol_62
- Mutation-breeding work by Vishwakarma, Das, Singh and Sai Prasad at IARI RS Indore on "sharbati" wheats mentions HI-1500 in the same paragraph, but the snippet does not confirm that the mutants were derived from HI 1500, so it is not attributed. -- https://graingenes.org/ggpages/awn/67/AWN_VOL_67.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institution: ICAR-IARI, Regional Station, Indore (Madhya Pradesh). Only the institute page URL was retrieved. No official email, phone or postal address for the station appeared in the results. -- https://www.iari.res.in/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=301&Itemid=735
- Institute-level contacts: Not found in the retrieved snippets. Check the IARI site contact page directly.
- Named scientists at Indore (Sai Prasad S.V., Head and Principal Scientist, per a 2014 newsletter; Das B.K.; Vishwakarma G.) are listed as station staff, but no contact details were found for them and they are not confirmed as HI 1500 breeders. -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/IARI-News/Newsletter_October-December-2014.pdf

PUBLICATIONS

- Vishwakarma G., Das B.K., Singh J.B., Sai Prasad S.V., Gadekar D.A. (year not shown). Improved sharbati wheat mutants suitable for cultivation in the Central Zone of India. Annual Wheat Newsletter Vol. 67 -- https://graingenes.org/ggpages/awn/67/AWN_VOL_67.pdf (HI 1500 link to the mutant work not confirmed)
- Authors not shown (year not shown). Genotypic characterization of elite Indian wheat genotypes using molecular markers and their pedigree analysis. drought.details: The IARI technology options document lists HD 2888 (Pusa Wheat 107) as moderately resistant to drought. This document has a conflicting release record (2003, SVRC Delhi, NCR Delhi), so the drought rating should be treated with caution. The input record (not web-verified) states good degree of tolerance to moisture stress and good performance under timely-sown rainfed conditions. No mechanisms were found in the searched sources.

heat.details: In a field study at RAU Pusa farm, HD 2888 (named 'HD 2888' in the evidence) was rated relatively heat tolerant on the heat susceptibility index among 18 genotypes. The rating is relative and no absolute score was found. A 2017 wheat-barley newsletter lists HD2888 among high-chlorophyll genotypes, but gives no stress-specific score for this variety.

disease_resistance.summary: Leaf (brown) rust, stem (black) rust and stripe (yellow) rust: high resistance, per the zone-wise variety page (named 'HD 2888'). Leaf blight: good resistance per the zone-wise page; the input record (not web-verified) describes moderate resistance to leaf blight. Powdery mildew and foot rot: good resistance per the zone-wise page. Soil-borne diseases: moderate resistance per the IARI technology options document. Spot blotch: HD 2888 appears among NEPZ entries in a 2017 spot blotch screening of 1,281 genotypes, but no resistance score for this variety was found in the excerpt. The input record also refers to adult plant resistance to the most virulent races of leaf and stem rust; the record names HD 2833 in that statement, so it is not attributed to this variety.

pest_resistance.summary: No pest resistance evidence found in searched sources. The input record (not web-verified) states no serious pest problem was observed in the field.

agronomic_details.yield: Conflicting records. The IARI technology options document gives 2.5-2.8 t/ha. The zone-wise variety page gives an average yield of 4.5 t/ha. The input record gives 2250 QTL/HA under normal conditions, a unit value that does not match the other records and should be verified.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Timely-sown rainfed conditions in the NEPZ region, per the input record and a farmer-information page. The zone-wise page describes late-sown irrigated conditions, which conflicts with this. The input record also cites medium maturity suited to Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Assam and parts of eastern UP. The zone-wise page also lists Orissa, Sikkim and NE plains, which are not in the input record and were not web-verified in the other records.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Input record (not web-verified): performs well under timely-sown rainfed conditions, with no lodging and no shattering. Morphological characteristics: Unknown.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) RAU Pusa farm field study: HD 2888 was rated relatively heat tolerant on the heat susceptibility index among 18 genotypes. (2) ICAR-IIWBR 2017 newsletter: HD2888 is included in NEPZ spot blotch screening (1,281 genotypes, 2012-13 to 2016-17) and in NEPZ quality tables, but no site-level yields for this variety were found in the excerpts. (3) The 2017 newsletter also lists HD2888 among high-chlorophyll genotypes, with no score given.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
Searches were run for variety name, breeder/institution, research papers and seed availability (4 queries in total). Pages were checked for "HD-2888" or "Pusa Wheat-107" before a finding was kept. Two name variants appear in the evidence: "Pusa Wheat-107 (HD-2888)" in the CSC notification list and "HD 2888 (Pusa Wheat 107)" in the IARI and AICRP documents. The Seednet name is identical to the CSC name.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Heat: in a field study at RAU Pusa farm, HD 2888 was rated relatively heat tolerant on the heat susceptibility index among 18 genotypes (evidence names "HD 2888") -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/281086563_HEAT_STRESS_INDUCED_MALE_STERILITY_OF_WHEAT_VARIETIES_AT_ANTHESIS_IN_RELATION_TO_HIGH_TEMPERATURE
- Drought: IARI technology options list HD 2888 (Pusa Wheat 107) as moderately resistant to soil-borne diseases and drought (conflicting release record, see AGRONOMY) -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Publication/Others/Tech_Options_English-15072014.pdf
- Heat/chlorophyll-related screening: a 2017 wheat-barley newsletter table lists HD2888 among high-chlorophyll genotypes, with no stress-specific score for this variety -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/Wheat-Barley-Newsletter-V.111-2017.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- Rust and other diseases: a zone-wise variety page (evidence names "HD 2888") reports high resistance to stripe, stem and leaf rusts, good resistance to leaf blight, powdery mildew and foot rot -- https://ztmbpd.iari.res.in/technologies/varietieshybrids/cereals/wheat/
- Spot blotch: a 2017 newsletter lists HD 2888 among NEPZ entries in a spot blotch screening across 1,281 genotypes (2012-13 to 2016-17). No resistance score for this variety was found in the excerpt -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/Wheat-Barley-Newsletter-V.111-2017.pdf
- Soil-borne disease: IARI technology options describe moderate resistance to soil-borne diseases -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Publication/Others/Tech_Options_English-15072014.pdf
- Pest resistance: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity and yield (conflicting records): the IARI document gives 145 days and 2.5-2.8 t/ha, with release in 2003 by SVRC Delhi for NCR Delhi -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Publication/Others/Tech_Options_English-15072014.pdf
- Maturity and yield (conflicting records): the zone-wise variety page gives 110-115 days maturity, average yield 4.5 t/ha, and a late-sown irrigated condition -- https://ztmbpd.iari.res.in/technologies/varietieshybrids/cereals/wheat/
- Production condition: a farmer-information page places HD-2888 under rainfed, timely-sown conditions for the NEPZ region -- https://krishisewa.com/crop-varietes/wheat-varieties/
- Multi-location trial data: the 2017 newsletter includes HD2888 in NEPZ spot blotch and quality tables. No site-level yields for this variety were found in the excerpts -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/Wheat-Barley-Newsletter-V.111-2017.pdf
- Flooding, submergence and salinity: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage (C 306/T.sphaerococcum//HW2004): No evidence found. The parentage string is only in the input record.
- QTL, markers and genome resources: No evidence found.
- Breeding-line code: No evidence found beyond the variety names.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Notified variety list: "Pusa Wheat-107 (HD-2888)" appears with notification date 25/04/2006 and S.O. 599(E) in a Bihar government notified-variety list -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf
- Institution: an IARI page lists HD 2888 under its wheat varieties, and the zone-wise variety page describes releases from IARI New Delhi. Neither names a breeder -- https://ztmbpd.iari.res.in/technologies/varietieshybrids/cereals/wheat/ ; https://www.iari.res.in/files/Publication/Others/Tech_Options_English-15072014.pdf
- Lead breeder or scientist name(s): No evidence found. A notified-varieties table lists names near a wheat entry, but they are not linked to HD 2888 and are not recorded here.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute page (no contact details in the retrieved text): https://www.iari.res.in/en/introduction.php?div_id=33
- Official email, phone and postal address: No evidence found.
- Breeder contact: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- Heat stress induced male sterility of wheat varieties at anthesis in relation to high temperature. Field trial at RAU Pusa farm (HD 2888 included among 18 genotypes). ResearchGate record -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/281086563_HEAT_STRESS_INDUCED_MALE_STERILITY_OF_WHEAT_VARIETIES_AT_ANTHESIS_IN_RELATION_TO_HIGH_TEMPERATURE
- ICAR-IIWBR Wheat-Barley Newsletter Vol. 111 (2017). Spot blotch screening of 1,281 genotypes and NEPZ tables with HD2888. Authors listed include R P Gangwar, Suresh Kumar, Rinki and Vinod Tiwari -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/Wheat-Barley-Newsletter-V.111-2017.pdf
- Authors, year, DOI and KrishiKosh thesis/AICRP report with this variety: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU seed sales or private dealer listings for HD 2888 / Pusa Wheat-107: No evidence found. The search returned online listings for a different wheat variety (Pusa Tejas HI-8759), which were discarded.

heat.details: In a delayed-sowing trial (35 days late, to expose the crop to heat at the reproductive stage), DBW-14 had high membrane stability index, high chlorophyll stability index and high canopy temperature depression, and showed smaller yield losses than other genotypes. Separately, DBW 14 is listed as a recurrent parent in heat-tolerance introgression work alongside PBW 343 and PDW 233. The CSC record describes tolerance to late heat stress in Northeastern India, indicated by very low yield and grain weight reductions under very late sowing. search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: DBW-14 (Wheat)
Name checked: "DBW-14" (CSC variety name) and "DBW-14" (Seednet name, same string). Seednet portal evidence was not found under either name. Input release year is 2003; the PLoS ONE table and the PMC pedigree table both give 2002. Input parentage is RAJ 3765/PBW 343, which matches both sources. Several results named other varieties (DBW 187, DBW 222, DBW 327, DBW 371, DBW 386, DBW 443, PBW 343, RAJ 3765, PBW 826) and were excluded.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Heat: in a delayed-sowing trial (35 days late, to expose the crop to heat at reproductive stage), DBW-14 had high membrane stability index, chlorophyll stability index and canopy temperature depression, and showed smaller yield losses than other genotypes. Authors and journal details are not in the retrieved text. -- https://www.ijcmas.com/abstractview.php?ID=16186&vol=9-2-2020&SNo=265
- Heat (breeding use): DBW 14 is listed as a recurrent parent in heat-tolerance introgression work, alongside PBW 343 and PDW 233. -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/DWR-Perspective-Plan-Vision-2025.pdf
- Drought, salinity, flood, submergence: No evidence found. The searches did not return DBW-14 results for these stresses.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Karnal bunt: DBW 14 is among the varieties that the DWR pocket guide suggests for producing Karnal bunt-free wheat. The guide's resistance-to-leaf-blight note refers to other varieties, not DBW 14. -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/EB-52-Wheat-Cultivation-in-India-Pocket-Guide.pdf
- Karnal bunt screening: DBW 14 was one of the checks in the Karnal bunt score evaluation of double haploid lines. -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/DWR-Annual-Report-2012-13.pdf
- Fusarium graminearum: DBW 14 was one of the wheat varieties in a spike-infection table after inoculation. The retrieved text gives no percentage values for DBW 14. -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/DWR-Annual-Report-2012-13.pdf
- Powdery mildew: DBW 14 is a recurrent parent in the powdery mildew breeding programme, with Pm donors Ae. speltoides (Pm 12), T. longissimum (Pm 13) and T. spelta (Pm1d). -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/DWR-Perspective-Plan-Vision-2025.pdf
- Rusts, other pests: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Release and zone: DBW-14 is listed as a NEPZ variety with a 2002 release, low-sown ("LS") production condition, and irrigated conditions. -- https://journals.plos.org/ (correction notice) https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC5903606/
- Maturity, plant height, yield: No DBW-14 values found. The AICRP report (https://www.aicrpwheatbarleyicar.in/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/wheat-varieties-notified-in-india.pdf) mentions DBW 14 as a recent release in a zone, but the retrieved text does not show its yield.
- Late-sown and seed production: DBW 14 is listed in the seed production chain for IIWBR-bred varieties. -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/DWR-Perspective-Plan-Vision-2025.pdf
- Trials: No DBW-14-specific multi-location results were found. The 2025-26 wheat research report (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/400935256_Wheat_Research_Report_2025-26) refers to RAJ 3765 and PBW 343 only, so it is excluded.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Pedigree: Raj 3765/PBW 343. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6065306 ; https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC5903606/
- Breeding-line code: Code 3 in the N-use efficiency study table. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6065306
- Parental and donor use: DBW 14 is listed as a donor or parent for heat tolerance and for grain-weight traits (synthetic hexaploid source). -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/DWR-Perspective-Plan-Vision-2025.pdf ; https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JWR/article/download/90083/36774/231170
- Breeding method, QTL/markers, genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: Directorate of Wheat Research (DWR), Karnal, now ICAR-IIWBR (Indian Institute of Wheat and Barley Research). -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/DWR-Perspective-Plan-Vision-2025.pdf
- Lead breeder or scientist name: No evidence found. The pedigree and release tables give no breeder name for DBW-14.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institution: ICAR-Directorate of Wheat Research, Karnal-132 001, Haryana, India (postal address as printed in the pocket guide). -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/EB-52-Wheat-Cultivation-in-India-Pocket-Guide.pdf
- Institute contact page: https://iiwbrseed.in/wheat-details.aspx has a "Contact us" link, but the retrieved page text gives no DBW-14 entry and no phone or email.
- Email, phone: No evidence found.
- Breeder contact: No evidence found.

disease_resistance.research_summary: Karnal bunt: the DWR pocket guide lists DBW 14 among varieties suggested for producing Karnal bunt-free wheat, and DBW 14 was one of the checks in a Karnal bunt score evaluation of double haploid lines (no score values in the digest). Fusarium graminearum: DBW 14 was included in a spike-infection table after inoculation, but the retrieved text gives no percentage values for DBW 14, so no resistance level can be assigned. Powdery mildew: DBW 14 is a recurrent parent in the powdery mildew breeding programme (Pm donors Ae. speltoides (Pm 12), T. longissimum (Pm 13), T. spelta (Pm1d)); this does not by itself establish resistance. Brown rust and leaf blight: the CSC record reports tolerance to brown rust (the prevalent rust in the NEPZ) and tolerance to leaf blight and other diseases. This is CSC-supplied data and is not supported by a digest source URL. Rusts other than the CSC note: no evidence found in digest.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pusa Wheat-105 (HD-2833)

Name note: The CSC release minutes name is "Pusa Wheat-105 (HD-2833)". The Seednet name is the same. Sources also use "Pusa Tripti (HD-2833)" as an alias for the same HD-2833 line. I treated that alias as the same variety, but it is not a separate confirmation. Searches run: 4 (the maximum allowed). Only the first search returned any usable variety-specific material.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The searches returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence data for HD-2833 or Pusa Wheat-105. The results were about other varieties (HD3086, HI 8759 Pusa Tejas, HD 3386, HS 542) and general heat-tolerance studies, which do not name this variety. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9638138/ (HD3086, not this variety, discarded)

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. No rust, Karnal bunt, or other disease or pest data for HD-2833 was returned. The only rust-related pages were for other varieties (HI 8759, HD 3386). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/342231273_High_yielding_durum_wheat_variety_HI_8759_Pusa_Tejas_-a_new_rust_and_karnal_bunt_resistant_variety (HI 8759, not this variety, discarded)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Krishisewa's wheat variety list gives Pusa Tripti (HD-2833), released in 2006 by IARI New Delhi, as suited to late-sown irrigated conditions in the peninsular/plains zone. -- https://krishisewa.com/crop-varietes/wheat-varieties/
An IIWBR wheat cultivation pocket guide lists HD 2833 among late-sowing varieties. The snippet does not give yield or agronomy details. -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/EB-52-Wheat-Cultivation-in-India-Pocket-Guide.pdf
An IARI technology options document has an HD 2833 (Pusa Tripti) entry giving 5.21 t/ha average yield, timely-sown irrigated production, and a 2010 CVRC release year for hilly areas of Tamil Nadu and Kerala. This conflicts with the 2006 release year and the 2006 date from the other sources. The text around the entry also appears to mix in another zone's entry, so treat this entry as unverified. -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Publication/Others/Tech_Options_English-15072014.pdf
No multi-location trial data for this variety was found.

GENETICS AND QTL
Parentage given in the record is PBW226/HW1042(TR380-147/3Ag#14//HD2285. No independent source confirmed this parentage, so it is recorded from the input record only.
No evidence found for QTL, marker, gene, or genome-resource data for HD-2833. The QTL results returned were for other materials. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC12758827/ (IARI SNP QTL study, variety not named as HD-2833, discarded)

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution (per input record and IARI-related sources): Division of Genetics, Indian Agricultural Research Institute, New Delhi. -- https://www.iari.res.in/en/introduction.php?div_id=33 (institute overview; does not name HD-2833 breeders)
No lead breeder or scientist name for HD-2833 was found in any search result.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: Harshita (HI-1531), Wheat

Search budget note: the four allowed searches ran, but the follow-up request to read full page text hit the tool limit. The findings below come from truncated search snippets, so several headings are incomplete. Searches used "Harshita (HI-1531)" and "Harshita (HI - 1531)". I did not find a separate Seednet portal page.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- Snippet describes HI 1531 as an early-maturing, semi-dwarf bread wheat suited to low-input, rainfed and restricted-irrigation conditions. No specific drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence scores were visible. -- https://indianjournals.com/article/ijgpb-68-2-abs005

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found in the retrieved text. Snippet mentions only glume traits (white, pubescent glumes) and ear shape, not resistance ratings.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Snippet indicates early maturity, semi-dwarf stature, and a target of low-input, rainfed or restricted-irrigation systems in the Central Zone. No yield or multi-location trial data were visible. -- https://indianjournals.com/article/ijgpb-68-2-abs005

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) -- No evidence found in the retrieved text. Parentage HI 1182 / CPAN 1990 is from the user-supplied record and was not confirmed by any search result.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Snippet states the variety was developed by the Indian Agricultural Research Institute, but the text is cut off before the station and breeder names. The Regional Station, Indore attribution comes from the user-supplied record only. -- https://indianjournals.com/article/ijgpb-68-2-abs005

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder, institute email, phone, address or contact-page URL appeared in the retrieved snippets.

PUBLICATIONS -- Indian Journal of Genetics and Plant Breeding (volume 68, issue 2) (year not visible in snippet). Notification of bread wheat variety HI 1531 (Harshita). Indian Journal of Genetics and Plant Breeding -- https://indianjournals.com/article/ijgpb-68-2-abs005
Authors and year not retrieved; the article is the notification note on HI 1531 (Harshita) and should be checked directly for authors, year and DOI.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- Private dealer listing only: Gold Mayur Natural Wheat Seeds, HI-1531 Harshita, 40 kg pack, Indore, offered by Mayur Seeds & Agritech. Treat as low reliability: the listing wrongly calls HI 1531 a hybrid, and it is not an NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK or SAU source. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/wheat-seeds-hi-1531-harshita-sharbati-21295958712.html

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Snippet gives the Central Zone as the target zone. The seednet record lists Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh, but no search result confirmed the state list. -- https://indianjournals.com/article/ijgpb-68-2-abs005

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: MP-4010 (wheat)

Name note: The CSC release-minutes name and the Seednet name are both "MP-4010" (Seednet crop: WHEAT (GEHON), code A0104341). Every finding below refers to that name. The searches did not return a Seednet portal page, so the Seednet record itself was not verified. Two other spellings appeared in the sources: "MP 4010" and "MP4010". Where a source used a different variety with a similar name, I did not use it.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Drought and heat: MP 4010 was one of 16 wheat genotypes grown under high-temperature and drought stress in a study of intra-spike grain-size variation. The paper reports that grain-area variation in MP 4010 was strongly influenced by environment. No tolerance rating was given. -- https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-023-44503-x
- Salinity, flood, submergence: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found for MP-4010 resistance or susceptibility to rusts, Karnal bunt, flag smut or other diseases, or to insect pests. The sources reviewed mention MP 4010 only in variety lists or trial tables. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/341821786_WHEAT_RESEARCH_REPORT_2018-19 ; https://www.aicrpwheatbarleyicar.in/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/wheat-varieties-notified-in-india.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Notification: The Bihar agriculture department's notified-variety list gives MP-4010 a release/notification date of 12/03/2003 (notification 283(E)). The list is for Bihar, so it does not establish state recommendation. -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf
- Yield in an IARI Indore regional trial: MP 4010 was used as a check and yielded 47.4 q/ha, against 51.6 q/ha for the entry that was identified for release. The entry's gain over MP 4010 was 8.9 percent. The same source says the entry's maximum potential was 70.6 q/ha. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348432282_IARI_Indore_Madhya_Bharat_Wheat_News_Vol_62
- AICRP 2024-25 workshop: MP4010 was a standard check in a trial with HD2932, HI1634 and CG1029. Sowing was December 5-15 at 125 kg/ha. -- http://www.aicrpwheatbarleyicar.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/Proceedings-of-64th-AICRP-Workshop-17.10.2025.pdf
- Late-sown performance: The ICAR Directorate of Wheat Research perspective plan lists MP 4010 as a suitable alternative to the susceptible variety Lok 1 under late sowing in central India. -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/DWR-Perspective-Plan-Vision-2025.pdf
- Maturity, plant height, 1000-grain weight, average yield (as a released-variety record): No evidence found for MP-4010 specifically.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage: The search did not confirm the Angostura-88 pedigree. No evidence found beyond the input record.
- Use as a parent: Crosses listed as VL 922 x MP 4010, PW 612 / MP 4010, and GW 2007-77 (D) / MP 4010 appear in a Gwalior study of discriminant function analysis for yield improvement. The study was run in 2018-19 at the Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding, College of Agriculture, RVSKVV Gwalior. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/370419935_Discriminant_function_analysis_for_yield_improvement_in_bread_wheat_Triticum_aestivum_L
- Breeding line codes, breeding method, QTL, markers, genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Lead breeder name: No evidence found. The input record names only the "Wheat Breeder, JNKVV College of Agriculture, Gwalior." 
- Institution: The Gwalior college that appears in the 2019 study is named as RVSKVV (Rajmata Vijayaraje Scindia Agricultural University), Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding. The input record names JNKVV. The sources do not explain the difference, so the institution name should be checked against the CSC minutes before use. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/370419935_Discriminant_function_analysis_for_yield_improvement_in_bread_wheat_Triticum_aestivum_L
- The AICRP notified-varieties table lists MP 4010 in a column that also includes Gwalior. The column layout is garbled, so the developer cannot be assigned with confidence. -- https://www.aicrpwheatbarleyicar.in/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/wheat-varieties-notified-in-india.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
- No individual breeder contact found.
- No institute-level email or phone found.
- Address-level information only: Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding, College of Agriculture, Rajmata Vijayaraje Scindia Agricultural University, Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh. This comes from the 2019 study's affiliation line, not a contact page. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/370419935_Discriminant_function_analysis_for_yield_improvement_in_bread_wheat_Triticum_aestivum_L
- Suggested next step: check the JNKVV or RVSKVV Gwalior contact pages directly. They were not returned by search.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not shown (n.d.). Discriminant function analysis for yield improvement in bread wheat (Triticum aestivum L.). ResearchGate (Gwalior department study, approx. 2022-23) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/370419935_Discriminant_function_analysis_for_yield_improvement_in_bread_wheat_Triticum_aestivum_L
- Authors not shown (2023). Image facilitated assessment of intra-spike variation in grain size in wheat under high temperature and drought stress. Scientific Reports (URL indicates s41598-023) -- https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-023-44503-x
- Authors not shown (2020). Madhya Bharti Wheat News, Vol. 6(2). IARI Regional Station, Indore -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348432282_IARI_Indore_Madhya_Bharat_Wheat_News_Vol_62 (this issue names MP 4010 only as a check)
- Authors not shown (2019). Wheat Research Report 2018-19. AICRP trial report (MP 4010 appears in a yield table) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/341821786_WHEAT_RESEARCH_REPORT_2018-19
- Dedicated MP-4010 KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP annual report entry, or breeding paper: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found for MP-4010 at NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU seed sales or private dealers.
- The fourth search returned unrelated items: a pea variety, wheatgrass microgreen seed, a Canadian pea product, and a Himachal district sales notice for DBW-187 and PBW-550. None of these name MP-4010.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Madhya Pradesh / Central Zone (as the input record reads "Unknown"): The ICAR Madhya Pradesh state page lists MP 4010 among irrigated late-sown technologies for the state. -- https://icar.gov.in/en/node/17271
- The DWR perspective plan places MP 4010 in the Central Zone bread wheat list for late sowing. -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/DWR-Perspective-Plan-Vision-2025.pdf
- The Bihar notification list records the notification date, but does not state where the variety is recommended. -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf

EVIDENCE DIGEST: Shalimar Wheat-1 (SKW-196), Wheat

Both refer to the same variety. No Seednet portal page was returned by any search, so no evidence came from Seednet itself. Seednet variety code A0104356 was not found in any result.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- The Crimson prospectus describes it as suited to rainfed or restricted-irrigation conditions in the temperate climate of Kashmir; the source does not explicitly say drought-tolerant. -- https://crimsonpublishers.com/mcda/fulltext/MCDA.000810.php
STRESS TOLERANCE (heat, salinity, flood, submergence) -- No evidence found in the retrieved text for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST (other pests, insects, nematodes) -- No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Maturity given as about 225–235 days, responds well to fertilizer, and yield given as roughly 35–38 q/ha. -- https://crimsonpublishers.com/mcda/fulltext/MCDA.000810.php

drought.details: No drought tolerance was found for this variety in the retrieved pages. The CSC record notes stable performance under late and very late sown conditions with very low grain yield reductions, but this is a sowing-date observation and not a drought test.

heat.details: The CSC record (ground truth) lists tolerance to heat stress, and it reports stable performance under late and very late sown conditions of the Central Zone with very low yield reductions. The digest does not confirm heat tolerance from any retrieved page and gives no quantitative heat data. The HI 1634 paper uses HD 2932 only as a yield check, so it is not evidence for this variety. The level is medium because the heat claim rests on the CSC record alone and is not corroborated by the digest sources.

disease_resistance.summary: Brown rust (leaf rust): resistance per CSC record and per the special-features entries (adult-plant resistance per Bhawani Seeds; seedling and adult-plant resistance to almost all pathotypes per IARI 2014 note). Black (stem) rust: resistance per CSC record and the second special-features entry; seedling resistance to almost all pathotypes per IARI 2014 note. Yellow (stripe) rust: adult-plant resistance per Bhawani Seeds; resistance per the first special-features entry; seedling resistance to almost all pathotypes per IARI 2014 note. Leaf blight: good levels of resistance per IARI 2014 note; resistance per the first special-features entry. Powdery mildew: good levels of resistance per IARI 2014 note. Foot rot: good levels of resistance per IARI 2014 note. Karnal bunt: resistance per both special-features entries (the reference guide layout is jumbled, so these entries are treated with caution). Leaf blast: moderate resistance is mentioned in the IARI 2014 note, but the text is cut off, so the claim is not confirmed. Gene postulation for rust resistance: not reliably assigned because of the layout problems in the reference guide.

pest_resistance.summary: Insect pest resistance: No evidence found.

agronomic_details.yield: CSC record: average yield 41.7 q/ha (recorded as 41.7 QT). Bhawani Seeds: 4.5-5.0 t/ha under late-sown irrigated conditions. IARI 2014 note: average yield 5.0 t/ha. The reference guide lists potential yield 61.8 q/ha, but these values are unverified because the layout is jumbled and they may belong to an adjacent entry.
agronomic_details.stability: CSC record: stable performance under late and very late sown conditions of the Central Zone with very low reductions in grain yield. Multi-location trial data beyond these summaries: No evidence found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Irrigated late-sown conditions (CSC record and Bhawani Seeds). IARI 2014 note: suited to high-fertility, irrigated, late-sown conditions of the NEP zone. CSC record: recommended for Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Kota and Udaipur divisions of Rajasthan, Maharashtra and Karnataka under irrigated late-sown conditions, early maturity group (92-130 days).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: CSC record: amber grain with very good scores for grain hardness, appearance, high protein content, hectolitre weight, sedimentation value, and iron, zinc and other micronutrient content; very good chapatti quality and excellent bread-making quality. Plant height 84 cm, maturity 112 days and 1000-grain weight 43.7 g are listed in the reference guide but are unverified (possible adjacent entry). The IARI 2014 note gives seed-to-seed maturity of 115-120 days, which differs from the CSC value of 109 days.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Notified under the name HD 2932 after three years of All India Wheat Coordinated Trials testing (reference guide and DBW 17 notification text). Yield summaries are from Bhawani Seeds (4.5-5.0 t/ha, late-sown irrigated), the IARI 2014 note (5.0 t/ha) and the CSC record (41.7 q/ha). Multi-location trial data beyond these summaries: No evidence found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pusa Wheat-111 (HD-2932), Wheat

Name check: The CSC minutes name (Pusa Wheat-111(HD-2932)) and the Seednet name are identical, so all evidence below refers to the same name. The Bihar list, the IARI and IIWBR documents, and the breeding papers use HD 2932 or Pusa Wheat 111 as synonyms for this variety. Search budget: 4 of 4 used. The seed-availability search did not target NSC, state seed corporations, or SAU seed sales specifically.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Late-sown irrigated adaptation is the recorded production condition, and it has been noted as suited to late-sown irrigated conditions -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344250282_Wheat_A_Reference_Guide_Highlighting_Special_Features_of_Varieties_Recommended_for_Cultivation_in_India
IARI's 2014 technology options note says it suits high-fertility, irrigated, late-sown conditions of the NEP zone -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Publication/Others/Tech_Options_English-15072014.pdf
No heat, drought, salinity, flood, or submergence tolerance was found for this variety in the retrieved pages. The HI 1634 heat-tolerance paper uses HD 2932 only as a yield check, so it is not evidence of heat tolerance in this variety -- https://www.academia.edu/104746552/HI_1634_Pusa_Ahilya_high_yielding_bread_wheat_variety_tolerant_to_terminal_heat_stress_conditions_of_Central_Zone

DISEASE AND PEST
Adult-plant resistance to brown and yellow rusts, with high zinc content and wide adaptability -- http://www.bhawaniseeds.in/Wheat.html
Seedling resistance to almost all pathotypes of the three rusts, adult-plant resistance to virulent rust pathotypes, and good levels of resistance to leaf blight, powdery mildew and foot rot -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Publication/Others/Tech_Options_English-15072014.pdf
Resistance to yellow and brown rusts, leaf blight and Karnal bunt (special-features entry, with gene postulation layout too jumbled to assign genes reliably) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344250282_Wheat_A_Reference_Guide_Highlighting_Special_Features_of_Varieties_Recommended_for_Cultivation_in_India
Resistance to black and brown rusts and Karnal bunt, with high yellow pigment (a second special-features entry, with the same gene-postulation layout problem) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344250282_Wheat_A_Reference_Guide_Highlighting_Special_Features_of_Varieties_Recommended_for_Cultivation_in_India
Moderate resistance to leaf blast is mentioned in the IARI 2014 note, but the text is cut off, so the claim is not confirmed -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Publication/Others/Tech_Options_English-15072014.pdf
Insect pest resistance: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Average yield of 4.5-5.0 t/ha under late-sown irrigated conditions -- http://www.bhawaniseeds.in/Wheat.html
Average yield of 5.0 t/ha, with seed-to-seed maturity of 115-120 days -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Publication/Others/Tech_Options_English-15072014.pdf
Plant height 84 cm, maturity 112 days, 1000-grain weight 43.7 g, and potential yield 61.8 q/ha are listed in the reference guide. The layout is jumbled, so these values could belong to an adjacent entry. Treat them as unverified -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344250282_Wheat_A_Reference_Guide_Highlighting_Special_Features_of_Varieties_Recommended_for_Cultivation_in_India
Notified under the name HD 2932 after three years of All India Wheat Coordinated Trials testing -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/291495202_Notification_of_a_wheat_variety_DBW_17
Multi-location trial data beyond these summaries: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Pedigree KAUZ/STAR//HD2643 (matches the parentage field) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344250282_Wheat_A_Reference_Guide_Highlighting_Special_Features_of_Varieties_Recommended_for_Cultivation_in_India
The notification text states HD2932 was developed from a cross involving Pusa Vishesh; the snippet is truncated, so the full parentage is not confirmed -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/291495202_Notification_of_a_wheat_variety_DBW_17
Lr19/Sr25 introgression into the HD2932 background produced line HD3209. This is a derivative line, not the variety itself -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC11187221/
HD2932 was converted into a CMS line (with HD3086) using A-GW365 as the cytoplasm donor, with 628 SSR markers used for genome recovery. This is a derivative line, not the variety itself -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12606944/
Breeding method, QTL, and marker data for the variety itself: No evidence found.
Discarded: "Unnat HD 2932" (HD 3407) is a different, derived variety with a similar name, so its entries are excluded -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/wheat-variety-synonyms-in-india-a-comprehensive-list/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Division of Genetics, ICAR-IARI, New Delhi is the institution named in the CSC release minutes, and it matches the institute affiliation on the 2024 HD3209 paper -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC11187221/
One reference-guide entry names ICAR-IARI Regional Station, Shimla as developer; another names Agharkar Research Institute, Pune. These entries are not reliably linked to HD 2932 because of the layout -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344250282_Wheat_A_Reference_Guide_Highlighting_Special_Features_of_Varieties_Recommended_for_Cultivation_in_India
Named lead breeder: No evidence found. The IIWBR compendium and the AICRP notified-varieties PDF list breeder names per variety, but the retrieved text did not show them for HD 2932 -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/RB-51-Compendium-of-Wheat-Varieties-Notified-in-India-During-2018-2023.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
Institute-level address (from paper affiliation): Division of Genetics, ICAR-Indian Agricultural Research Institute, New Delhi, 110012, India -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC11187221/
Official email, phone, and breeder contact: No evidence found.
IIWBR (Karnal) is the nodal wheat centre, but no contact details were retrieved -- https://www.aicrpwheatbarleyicar.in/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/wheat-varieties-notified-in-india.pdf

PUBLICATIONS

drought.details: The variety record describes high resistance to drought and thermo-insensitivity. The 2007 release announcement reports that the variety helps secure yield under deficient irrigation (water-saving claim). The Hindi dealer page (Pusa Purna HI 1544) also states drought tolerance, but the digest marks this as unverified and not from an official source, so it is given no weight. No field-trial data quantifying drought response were found in the digest. Level reflects the official variety record plus the release-announcement claim; the digest contains no independent quantitative drought data.

heat.details: The official-source journal abstract reports that the variety combines early maturity, stable yield and tolerance to terminal heat. The variety record describes it as thermo-insensitive. A seed trade listing repeats the terminal heat tolerance claim, but trade listings are weaker evidence. The sowing-date study (CCS HAU Hisar, 2017-18) shows yield declining steeply with late sowing (9.1% at 25 November, 21.0% at 15 December, 42.3% at 5 January), which indicates sensitivity to late-season heat stress when sowing is delayed, though the study does not isolate heat as the cause. Early maturity (110-115 days) is cited as a mechanism for escaping terminal heat.

salinity.details: Not found in searched sources. The digest reports no evidence for salinity tolerance.

flood.details: Not found in searched sources. The digest reports no evidence for flood or waterlogging tolerance.

disease_resistance.summary: Stem rust: high field resistance under natural and artificial screening (IJGPB 68(2) abstract), and seedling and field resistance to stem and leaf rust pathotypes (2007 release announcement). Leaf rust (Puccinia triticina): resistant to all Indian leaf-rust pathotypes in a Central India study that lists HI 1544 among four varieties; this study is part of the Lr24 validation work. Wilt: resistance is claimed on an Amazon retail listing for 'HI 1544 Sharbati'. The digest marks this as conflicting with the official rust-resistance profile and unverified, so it is not accepted as established. Black rust, flag smut, Karnal bunt and high-protein claims were found in the Madhya Bharat Wheat News but refer to other entries (MP 3465, HI 8765) and are excluded for HI 1544. Other diseases: Not found in searched sources.

pest_resistance.summary: Rice weevil (Sitophilus oryzae): reported as least susceptible among tested cultivars (tested alongside GW 322) in the Lr24 study. The snippet is mixed with other page text, so this must be verified against the full paper. No other pest resistance evidence found; remaining pests: Not found in searched sources.

agronomic_details.yield: Average yield 51.4 q/ha (2007 release announcement; the variety record gives 51.40 q/ha under normal conditions). Yields 6.3% above GW 190 and 8% above Lok-1 (release announcement). Superiority of 7.9% over Lok-1 in three years of National trials by DWR Karnal (IJGPB abstract). Mahabeej listing gives 48-52 q/ha. Compendium 2018-2023 reports 51.2 q/ha under timely sowing, grouped with GW 366. Sowing-date study (CCS HAU Hisar, 2017-18) recorded 6007 kg/ha at 5 November sowing, the highest among varieties tested. Dealer pages give 51-55 q/ha in some listings; official values are preferred.
agronomic_details.stability: Highest yield under timely sowing and equally good under late planting in agronomic evaluation (IJGPB abstract). The Hisar sowing-date study shows yield loss with delayed sowing: 9.1% at 25 November, 21.0% at 15 December and 42.3% at 5 January. Stability across environments beyond these sources: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for timely sown, irrigated conditions in the Central Zone (DWR Wheat Cultivation pocket guide), for Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat and Kota and Udaipur divisions of Rajasthan. Suitable for low to high fertility and irrigated timely-sown November plantings (variety record). Seed rate 125 kg/ha, spacing 23 cm (irrigated).
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 110 To 115Days (official variety record). Mahabeej listing gives 115-120 days; dealer pages vary (105-110, 110-115, 115-120 days). Official values are preferred.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: WHITE & PUBESCENT GLUMES, WHITE AURICLE, ELLIPTICAL AND MEDIUM DENSE EARHEAD, MEDIUM BOLD, AMBER AND HARD GRAIN. Semi-dwarf and early maturing (IJGPB abstract); non-lodging and non-shattering (variety record and Mahabeej listing); growth habit semi-erect (Mahabeej listing); grain medium bold and lustrous (variety record).
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) DWR Karnal National trials, three years: 7.9% yield superiority over Lok-1 (IJGPB abstract). (2) Agronomic evaluation: highest yield under timely sowing, equally good under late planting (IJGPB abstract). (3) Release trials: average 51.4 q/ha; 6.3% above GW 190 and 8% above Lok-1 (2007 release announcement). (4) 2018-2023 compendium: 51.2 q/ha under timely sowing, grouped with GW 366. (5) CCS HAU Hisar sowing-date study, 2017-18: highest grain yield at 5 November sowing (6007 kg/ha) and top among varieties; yield fell 9.1%, 21.0% and 42.3% for later sowings. Excluded: the Madhya Bharat Wheat News (Vol 6(2), 2020) figure of 51.42 q/ha is for a test entry, not HI 1544; the Journal of Cereal Research Vol 15(3) uses HI 1544 only as a check for HI 1636 trial data.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
VARIETY: Purna (HI-1544), wheat. Seednet name "Purna(HI-1544)" and variety code A0104383 did not appear in any search result. All evidence below refers to "HI 1544 (Purna)" under the names used in the notification and trade listings.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Early maturing, semi-dwarf, bred for high-fertility timely-sown Central Zone conditions; reported to combine early maturity, stable yield and tolerance to terminal heat -- https://indianjournals.com/article/ijgpb-68-2-abs007
- Reported to help secure yield under deficient irrigation, which is a water-saving claim from the 2007 release announcement -- https://www.seedquest.com/News/releases/2007/september/20491.htm
- Terminal heat tolerance is repeated in a seed trade listing -- https://www.nukrishi.com/products/wheat-hi-1544tl/
- Drought tolerance is stated only on a Hindi dealer page (Pusa Purna HI 1544, "सुखे के प्रति सहनशील"). This is unverified and not from an official source -- https://www.mkdseeds.com/Pusa%20Purna%20HI%201544%20Wheat%20Seeds
- Salinity, flood, submergence and waterlogging: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- High field resistance to stem rust and leaf rust under natural and artificial screening -- https://indianjournals.com/article/ijgpb-68-2-abs007
- Seedling and field resistance to stem and leaf rust pathotypes -- https://www.seedquest.com/News/releases/2007/september/20491.htm
- Resistant to all Indian leaf-rust pathotypes (Puccinia triticina) in a Central India study that lists HI 1544 among four varieties -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/280082991_Validation_of_Lr24_in_some_released_bread_wheat_varieties_and_its_implications_in_leaf_rust_resistance_breeding_and_deployment_in_central_India
- Least susceptible to rice weevil among tested cultivars (with GW 322), per the Lr24 study page. This snippet is mixed with other text on that page, so verify against the full paper -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/280082991_Validation_of_Lr24_in_some_released_bread_wheat_varieties_and_its_implications_in_leaf_rust_resistance_breeding_and_deployment_in_central_India
- Wilt resistance is claimed on an Amazon retail listing for "HI 1544 Sharbati". This conflicts with the official rust-resistance profile and is unverified -- https://www.amazon.in/wheat-Seeds-HI-1544-Sharbati/dp/B0CJRC2VYP
- Black rust, flag smut, Karnal bunt, and high-protein claims in the Madhya Bharat Wheat News refer to other entries (MP 3465, HI 8765), so they were excluded for HI 1544.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Yield superiority of 7.9% over Lok-1 in three years of National trials by DWR Karnal -- https://indianjournals.com/article/ijgpb-68-2-abs007
- Highest yield under timely sowing and equally good under late planting in agronomic evaluation -- https://indianjournals.com/article/ijgpb-68-2-abs007
- Average of 51.4 q/ha, with yields 6.3% above GW 190, 8% above Lok-1 -- https://www.seedquest.com/News/releases/2007/september/20491.htm
- 51.2 q/ha under timely sowing in the 2018–2023 compendium, where it is grouped with GW 366 -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/RB-51-Compendium-of-Wheat-Varieties-Notified-in-India-During-2018-2023.pdf
- Central Zone timely-sown recommendation in the DWR Wheat Cultivation pocket guide -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/EB-52-Wheat-Cultivation-in-India-Pocket-Guide.pdf
- Sowing-date study (CCS HAU Hisar, 2017–18): HI 1544 gave the highest grain yield on 5 November sowing (6007 kg/ha) and was top among varieties. Yield fell 9.1% for 25 November sowing, 21.0% for 15 December and 42.3% for 5 January -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/338511065_Effect_of_Sowing_Dates_and_Varieties_on_Yield_and_Quality_Performance_of_Wheat_Triticum_aestivum_L
- Mahabeej listing: maturity 115–120 days, growth habit semi-erect, non-lodging, non-shattering, yield 48–52 q/ha -- https://www.mahabeej.co.in/cereals?id=48
- Madhya Bharat Wheat News (Vol 6(2), 2020) uses HI 1544 as a check; it reports 51.42 q/ha for the test entry, not for HI 1544 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348432282_IARI_Indore_Madhya_Bharat_Wheat_News_Vol_62
- Journal of Cereal Research Vol 15(3) uses HI 1544 as a check for HI 1636 trial data; it is not a study of HI 1544 itself -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JWR/article/download/135083/55161/421851
- Maturity and yield values from dealer pages vary (105–110 days, 110–115 days, 115–120 days; 51–55 q/ha in some listings). Official values are preferred -- https://www.skbseeds.com/blog/best-variety-of-wheat-in-india

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage per the notification: derived from the cross "HD 2402/HW 3007" by pedigree method. The user record says HD 2404 / HW 3007. The number differs (2402 vs 2404), so verify against the official record -- https://indianjournals.com/article/ijgpb-68-2-abs007
- A different pedigree for HI 1544 appears in a central India leaf-rust study: HINDI 62/BOBWHITE//CPAN 2099. This conflicts with the notification pedigree and must be reconciled -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/365274273_Madhya_Bharat_Wheat_News_Volume_8_Issue_1 and https://www.researchgate.net/publication/280082991_Validation_of_Lr24_in_some_released_bread_wheat_varieties_and_its_implications_in_leaf_rust_resistance_breeding_and_deployment_in_central_India
- Lr24 testing: the Lr24 study crossed HI 1544 with DL 788-2 and reported segregation ratios. Gene identity and marker data should be confirmed in the full paper -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/280082991_Validation_of_Lr24_in_some_released_bread_wheat_varieties_and_its_implications_in_leaf_rust_resistance_breeding_and_deployment_in_central_India
- Breeding-line code: no evidence found beyond the HI 1544 designation. Genome resources, QTL, and marker studies specific to HI 1544: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developed by ICAR-IARI Regional Station, Indore. Author list in the notification: H. Pandey, R. Bhawsar, M. Samdur, S. Sai Prasad, A. Mishra, P. Varma, A. Singh, S. Kantwa. The lead breeder is not stated as such -- https://indianjournals.com/article/ijgpb-68-2-abs007

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: MP-1203 (Wheat)

Scope note: the search tool hit its usage limit after four queries, so the later checks on the breeder, contacts, publications and seed sources could not be re-run. Both names in the record are "MP-1203", so the evidence applies to both. Only one search result names this variety, and it is a secondary slide deck.

STRESS TOLERANCE: A slide deck on wheat cultivation lists MP-1203 among JNKVV varieties and describes it as terminal-heat tolerant with bold grains -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshare/wheat-cultivation/47807540 (secondary, non-official source; not verified against a JNKVV or ICAR document)

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found. The four searches returned no disease or pest resistance data for MP-1203.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: The same slide deck says MP-1203 is suited to late-sown irrigated conditions (I have not verified this claim against an official source) -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshare/wheat-cultivation/47807540. No yield data, maturity data or multi-location trial results were found.

GENETICS AND QTL: The GRIS (Genetic Resources Information System for Wheat and Triticale) accession page for MP-1203 gives the pedigree FASN/2*TEPOCA/3/CHEN/TR.TA/TRANSVAAL-AFRICA -- http://www.wheatpedigree.net/sort/show/117146. This differs from the parentage in the record (FASN/2*TEPOCA/3/CHEN/A. Squarrosa/TA), so the two pedigrees need reconciling against the CSC release minutes. No breeding-line code, breeding method, QTL or marker study was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: The slide deck attributes the variety to JNKVV (Jawaharlal Nehru Krishi Vishwa Vidyalaya, Madhya Pradesh) -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshare/wheat-cultivation/47807540. The record names the Zonal Agricultural Research Station, Powarkheda, but no source found links that station to MP-1203. No breeder name was found.

CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found. No breeder, institute email, phone or address was returned for MP-1203. The Powarkheda station address in the record (Powarkheda - 461 110, Hoshangabad, M.P.) comes from the input record, not from a search result.

PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found. The searches returned no peer-reviewed papers, AICRP or ICAR reports, or KrishiKosh theses for MP-1203.

SEED AVAILABILITY: An IndiaMART private-dealer listing (titled for "Wheat Seed Wh 1105") mentions "MP 1203 wheat seed", 40 kg PP bags, in Karera, Madhya Pradesh -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/wheat-seed-wh-1105-22808266155.html. This is a commercial listing for a different product title, so it is weak evidence. No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK or SAU seed-sales source was found, and the Seednet portal (seednet.gov.in) was not reached.

RECOMMENDED STATES: The slide deck's JNKVV description covers Madhya Pradesh. The record lists Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan, but no search result confirms the notified recommendation for any state -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshare/wheat-cultivation/47807540 (only MP is supported, and only weakly).

PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found (repeated under its own heading as required).

Recommended next steps: check the CSC release notification and the seednet.gov.in entry for code A0104394 for the official name, parentage, recommended states and breeder; check the JNKVV and ZARS Powarkheda sites for a breeder contact; and search KrishiKosh and AICRP wheat annual reports for MP-1203 trial data.

heat.details: A heat-stress study of bread wheat parents and F1 crosses reports PBW 590 as a heat-tolerant parent for grain yield per plant and harvest index, and as one of the most desirable parents in the late-sown evaluation (E2). A nitrogen-level trial at Baba Farid College reports PBW 590 with the maximum grain yield and maximum harvest index among the varieties tested; the page text is partly garbled and this is a single-site result. The original variety record states the variety is suitable for late-sown conditions and has tolerance to terminal heat stress. The level is rated medium because the evidence is from parent-evaluation and single-site studies rather than multi-location heat-stress trials.

disease_resistance.summary: Leaf rust: the original variety record (CSC) states PBW 590 possesses a higher degree of resistance to leaf rust under natural and artificial epiphytotic conditions than all the check varieties. Brown rust: resistance stated only by the third-party page noted above. Karnal bunt: a Karnal bunt comparison reports DBW 71 shows better Karnal bunt resistance than PBW 590, which was the latest check, implying PBW 590 is less resistant to Karnal bunt.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
PBW-590 (Wheat). Both names are the same: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "PBW-590", and no Seednet page was returned, so all evidence below refers to the name PBW-590. Variety code A0104396 did not appear in any result.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- A heat-stress study of bread wheat parents and F1 crosses reports PBW 590 as a heat-tolerant parent for grain yield per plant and harvest index, and as one of the most desirable parents in the late-sown evaluation (E2). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/326777394_Estimation_of_Heat_Stress_Tolerance_for_Yield_and_its_Contributing_Attributes_in_Bread_Wheat
- A nitrogen-level trial at Baba Farid College reports PBW 590 with the maximum grain yield and maximum harvest index among the varieties tested; the page text is partly garbled, so treat this as a single-site result. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/375026232_Response_of_Wheat_Triticum_aestivum_L_Varieties_to_Nitrogen_Levels
- No evidence found for drought, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to PBW 590.

DISEASE AND PEST
- A Wheat Cultivation in India pocket guide recommends PBW 590 for late-sown conditions as a stripe (yellow) rust-avoidance option in NWPZ and NHZ. -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/EB-52-Wheat-Cultivation-in-India-Pocket-Guide.pdf
- A third-party agronomy page (not an official source) states PBW 590 is resistant to yellow and brown rusts and is about 80 cm tall. -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/pn/agriculture/crops/cereals/wheat-kanak-gehu
- A Karnal bunt comparison says DBW 71 shows better Karnal bunt resistance than PBW 590, which was the latest check, implying PBW 590 is less resistant to Karnal bunt. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/270338427_DBW_71_A_new_wheat_variety_for_late_sown_irrigated_conditions_of_north_western_plains_zone_of_India
- No evidence found for leaf rust or other pest-specific resistance ratings in official sources.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- PAU breeder-seed release table entry: PBW 590, year 2008, yield 41.0 (q/ha), notification date 11.02.09, double dwarf (79 cm), suitable for late-sown irrigated conditions. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/357701641_Breeder_seed_production_of_wheat_at_PAU_A_way_to_quality_seed_availability
- A district study (Amritsar) recommends PBW 590 for late-sown conditions and notes sufficient late-sown area there. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/276135925_Performance_of_wheat_crop_in_Punjab_A_case_study_of_Amritsar_district
- Maturity: a third-party page gives about 128 days to harvest readiness (not an official source); no official maturity record found. -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/pn/agriculture/crops/cereals/wheat-kanak-gehu
- Yield values from official trials: only the 41.0 figure in the PAU table above; no multi-location AICRP yield table naming PBW 590 was found.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
