search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: MPO(JW) 1215 (MPO 1215), Wheat, variety code A0104404
Name note: The evidence below refers to "MPO 1215" or "MPO (JW) 1215" in both name forms. Most sources describe it as a durum (Triticum durum) wheat in the central zone, not a bread wheat. No Seednet portal page was returned by any search, so the Seednet name is not independently confirmed.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Listed among rust-resistant varieties recommended for the central zone, especially in Madhya Pradesh, for controlling Puccinia rust -- https://en.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cereals-and-millets/wheat
Listed among Ug99 (stem rust) resistant varieties from the Central Zone of India, alongside other varieties -- https://bgri.cornell.edu/wp-content/uploads/2020/11/saarc-nov2020-ada.pdf
Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found. Searches returned no trait-specific data for these stresses.

DISEASE AND PEST
Rust resistance: the Vikaspedia page above lists it as a rust-resistant variety for the central zone. The BGRI Ug99 list above includes it as a Ug99-resistant variety.
Wheat crop health newsletter (Nov 2023) lists MPO 1215 (d) among varieties reported in a rust-related context, but the excerpt does not state its resistance rating -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/Wheat-Crop-Health-Newsletter-Nov.-2023.pdf
Gene postulation (Sr/Lr genes): Not confirmed for this variety. The ResearchGate reference guide lists gene postulations, but the page layout mixes entries, so they cannot be reliably assigned to MPO 1215 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344250282_Wheat_A_Reference_Guide_Highlighting_Special_Features_of_Varieties_Recommended_for_Cultivation_in_India
Insect pest resistance: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Grain test weight highest in pooled organic-farming trial (58.00 g), ahead of HI 8627 -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Grains-of-bread-durum-and-local-wheat-varieties_fig1_350950793
Multi-location stability: MPO-1215 was among genotypes assessed for stability at Madhya Pradesh under conventional and zero tillage; it was stable across years under conventional tillage and showed a negative regression coefficient under zero tillage at that location -- https://www.scirp.org/journal/paperinformation?paperid=78066
Junagadh (Gujarat) hybrid trial, rabi 2017-18: MPO 1215 used as a parent in a heterosis study of ten lines -- https://www.chemijournal.com/archives/2019/vol7issue3/PartBK/7-3-394-807.pdf
Directorate of Wheat Research annual report 2012-13: MPO 1215 appears in varietal trial and check lists -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/DWR-Annual-Report-2012-13.pdf
Indian Farming article on durum HI 8713: MPO 1215 used as a zonal check in AVT trials; yield tables (2009-10 to 2011-12) give MPO 1215 mean yields of about 49.5 to 50 q/ha in several seasons -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/download/121681/46450/317172
Seed rate, sowing and fertilizer guidance for the central zone: Not specific to this variety. Vikaspedia and the Wheat Cultivation pocket guide list MPO 1215 (d) among central zone varieties without variety-specific agronomy -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/EB-52-Wheat-Cultivation-in-India-Pocket-Guide.pdf

Pedigree: GW 1113 / GW 1114 // HI 8381 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344250282_Wheat_A_Reference_Guide_Highlighting_Special_Features_of_Varieties_Recommended_for_Cultivation_in_India

disease_resistance.summary: The notification describes DBW 39 as disease-resistant, but the retrieved text does not name the diseases. The ICAR-DWR pocket guide lists DBW 39 among varieties to be encouraged in rust-related and Karnal bunt-related recommendations; the text is ambiguous about which disease each list refers to, so this is unconfirmed. The IIWBR compendium (2018-2023) has a garbled table row for DBW 39 with a 'highly resistant' note, but the disease cannot be identified from the extracted text. No disease resistance is confirmed for a named disease in the digest. The original variety record's claims of rust, leaf blight, foot rot and flag smut resistance are not corroborated by the digest and are not adopted here.

agronomic_details.yield: Average 44.3 q/ha and potential 55.2 q/ha over three years of multi-location tests, ranking first in the zone. Assam AICRP report: yield 30-35 q/ha (recommended 2019).
agronomic_details.stability: Wider adaptability and stable yields under both timely and late sown conditions, per the notification.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Digest evidence points to the North Eastern Plain Zone (NEPZ): the salinity study genotype listing (NEPZ, timely sown and irrigated), and adoption as one of the most popular NEPZ varieties in a 2017 newsletter. The digest does not contain a separate state recommendation statement.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Digest reports duration of 110-115 days (Assam AICRP report). The original variety record states 119 to 123 days. These figures are not reconciled in the digest.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Semi-erect growth habit; amber, hard and bold grain; chapati/bread quality. Spike density 349 spikes/m2, 31.1 grains per spike, 1000-grain weight 42 g. The digest contains no ear, awn, glume or other morphological descriptors.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Multi-location tests over three years: average 44.3 q/ha, potential 55.2 q/ha, first in zone. (2) Station trials at Karnal, 2001-03 (rabi), cited as the testing period in the notification. (3) Assam AICRP report: duration 110-115 days, yield 30-35 q/ha (recommended 2019). (4) Farmer-field demonstrations, 2012-14, 10 farmers: 39.0% yield increase over the check, benefit-cost ratio 1.95 under demonstration practice. (5) Yield components as listed above. A DBW 187 trial that uses DBW 39 as a check was excluded because it is not a DBW 39 result.

DBW 39 evidence digest (wheat, Triticum aestivum)

Name check: The variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "DBW 39", so every search used the same name. The Seednet portal page (variety code A0104407) did not appear in any search, so no Seednet-specific evidence was found. Four searches were run in total.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Stress-specific evidence for DBW 39 is thin. The notification reports wider adaptability and stable yield under both timely and late sowing, and bolder grains under late sowing -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/279806613_Notification_of_crop_variety_DBW_39_-_A_new_bread_wheat_variety
The DBW 39 entry in the salinity study is a genotype listing (Attila/Hui, 2010, NEPZ, timely sown and irrigated). It gives no DBW 39-specific salinity result -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC5903606/
No drought, heat, flood, submergence or waterlogging evidence specific to DBW 39 was found.

DISEASE AND PEST
The notification describes DBW 39 as a disease-resistant variety, but the retrieved text does not name the diseases -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/279806613_Notification_of_crop_variety_DBW_39_-_A_new_bread_wheat_variety
The ICAR-DWR pocket guide lists DBW 39 among varieties to be encouraged in rust-related and Karnal bunt-related recommendations. The text is ambiguous about which disease each list refers to, so treat it as unconfirmed -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/EB-52-Wheat-Cultivation-in-India-Pocket-Guide.pdf
The IIWBR compendium (2018-2023) has a garbled table row for DBW 39 with a "highly resistant" note, but the disease is not identifiable from the extracted text -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/RB-51-Compendium-of-Wheat-Varieties-Notified-in-India-During-2018-2023.pdf
No pest-resistance evidence was found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Yield: average 44.3 q/ha and potential 55.2 q/ha over three years of multi-location tests, ranking first in the zone -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/279806613_Notification_of_crop_variety_DBW_39_-_A_new_bread_wheat_variety
Yield components: high spike density (349 spikes/m2), 31.1 grains per spike, and 1000-grain weight of 42 g -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/279806613_Notification_of_crop_variety_DBW_39_-_A_new_bread_wheat_variety
Growth habit and grain: semi-erect habit, amber, hard and bold grain, and chapati/bread quality -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/279806613_Notification_of_crop_variety_DBW_39_-_A_new_bread_wheat_variety
Maturity and yield in the Assam AICRP report: duration 110-115 days and yield 30-35 q/ha (recommended 2019) -- https://aau.ac.in/department/department_details/266
Farmer-field demonstrations (2012-14, 10 farmers): 39.0% yield increase over the check, with benefit-cost ratio 1.95 under demonstration practice -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/334084624_PERFORMANCE_OF_NEWLY_RELEASED_WHEAT_VARIETIES_AT_FARMER'S_FIELD
Station trials at Karnal, 2001-03 (rabi), are the testing period cited in the notification -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/279806613_Notification_of_crop_variety_DBW_39_-_A_new_bread_wheat_variety
Adoption: DBW 39 was named among the most popular varieties in NEPZ in a 2017 newsletter -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/Wheat-Barley-Newsletter-V.111-2017.pdf
A DBW 187 trial report uses DBW 39 as the best check and records DBW 187 with less late-sown yield loss. This is a comparison for DBW 187, not a DBW 39 result -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343097264_DBW_187_Notification

GENETICS AND QTL
Parentage: Attila/Hui (also written Attila/Hui in the AICRP table) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/279806613_Notification_of_crop_variety_DBW_39_-_A_new_bread_wheat_variety ; https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC5903606/ ; https://www.aicrpwheatbarleyicar.in/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/wheat-varieties-notified-in-india.pdf
Breeding-line code and breeding method: No evidence found.
QTL, markers and genome resources: No evidence found for DBW 39. The SSR and pathotype results in one search belong to DBW 187 and were discarded.

Developing institution: ICAR-Indian Institute of Wheat and Barley Research (formerly Directorate of Wheat Research), Karnal. The AICRP table lists IIWBR, Karnal as developer -- https://www.aicrpwheatbarleyicar.in/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/wheat-varieties-notified-in-india.pdf

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pusa Gautami (HD) 3086 (also searched as HD 3086 / HD3086). Crop: Wheat.
Name note: the variety_name and seednet_variety_name are identical in the input, and the sources use "HD 3086" or "HD3086 (Pusa Gautami)". No CSC minutes or Seednet portal page was retrieved, so the evidence below cannot be confirmed against either official record.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Reported resistant to yellow rust and brown rust under timely-sown irrigated conditions -- https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/HD-3086:-A-new-wheat-variety-for-irrigated,-timely-Singh-Prabhu/736859a81357049b9c322ccef2ce430e50375302
- Used as a parent of a 220-line RIL population grown at IARI under control, drought, heat and combined heat-drought stress. No tolerance rating for HD 3086 itself was given in the snippet -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/281264937_HD_3086_A_new_wheat_variety_for_irrigated_timely_sown_condition_of_North_Western_Plains_Zone_of_India
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to this variety as a standalone rating.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Rust resistance (yellow and brown): see STRESS TOLERANCE line 1 -- https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/HD-3086:-A-new-wheat-variety-for-irrigated,-timely-Singh-Prabhu/736859a81357049b9c322ccef2ce430e50375302
- Retailer listing claims high resistance to loose smut and flag smut. This is a commercial product page, not an official source, so treat as unverified -- https://www.amazon.in/Green-World-HD-3086-Gautami-Agriculture/dp/B0CG3K8FSJ
- A 2020-21 and 2021-22 IARI rabi study assessed yield loss from multiple pests on HD 3086. Its results were not in the retrieved text -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/281264937_HD_3086_A_new_wheat_variety_for_irrigated_timely_sown_condition_of_North_Western_Plains_Zone_of_India

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Released for timely-sown irrigated conditions in the North Western Plains Zone. Average yield 5.46 t/ha, yield potential 7.1 t/ha, superior to checks -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/281264937_HD_3086_A_new_wheat_variety_for_irrigated_timely_sown_condition_of_North_Western_Plains_Zone_of_India
- Semi-dwarf, about 93 cm tall, maturity about 143 days, average yield 54.56 q/ha (retailer listing, unverified) -- https://www.amazon.in/Green-World-HD-3086-Gautami-Agriculture/dp/B0CG3K8FSJ

seednet_fields.Institution Responsible for developing B: Himachal Pradesh Krishi Vishvavidayala, Regional Research Station, Kukumseri (Lahul & Spiti)
seednet_fields.Parentage: Selection out of the eight indigenous lines of buckwheat germplasm collected from the dry and wet temperate regions (tribals area) of Himachal Pradesh.
seednet_fields.Resemblence to Variety: Till date no other variety has been released/recommended for the dry & wet temperate regions of HP, Prior to the present variety, farmers were growing the mixture of various landraces.
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Dry and Wet temperate regions of Himachal Pradesh.
seednet_fields.Specific Morphological Characteristics: The leaves of this variety are a good source of rutin, which is used in medicines for controlling retinal hemorrhage. It is the first ever released variety for this zone; determinate bushy growth behaviour; Reddish pink stem; The flowers borne in axillary racemes ate small and having inconspicuous light green sepals; The seeds are bold and browinish grey in colour.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: plant height:70-75; this variety is self compatible and belongs to the species Fagopyrum tataricum. it is determinate (plant height 70-75 cm) and bushy in its growth and holds broad dark green leaves and brownish grey coloured conical seeds. it is very early (95-98 days) in maturity and fits well in the existing two crop system (peasbuckwheat and barley buck wheat) of tribal areas of H.P. it is tolerant to frost and resistant to powdery mildew, shattering and lodging. It is suitable for sowing in the second fortnight to the end of July, that is, after harvesting barley and peas. the seed requirement is 30 kg haley2 (row spacing 30 cm) and responds well to 40 kg N, 20kg P2O5 and 10kg K2O per hectare. Besides 16-18 q/ha1 of grain yield, it gives a green foliage cut (used as green vegetable) by clipping the crop at knee high stage with out having any significant effect on the grain yield. flour recovery from the seeds is good which is used for the preparation of panckers.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: Resistant to powdery mildew.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: No insect pest has been observed.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Chilika (OEB-10), Finger millet

Search status: I ran 4 web_search queries (variety, breeder/institute, research, seed availability). A fifth call to re-read full page text was blocked by a server tool-use limit, so this digest relies on the search snippets I could read. Several snippets were cut short, so some "No evidence found" entries may reflect truncation, not absence. Variety name evidence refers to "Chilika (OEB-10)" for the release minutes name and "CHILIKA (OEB-10)" for the Seednet name. I found no page using the Seednet code A0204014, so I cannot confirm the Seednet entry from these results.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- Partial evidence only. The Springer finger millet breeding chapter lists Chilika (OEB 10) as a cultivar with traits recorded as moderately resistant to blast and resistant to stem borer. No drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence data was visible in the snippet. -- https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-030-23108-8_3

DISEASE AND PEST -- Blast: moderately resistant. Stem borer: resistant. Same source as above. -- https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-030-23108-8_3

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. Searches returned no maturity, yield, or multi-location trial data naming this variety.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) -- Parentage GE-68 x GE-156 is supplied in the task brief only; I found no independent web source confirming it. No QTL or marker study naming Chilika was found. Ragi breeding overview (ResearchGate copy) returned, but the Chilika-specific text was not visible. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/336439015_Finger_Millet_Eleusine_coracana_L_Gartn_Breeding

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- The brief names the Small Millets Improvement Project, Berhampur/Semiliguda, OUAT. The ResearchGate/Springer breeding review appears to discuss Indian finger millet breeding in general; I could not confirm lead breeder names for Chilika from the visible text. No evidence found for named breeders.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder, institute email, phone, postal address, or contact page for the Small Millets Improvement Project, OUAT, appeared in the results.

PUBLICATIONS -- Springer chapter "Finger Millet (Eleusine coracana L. Gartn.) Breeding" (book chapter, year and authors not visible in snippet) -- https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-030-23108-8_3
ResearchGate version of the same review (authors and year not visible in snippet) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/336439015_Finger_Millet_Eleusine_coracana_L_Gartn_Breeding
The ScienceDirect results on folate fortification and on Levilactobacillus fermentation of finger millet are about finger millet food processing. They do not name Chilika in the visible text, so I excluded them.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. The seed-related search returned only food-science papers about finger millet fermentation, which are not about this variety.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found. The release minutes entry lists "Unknown", and no source gave a state recommendation.

Gaps to close next: check seednet.gov.in for code A0204014, the CSC release notification for 2001, OUAT Small Millets Project pages, and KrishiKosh for theses or AICRP Small Millets annual reports naming Chilika.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Ratnagiri (PR-1044), Finger millet (Eleusine coracana)

Name note: The evidence refers to "Ratnagiri (PR 1044)" in ANGRAU and compendium sources. The Seednet form "RATNAGIRI (PR-1044)" did not appear in any result, and I did not retrieve a Seednet page, so the Seednet name is unverified. The "variety_name" (CSC minutes) also did not surface. The searches returned no CSC notification text.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Described as drought tolerant and responsive to fertilizers, with uniform maturity -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/6_ARS_Peddapuram_Notable_Achievements.pdf
No evidence found for submergence, salinity, heat, or flood tolerance.

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. Searches returned blast and leaf spot resistance only for other varieties (for example Tirumala PPR 1012, CFMV-2/Gira, PR 202), which I have excluded.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Plant height is recorded as 90-100 cm, with semi-compact habit and large incurved ears of 6-7 fingers, 8.2-8.5 cm long -- https://www.dhan.org/smallmillets/docs/report/Compendium_of_Released_Varieties_in_Small_millets.pdf
Yield is listed as 25-30 (units as given, presumably q/ha) -- https://www.dhan.org/smallmillets/docs/report/Compendium_of_Released_Varieties_in_Small_millets.pdf
Protein content is reported as about 14.3-14.4 g/100 g, with ash 2.48 g and calcium 561 mg/100 g -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/6_ARS_Peddapuram_Notable_Achievements.pdf and https://www.dhan.org/smallmillets/docs/report/Compendium_of_Released_Varieties_in_Small_millets.pdf (the two sources give slightly different protein values, 14.43 and 14.33).
No multi-location or AICRP trial data for this variety were found.

GENETICS AND QTL
Pedigree: pure line selection from the local Mettachodi (Metta chodi) variety of Raghavapuram, Chintalapudi taluk, West Godavari district, selected under acquisition number PM 629 -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/6_ARS_Peddapuram_Notable_Achievements.pdf and https://www.dhan.org/smallmillets/docs/report/Compendium_of_Released_Varieties_in_Small_millets.pdf
Breeding method: pure line selection (inferred from the pedigree statement; the ANGRAU sheet lists the method only for other entries) -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/6_ARS_Peddapuram_Notable_Achievements.pdf
No breeding-line codes beyond PM 629, QTL, marker, or genome-resource studies for this variety were found. Generic finger millet genome papers were excluded because they do not name this variety.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developed by Agricultural Research Station (ARS), Peddapuram, Andhra Pradesh, now under Acharya N G Ranga Agricultural University (ANGRAU) -- https://www.dhan.org/smallmillets/docs/report/Compendium_of_Released_Varieties_in_Small_millets.pdf and https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/6_ARS_Peddapuram_Notable_Achievements.pdf
Lead breeder or scientist name: No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS
Institute-level only: ARS Peddapuram, East Godavari district, Andhra Pradesh, is an ANGRAU unit -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/6_ARS_Peddapuram_Notable_Achievements.pdf
No official email, phone, postal address, or contact page for ARS Peddapuram was found in any result. The ANGRAU PDF is the only institutional URL retrieved.

PUBLICATIONS
Report, author not stated in the retrieved excerpt: Compendium of Released Varieties in Small Millets (year not stated in the excerpt). Report -- https://www.dhan.org/smallmillets/docs/report/Compendium_of_Released_Varieties_in_Small_millets.pdf
ANGRAU notable achievements sheet, author not stated (undated). Document -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/6_ARS_Peddapuram_Notable_Achievements.pdf
No peer-reviewed papers, theses, KrishiKosh records, or conference papers specific to Ratnagiri (PR 1044) were found. The Peddapuram finger millet paper (PR 10-45, "A Newly Evolved Non-Lodging Finger Millet Variety") concerns a different culture and is excluded.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found for this variety. Searches returned Rani Brand and Pioneer Agro retail ragi products, which are not this variety, and these are excluded. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU, or dealer listing for Ratnagiri was found. Seednet, ANGRAU seed-sales, and KVK pages were not retrieved.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Andhra Pradesh, recorded as a state release -- https://www.dhan.org/smallmillets/docs/report/Compendium_of_Released_Varieties_in_Small_millets.pdf
Notification: S.O. 540(E) dated 24.7.1985 (state release), year of release 1985 -- https://www.dhan.org/smallmillets/docs/report/Compendium_of_Released_Varieties_in_Small_millets.pdf
The raw "Unknown" value in the input record is contradicted by these sources.

Gaps to close: the CSC/Gazette notification text, the Seednet entry, a named breeder, ANGRAU or ARS Peddapuram contact details, and any seed-chain listing.

heat.details: No evidence found for this variety. Heat tolerance was not reported in any searched source.

salinity.details: Sodic-soil tolerance is the trait the sources emphasise. The variety was screened as a check in a 120-genotype sodic-soil study at ADAC&RI Trichy. A national table of released finger millet varieties (1986-2016) lists it as tolerant to salinity. Another source describes it as well adapted to sodic soil and popular in the sodic cultivation belt of India. The original record states tolerance to sodic soils at pH 8.5 and above. The sources use qualitative wording ('tolerant', 'well adapted'), so the 'high' level reflects the consistency of the qualitative claims rather than a quantified tolerance score. Mechanisms were not described in the digest.

(2) Organic nutrient management trial on TRY 1 in sodic soil, kharif 2019 and 2020, ADAC&RI Tiruchirappalli: 100% RDF plus FYM gave the highest growth and yield; 125% N as vermicompost or composted poultry manure was recommended for productivity. (3) Crop residue composting trial that used TRY 1 as the test crop; results were not stated in the digest. (4) Genetic variability study of 120 genotypes under sodic conditions at ADAC&RI Trichy (kharif 2018), in which the variety was a check; its specific values were not stated in the digest. search_metadata.evidence_digest:
NAMES: CSC minutes name "TRY-1" and Seednet name "TRY-1". Every source that mentions this variety spells it "TRY 1" (space, no hyphen). I treated these as the same variety. The record's institution, "Soil Salinity Research Centre, Trichy", appears in none of the sources. The sources credit Anbil Dharmalingam Agricultural College and Research Institute (ADAC&RI), Tiruchirappalli, TNAU.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Sodic-soil tolerance is the trait the sources emphasise; the variety was screened as a check in a 120-genotype sodic-soil study at ADAC&RI Trichy -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/334113665_Studies_on_genetic_variability_in_finger_millet_Eleusine_coracana_L_Gaertn_genotypes_under_sodic_conditions_Research_Article_Studies_on_genetic_variability_in_finger_millet_Eleusine_coracana_L_Gaertn_
- Listed as tolerant to salinity in a national table of released finger millet varieties (1986-2016) -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/finger_millets_varieties.pdf
- Described as well adapted to sodic soil and popular in the sodic cultivation belt of India -- https://horizonepublishing.com/index.php/PST/article/download/6380/version/7128/6225/44509
- Drought, heat, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found. Searches returned blast, Striga and lodging resistance for other finger millet varieties (for example P-224 and the Kenyan KALRO releases), which were discarded. -- https://kalrotimps.com/timps/7

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Land configuration and nitrogen management trial on TRY 1 under sodic soil, kharif 2017, ADAC&RI Tiruchirappalli -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/328352422_Enhancement_of_Finger_Millet_Productivity_through_Land_Configuration_and_Nitrogen_Management_under_Sodic_Soil
- Organic nutrient management trial on TRY 1 in sodic soil, kharif 2019 and 2020, ADAC&RI Tiruchirappalli; 100% RDF plus FYM gave the highest growth and yield, and 125% N as vermicompost or composted poultry manure was recommended for productivity -- https://horizonepublishing.com/journals/index.php/PST/article/view/6149
- Crop residue composting trial that used TRY 1 as the test crop -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348961418_Growth_and_yield_of_finger_millet_as_influenced_by_crop_residue_composting
- Yield: 4010 kg/ha in sodic-soil conditions -- https://horizonepublishing.com/index.php/PST/article/download/6380/version/7128/6225/44509
- Maturity: 102 days in the TNAU Ragi Information System table, season kharif irrigated, sodic/saline soils -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/millets_ragi.html
- Duration 100-105 days and yield 20-25 (units as listed in source) -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/finger_millets_varieties.pdf
- Crop calendar: TRY 1 listed for irrigated Marghazipattam and Chithiraipattam sowing in most Tamil Nadu districts (not Kanyakumari or Nilgiris) -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/millets_ragi.html

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage: selection from HR 374, per the TNAU table. This matches the record's "RESELECTION FROM ACCESSION 350 (HR 374)" only in the HR 374 link. No source mentions accession 350 -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/millets_ragi.html
- Breeding method: in-house development by recombination breeding at TNAU -- https://horizonepublishing.com/index.php/PST/article/download/6380/version/7128/6225/44509
- Induced mutagenesis of TRY 1 with gamma rays and EMS to obtain early-maturing mutants -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/336439015_Finger_Millet_Eleusine_coracana_L_Gartn_Breeding
- Breeding-line codes: No evidence found.
- Genome or QTL/marker resources specific to TRY 1: No evidence found. General finger millet genomics reviews were discarded because they do not name this variety.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Breeder name(s): No evidence found. Sources describe the variety as in-house developed but name no scientist.
- Developing institution: TNAU, Anbil Dharmalingam Agricultural College and Research Institute, Tiruchirappalli -- https://horizonepublishing.com/index.php/PST/article/download/6380/version/7128/6225/44509
- Station: ADAC&RI, Tiruchirappalli (Trichy), Tamil Nadu -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/328352422_Enhancement_of_Finger_Millet_Productivity_through_Land_Configuration_and_Nitrogen_Management_under_Sodic_Soil
- Institute address fragment: "Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Tiruchirappalli-620 027, Tamil Nadu, India" -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/328352422_Enhancement_of_Finger_Millet_Productivity_through_Land_Configuration_and_Nitrogen_Management_under_Sodic_Soil

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
GAVARI (SR-11) EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name note: variety_name "Gavari (SR-11)" and seednet_variety_name "GAVARI (SR-11)" differ only in capitalisation. Evidence below refers to the same variety under both names, and the SR 11 code is used interchangeably. Crop: foxtail millet (Setaria italica). Searches run: 4.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Described as tolerant of foliar diseases and insect pests; no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data found for this variety. -- https://eurekamag.com/research/003/149/003149108.php
- Gavari is listed among varieties that are non-lodging and early, but this is a general table entry rather than a stress-specific finding. -- https://millets.res.in/technologies/foxtail_millet.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- Tolerant of foliar diseases and insect pests. -- https://eurekamag.com/research/003/149/003149108.php
- No variety-specific blast, downy mildew, smut or stem borer reaction found. The general foxtail blast, brown spot, rust and grain smut advice on the IIMR and PoP pages is not attributed to Gavari, so it is discarded. -- https://millets.res.in/technologies/2-Recommended_Package_of_Practices-Foxtail_Millet.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- In AICSMIP and on-station trials at Rajasthan during 1992-95, SR 11 gave 24% higher grain yield and 15% higher straw yield than the control SiA 326. -- https://eurekamag.com/research/003/149/003149108.php
- Plants are tall (about 125 cm) with straw yield up to about 5.5 t/ha. -- https://eurekamag.com/research/003/149/003149108.php
- Maturity is 75-80 days, with bold grain of 12.04% protein and 4.83% oil. -- https://eurekamag.com/research/003/149/003149108.php
- Millets.res.in table lists Gavari (SR 11), RAU Rajasthan, 1994, 75-80 days, 15-16 q/ha, Rajasthan. The 1994 year differs from the 1995 release year in the record. -- https://millets.res.in/technologies/foxtail_millet.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- Pedigree: pure-line selection from local germplasm of Dungarpur district (Zone IV B), matching the parentage field. -- https://eurekamag.com/research/003/149/003149108.php
- DUS morphology: Gavari (SR 11) has non-pigmented inflorescence and medium inflorescence bristles, and apical sterility is recorded as present. -- https://www.academia.edu/35425416/DISTINCTNESS_UNIFORMITY_AND_STABILITY_DUS_CHARACTERIZATION_USING_MORPHOLOGICAL_TRAITS_OF_FOXTAIL_MILLET_Setaria_italica_L_Beauv
- No breeding-line code beyond SR 11, no QTL, marker or gene study naming this variety, and no variety-specific genome resource found. The genome papers found are on other accessions and are discarded. Variety code A0205002 was not found on any page.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The source note says the breeding programme was started in the 1990s at Rajasthan Agricultural University, with SR 11 developed by pure-line selection. -- https://eurekamag.com/research/003/149/003149108.php
- The newsletter note is by Maloo, S.R. (1997). This shows the note's author only; it does not confirm Maloo as the lead breeder. -- https://eurekamag.com/research/003/149/003149108.php
- Institution per the record: Associate Professor (Minor Millets), Rajasthan College of Agriculture, Rajasthan Agricultural University, Udaipur. The web sources only say "RAU, Rajasthan".
- No breeder name confirmed by the search results.

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder or variety-specific contact found. No RAU / Rajasthan College of Agriculture email, phone or address was returned by any search.
- Institute-level (national foxtail mandate, not Gavari-specific): ICAR - Indian Institute of Millets Research, Rajendranagar, Hyderabad - 500 030, Telangana. -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/brochures/Foxtail_Millet_Brochure.pdf
- Phone and email for the institute were not present in the retrieved text.

PUBLICATIONS
- Maloo, S.R. (1997). Gavari (SR 11) - A foxtail millet for Rajasthan, India. International Sorghum and Millets Newsletter 38: 120. -- https://eurekamag.com/research/003/149/003149108.php
- Listing only, no entry text retrieved: "Compendium of Released Varieties in Small Millets" (DHAN Foundation) includes SR 11 (Gavari) in its variety list. -- https://www.dhan.org/smallmillets/docs/report/Compendium_of_Released_Varieties_in_Small_millets.pdf
- No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP annual report, KrishiKosh thesis or DOI specific to Gavari was found. The Rajasthan-related papers and genome studies returned are about other varieties or foxtail millet generally and are discarded.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found. The search returned only Gavari-related variety listings. Seed sellers in the results were US, Canadian or general (for example seed-company pages for unnamed foxtail millet), so they are discarded. No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or Seednet availability was retrieved.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Rajasthan. -- https://eurekamag.com/research/003/149/003149108.php
- Rajasthan (listed among varieties). -- https://millets.res.in/technologies/2-Recommended_Package_of_Practices-Foxtail_Millet.pdf
- Rajasthan (listed among varieties). -- https://en.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cereals-and-millets/foxtail-millet?lgn=en
- The "Unknown" recommended_states_raw field in the record is therefore resolved to Rajasthan.

seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: MAINLY FOXTAIL MILLET IS CULTIVATED DURING KHARIF UNDER RAINFED CONDITION AND SOWN WITH THE ONSET OF MONSOON. AMONG THE VARIOUS CROPS, THE PRIORITY OF SOWING OF THIS IS WITH THE KHARIF PULSES. AS CATCH CROP IT COULD BE PLANTED DURING LAST WEEK OF MARCH TO FIRST WEEK OF APRIL. IN AGRONOMIC ZONE IV B COMPRISING BANSWARA, DUNGARPUR DISSTT., IT CAN BE ALSO SUCCESSFULLY GROWN IN RABI APPLYING ONE/TWO IRRIGATIONS. FERTILIZER RESPONSIVENESS : ALL THE VARIETIES VIZ SR 16 AND CHECKS SR 11  AND ARJUNA RESPONDED TO THE APPLICATION OF NITROZEN. APPLICATION OF 40 KG. N/HA SIGNIFICANTLY IMPROVED THE GRAIN YIELD OVER 20 KG.N. FURTHER INCREASE IN THE LEVEL OF N UPTO 60 KG DID NOT PROVE BENIFICIAL. THE TILLERING INCREASED WITH THE INCREASE IN LEVEL OF N APPLICATION. RESISTANT TO LODGING: THE VARIETY SR 16 DID NOT SHOW ANY LODGING SYMPTOM EVEN AT 60 KG. N/HA.
seednet_fields.Specific Morphological Characteristics: 1.MEERA IS A MEIDUM-TALL VARIETY HAS COMPACT PANICLE PIGMENTED WITH PURPLE VIOLET COLOUR AND BEARS LONG STIFF VIOLET AWNS. 2.LEAVES ARE BROAD, ERECT AND GLOSSY. ITS PLANT DEMONSTRATE STAY GREEN CHARACTER AT PHYSIOLOGICAL MATURITY.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: PLANT HEIGHT : 100 -110 CM.;SR 16 IS A MEDIUM TALL VARIETY WITH ERECT AND COMPACT PANICLES. THE MOST CHARACTERISTIC MORPHOLOGICAL FEATURE IS THAT ITS PANICLE IS PIGMENTED WITH PURPLE-VIOLET COLOUR AND BEARS LONG, STIFF, VIOLET AWNS(2+0.5 CM). LEAVES ARE BROAS, ERECT AND GLOSSY HAVING DISTINGUISHING DARK GREEN COLOUR. INTERMODES ARE THICK AND SHORT THEREBY PROVIDE ERECTNESS TO THE PLANT. ANOTHER PECULARITY OF THIS VARIETY IS THAT ITS PLANTS REMAIN ALMOST GREEN AT PHYSIOLOGICAL MATURITY DEMONSTRATING STAY GREEN CHARACTER, . SEED IS BOLD AND CREAMISH.

drought.details: Described as drought tolerant in the variety description (special attributes include easy threshability, synchronized maturity, non-lodging growth habit and drought tolerance) and in a variety table listing ATL-1 TNSi 331 (2020) as non-shattering, non-lodging and drought tolerant. The digest gives no quantitative drought data, mechanism or degree of tolerance; the level 'high' reflects the qualitative 'tolerant' classification only. Rainfed cultivation is reported for Aadi (June-August) and Puratasi (September-October) pattams in the ground-truth record.

heat.details: No evidence found. Searches returned only drought and non-lodging claims for this variety.

salinity.details: No evidence found. Searches returned only drought and non-lodging claims for this variety.

flood.details: No evidence found. Searches returned only drought and non-lodging claims for this variety.

disease_resistance.summary: Ground-truth variety record lists tolerance to blast. The searched sources contain no variety-specific disease evidence for ATL 1 (TNSi 331). The foxtail blast paper found studies the Magnaporthe grisea pathogen population and does not concern this variety, so it was not used. The shoot fly, grain smut and sheath blight entries in the table belong to ATL-1 (TNPsu 177) and were discarded. Blast tolerance therefore remains unverified by the digest.

pest_resistance.summary: Ground-truth variety record lists tolerance to shoot fly. No variety-specific pest evidence for ATL 1 (TNSi 331) was found in the searched sources. The shoot fly tolerance in the research table belongs to ATL-1 (TNPsu 177) and was discarded.

agronomic_details.yield: Under rainfed conditions, average grain yield was 2117 kg/ha and straw yield 2785 kg/ha, representing 9.6% (grain) and 14.8% (straw) increases over the check CO (Te) 7. Per plant grain yield was 20.8% higher than CO (Te) 7. Note: the ground-truth average_yield field (2785 kg/ha) matches the straw yield value in the digest, not the grain yield; this discrepancy is unresolved.
agronomic_details.stability: Multi-location or AICRP trial results: No evidence found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Rainfed conditions (digest). Ground-truth record lists rainfed cultivation during Aadi (June-August) and Puratasi (September-October) pattams. Suitable for both early and late sown conditions (ground-truth record).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Digest reports synchronous flowering and uniform maturity, non-lodging and non-shattering habit, and easy threshability. Quality: protein 12.3%, mineral matter 3.5%, calcium 34 mg/100 g and iron 5.7 mg/100 g, the highest among compared varieties including CO (Te) 7. Apical sterility is absent in ATL 1 and present in CO (Te) 7. Ground-truth record also lists strong culm, stay-green leaves, and positive response to nitrogenous fertilizers.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Rainfed trial: grain yield 2117 kg/ha and straw yield 2785 kg/ha, 9.6% (grain) and 14.8% (straw) above check CO (Te) 7. Per plant grain yield 20.8% above CO (Te) 7. Grain quality analysis: highest protein (12.3%), mineral matter (3.5%), calcium (34 mg/100 g) and iron (5.7 mg/100 g) versus CO (Te) 7 and other checks. Multi-location or AICRP trials: No evidence found.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: ATL 1 is differentiated from the popular variety CO (Te) 7 using SSR and RAPD markers (DNA fingerprinting study). No marker names, loci, or positions were reported in the digest.

Note: the ground-truth average_yield field (2785 kg/ha) matches the straw yield value in the digest, not the grain yield; this discrepancy is unresolved.

agronomic_performance.adaptation: Rainfed conditions (digest). Ground-truth record lists rainfed cultivation during Aadi (June-August) and Puratasi (September-October) pattams. Suitable for both early and late sown conditions (ground-truth record).
agronomic_performance.plant_characteristics: Digest reports synchronous flowering and uniform maturity, non-lodging and non-shattering habit, and easy threshability. Quality: protein 12.3%, mineral matter 3.5%, calcium 34 mg/100 g and iron 5.7 mg/100 g, the highest among compared varieties including CO (Te) 7. Apical sterility is absent in ATL 1 and present in CO (Te) 7. Ground-truth record also lists strong culm, stay-green leaves, and positive response to nitrogenous fertilizers.
agronomic_performance.field_trials: Rainfed trial: grain yield 2117 kg/ha and straw yield 2785 kg/ha, 9.6% (grain) and 14.8% (straw) above check CO (Te) 7. Per plant grain yield 20.8% above CO (Te) 7. Grain quality analysis: highest protein (12.3%), mineral matter (3.5%), calcium (34 mg/100 g) and iron (5.7 mg/100 g) versus CO (Te) 7 and other checks. search_metadata.evidence_digest:
ATL 1 (TNSi 331) -- EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name note: the input gives variety_name and seednet_variety_name as the same string, "ATL 1 (TNSi 331)". Most evidence below uses "ATL-1 (TNSi 331)" or "ATL 1". Several other TNAU releases are also named ATL 1 (kodo, ragi, samai, proso, kudiraivali). Those were discarded under the strict relevance rule. Searches used: 4 of 4 allowed.

STRESS TOLERANCE
It is endowed with special attributes like easy threshability, synchronized maturity, non-lodging growth habit and is drought tolerant. -- https://agris.fao.org/search/en/providers/122436/records/675acd490ce2cede71d18e69
Variety table listing: Non-shattering, non-lodging, drought tolerant (ATL-1 TNSi 331, 2020) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369241196_High_yielding_varieties_for_enhancing_the_production_of_small_millets_in_India
Heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found. Searches returned only drought and non-lodging claims for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
Disease and pest resistance for ATL 1 (TNSi 331): No evidence found. The foxtail blast paper (foxtail millet blast caused by Magnaporthe grisea is becoming a severe problem in foxtail millet growing regions of India) studies the pathogen population, not this variety. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC10624167/ (discarded as variety evidence)
The shoot fly, grain smut and sheath blight tolerance in the table belongs to ATL-1 (TNPsu 177), a different variety, so it was discarded. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369241196_High_yielding_varieties_for_enhancing_the_production_of_small_millets_in_India

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
It is a short duration culture and matures in 80-85 days. -- https://agris.fao.org/search/en/providers/122436/records/675acd490ce2cede71d18e69
Under rainfed condition, this culture has recorded an average grain yield of 2117 kg/ha and straw yield of 2785 kg/ha, which was 9.6 and 14.8 per cent increase in terms of grain and straw yield, respectively over the check variety, CO (Te) 7. -- https://agris.fao.org/search/en/providers/122436/records/675acd490ce2cede71d18e69
Per plant grain yield of ATL 1 accounted 20.8% increase over the check variety CO (Te) 7, and apical sterility is absent in ATL 1 and present in CO (Te) 7 variety. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/349009171_DNA_fingerprinting_of_foxtail_millet_Setaria_italica_L_variety_ATL_1_using_SSR_and_RAPD_markers_along_with_morphological_descriptors
Quality: ATL-1 had the highest protein, mineral matter, calcium, and iron content at 12.3%, 3.5%, 34 mg/100 g, and 5.7 mg/100 g, respectively, surpassing CO (Te) 7 and other check varieties. -- https://jabonline.in/abstract.php?article_id=1374&sts=2
Carotenoid check value (0.48 mg/100 g) in a germplasm study: -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/indian-journal-of-agricultural-research/A-6338
Multi-location or AICRP trial results for this variety: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage: The tenai (Vernacular name in tamil) culture ATL 1 is a cross derivative of PS 4 x (text truncated; the full cross is given as PS 4 x Ise 198 elsewhere). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/349009171_DNA_fingerprinting_of_foxtail_millet_Setaria_italica_L_variety_ATL_1_using_SSR_and_RAPD_markers_along_with_morphological_descriptors
It is a derivative of a cross between PS 4 x Ise 198. -- https://agris.fao.org/search/en/providers/122436/records/675acd490ce2cede71d18e69
Breeding-line code TNSi 331 and pedigree-selection method: the source line (PS 4 x ISE 198) is listed with the TNSI-331 code in a millet table. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/384662135_Food_System_for_Sustainability_and_Profitability_of_Millets
Marker fingerprinting: The newly released variety ATL 1 is differentiated from popular variety CO (Te) 7 using SSR and RAPD markers. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/349009171_DNA_fingerprinting_of_foxtail_millet_Setaria_italica_L_variety_ATL_1_using_SSR_and_RAPD_markers_along_with_morphological_descriptors
QTL or genome-wide mapping specific to this variety: No evidence found. The foxtail RIL QTL papers found do not name ATL 1 and were discarded.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: A high yielding drought tolerant fertilizer responsive non lodging tenai variety ATL 1 was developed at Centre for Excellence in Millets, TNAU, Athiyandhal. -- https://agris.fao.org/search/en/providers/122436/records/675acd490ce2cede71d18e69
Lead scientist named in the ATL 1 tenai paper: Nirmalakumari A. (with Subramanian A, Geethanjali S, Kanchanarani R). -- https://ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/800
Co-author on the fingerprinting study: Senthil Natesan (TNAU Biotechnology, Coimbatore), with Nirmalakumari A. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/349009171_DNA_fingerprinting_of_foxtail_millet_Setaria_italica_L_variety_ATL_1_using_SSR_and_RAPD_markers_along_with_morphological_descriptors
Breeder profile page: lists the ATL 1 tenai paper, but also kodo, ragi and samai ATL 1 items, so only the tenai paper is attributed. -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Angamuthu-Nirmalakumari

CONTACT DETAILS

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
The search budget ran out during my fourth call, so this digest is based on the four searches that completed. I could not retrieve the full text of the matching pages, so the findings below come from short search snippets only.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: JAWAHAR KODO-155 (RBK-155), Kodo millet (variety_name "Jawahar Kodo-155 (RBK-155)"; seednet_variety_name "JAWAHAR KODO-155 (RBK-155)"; variety code A0206004)

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The searches returned no page that describes drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. No page on disease or pest resistance for this variety appeared in the results.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
No evidence found. The one matching list entry gives no yield, maturity or trial data. The Vikaspedia list row for JK 155 (RBK 155) shows a selection from GPLMP 251, release year 2000, and figures in the 80-100 and 20-22 columns, but the snippet cut off before the column headings, so I cannot say what those figures measure. -- https://en.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cereals-and-millets/released-varieties-of-kodo-millet-in-india-for-cultivation?lgn=en

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage: "selection from germplasm no. GPLMP 251", as recorded in the Vikaspedia list row and in the variety record supplied with this request. -- https://en.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cereals-and-millets/released-varieties-of-kodo-millet-in-india-for-cultivation?lgn=en
Breeding method: selection, as the parentage entry states. No QTL, marker or genome studies were found. The ResearchGate result on Kodo millet is a general review and did not name this variety in the snippet.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution, as given in the variety record: All India Co-ordinated Research Project on Small Millets, College of Agriculture, Rewa (MP). The search results did not name any lead breeder or scientist for this variety. -- No breeder page found.

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found. No breeder name, email, phone, postal address or institute contact page for this variety was returned. The Rewa institution's contact details could not be verified from these searches.

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. No paper, AICRP report, thesis or KrishiKosh record naming this variety was returned. The ResearchGate review "Kodo Millet: Sowing Sustainability for a Flourishing Future" -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/383947677_Kodo_Millet_Sowing_Sustainability_for_a_Flourishing_Future is a general Kodo millet review. It was returned by the search, but I did not confirm that it discusses this variety, so I have not listed it as a publication for this variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. The seed-availability search returned only general Kodo millet pages and no NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing for this variety.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Variety record (as supplied, with repeated entries): Karnataka and Madhya Pradesh. The Vikaspedia list row begins "Karnataka a..." in the snippet, which partly matches this, but the snippet cut off before the full state list. -- https://en.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cereals-and-millets/released-varieties-of-kodo-millet-in-india-for-cultivation?lgn=en

RELEASE AND NOTIFICATION (supporting item, for the variety-name check)
The Bihar notified-variety list places "JAWAHAR KODO-155 (RBK-155)" under KODO MILLET (KODARA/VARAGU), with notification date 13/09/2000 and S.O. 821(E). This matches the seednet_variety_name, and the variety_name in the CSC minutes is the same string with different casing. The record gives the same name for both. -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf

Gaps to fill in a follow-up session: breeder names and contact details from the Rewa AICRP on Small Millets (JNKVV), trial and yield data, and seed sources through the MP and Karnataka agriculture departments, KVKs and the Seednet portal.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Jawahar Kodo-48 (DPS-48) / JK 48, Kodo millet (Paspalum scrobiculatum)

Name note: the CSC minutes name is "Jawahar Kodo-48 (DPS-48)" and the Seednet name is "JAWAHAR KODO-48 (DPS-48)". The Bihar notified-variety list uses the Seednet form. The Vikaspedia and MP-recommendation pages use the short form "JK 48". I treat "JK 48" as this variety only where the release year, pure-line origin, or MP recommendation fits; that link is an inference, not a stated identity.

STRESS TOLERANCE: Vikaspedia lists JK 48 as tolerant to drought and as non-lodging and non-shattering (name given as "JK 48", 2001 release). -- https://en.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cereals-and-millets/released-varieties-of-kodo-millet-in-india-for-cultivation?lgn=en
STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found for heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to this variety. Generic kodo-millet drought-hardiness statements (Wikipedia, FAO) name no variety, so they were discarded.

DISEASE AND PEST: Vikaspedia lists JK 48 as resistant to head smut. -- https://en.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cereals-and-millets/released-varieties-of-kodo-millet-in-india-for-cultivation?lgn=en
DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found for pest resistance (shoot fly or other) specific to JK 48. The head-smut tolerance attributed to GPUK 3 on the millets.res.in package-of-practices PDF is a different variety and was discarded. -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/3-Recommended_Package_of_Practices-Kodo_Millet.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: Vikaspedia gives JK 48 a maturity of about 95-100 days and a yield of about 26-27 q/ha. -- https://en.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cereals-and-millets/released-varieties-of-kodo-millet-in-india-for-cultivation?lgn=en
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: A kodo-millet variety comparison slide deck lists "Jawahar Kodo 48" with a 95-100 day maturity and a yield band, but its table columns are misaligned, so the values cannot be reliably assigned. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/kodo-millet-ppt-made-by-ghanshyam-bairwa-college-of-agriculture-kumher-bharatpur-pptx/267806541
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: The MP kodo-millet recommendations list "JK 48" among varieties recommended for Madhya Pradesh. Chhattisgarh's list names "Indira Kodo-48", a different variety, which was discarded. -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/3-Recommended_Package_of_Practices-Kodo_Millet.pdf
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: The package-of-practices PDF gives line sowing at 10 kg/ha seed rate and 15 kg/ha for broadcasting. It is crop-level, not specific to JK 48. -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/3-Recommended_Package_of_Practices-Kodo_Millet.pdf
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No multi-location or AICRP trial yield data specific to JK 48 was found.

GENETICS AND QTL: Vikaspedia records JK 48's breeding origin as pure-line selection. -- https://en.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cereals-and-millets/released-varieties-of-kodo-millet-in-india-for-cultivation?lgn=en
GENETICS AND QTL: The parentage given in the CSC record ("pure line selection from local germplasm No. 48") was supplied by the user and is not independently confirmed by any web page found. -- user-supplied record; no URL
GENETICS AND QTL: No evidence found for QTL, marker, genome or breeding-line code studies for JK 48. The biorxiv kodo-millet population study covers accessions generally and does not name this variety. -- https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/499087.full.pdf

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: The Bihar notification list places JAWAHAR KODO-48 (DPS-48) under kodo millet, notified 15/11/2001 (S.O. 1134(E)). -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: A 2018 study says JK 48 seed was obtained from the Regional Agricultural Research Station, AICRP on Small Millets, College of Agriculture, Rewa (M.P.). This links the variety to the AICRP small-millets programme at Rewa. -- https://www.chemijournal.com/archives/2018/vol6issue2/PartX/6-1-88-649.pdf

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Jawahar Kodo-41 (CSC name) / JAWAHAR KODO-41 (Seednet name), Kodo millet

Search note: Three searches returned content, and a fourth attempt timed out, so the seed-availability topic was not confirmed. Only one page (Vikaspedia) mentions this variety, and it lists it as "JK 41", not "Jawahar Kodo-41". I am treating JK 41 as a probable match on the basis of the year (1986) and the recommended states, not as confirmed. Neither name appears on any Seednet page in the results.

STRESS TOLERANCE:
- Vikaspedia's released-variety table (under "JK 41", 1986) describes the variety as resistant to head smut and moderately drought tolerant, with non-lodging and stay-green traits. Probable match, not confirmed as this variety. -- https://en.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cereals-and-millets/released-varieties-of-kodo-millet-in-india-for-cultivation?lgn=en

DISEASE AND PEST:
- Head smut resistance is listed for "JK 41" in the Vikaspedia table above. No separate pest-resistance evidence found. -- https://en.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cereals-and-millets/released-varieties-of-kodo-millet-in-india-for-cultivation?lgn=en

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS:
- Vikaspedia lists "JK 41" as a pure-line selection with a duration of about 105-110 days and a yield of about 20-22 q/ha (units as printed on the page). Probable match. -- https://en.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cereals-and-millets/released-varieties-of-kodo-millet-in-india-for-cultivation?lgn=en
- The same table lists the variety as suited to inter- or mixed cropping. -- https://en.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cereals-and-millets/released-varieties-of-kodo-millet-in-india-for-cultivation?lgn=en
- No multi-location trial data found for Jawahar Kodo-41 itself. -- No evidence found

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources):
- The CSC record gives parentage as a single-plant selection from germplasm collected at Maulapurwa village, Chhatarpur district, Madhya Pradesh. This comes from the task input, not from a search result. No independent source found. -- No evidence found
- Vikaspedia's "pure line selection" entry is consistent with the single-plant-selection parentage. -- https://en.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cereals-and-millets/released-varieties-of-kodo-millet-in-india-for-cultivation?lgn=en
- No QTL, marker, or genome-resource evidence found. -- No evidence found

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION:
- No breeder name found for this variety. The Vikaspedia page credits its compilation to the All India Coordinated Small Millets Improvement Project at GKVK, Bangalore. This is the project's compilation, not evidence of who bred this variety. -- https://en.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cereals-and-millets/released-varieties-of-kodo-millet-in-india-for-cultivation?lgn=en
- The CSC record names the AICRP on Minor Millets at the College of Agriculture, Rewa (M.P.) as the institution. The Rewa location was not confirmed by any search result. -- Task input only; No independent evidence found

CONTACT DETAILS:
- No breeder or institute contact (email, phone, address, or contact page) found. Searched. -- No evidence found
- The task input gives the institution as "College of Agriculture, Rewa-486004 (M.P.)". This is not verified by a search result. -- Task input only

PUBLICATIONS:
- No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report, or KrishiKosh thesis found that names Jawahar Kodo-41 or JK 41.
- The ResearchGate Kodo millet review mentions Jawahar Kodo-137 but not Jawahar Kodo-41; it is not attributed to this variety. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/383947677_Kodo_Millet_Sowing_Sustainability_for_a_Flourishing_Future

SEED AVAILABILITY:
- No evidence found. The seed-availability search (NSC, state seed corporations, KVKs, SAU sales, dealers) timed out and was not completed.

RECOMMENDED STATES:
- Vikaspedia's entry for "JK 41" lists the plains of Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, and South India. This matches the CSC record (Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh), but the Andhra Pradesh entry is not confirmed by this page. Probable match. -- https://en.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cereals-and-millets/released-varieties-of-kodo-millet-in-india-for-cultivation?lgn=en

The one general kodo millet review mentions breeding goals including head smut and shoot fly resistance, but does not attribute them to PSC-1 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/383947677_Kodo_Millet_Sowing_Sustainability_for_a_Flourishing_Future

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found for PSC-1 specifically. The same review names head smut and shoot fly as breeding targets in kodo millet generally, not for this variety -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/383947677_Kodo_Millet_Sowing_Sustainability_for_a_Flourishing_Future

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: Vikaspedia's list of released kodo millet varieties gives PSC 1 as a pure line selection from IPS 115, released 1986, with 100-105 days maturity, 18-20 (units as listed, likely q/ha), profuse tillering, and high yield -- https://en.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cereals-and-millets/released-varieties-of-kodo-millet-in-india-for-cultivation?lgn=en . No multi-location trial data was found.

GENETICS AND QTL: Parentage recorded as "single plant selection from IPS 115" (Vikaspedia row above, consistent with the input record). No breeding-line code, QTL or marker study for PSC-1 was found. The genome-wide population structure paper on kodo, little and proso millet does not name PSC-1 -- https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/499087.full.pdf (not attributed to this variety).

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: No evidence found for a named lead breeder or scientist. The institution in the input record is the All India Coordinated Millets Improvement Project (Coordinating Unit, College of Agriculture, Pune). search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Jawahar Kodo-76 (kodo millet)

Searches run: 4 (variety and release; breeder and institute; research papers and trials; seed availability). The CSC release name is "Jawahar Kodo-76" and the Seednet name is "JAWAHAR KODO-76". Seednet itself did not appear in any search result. Where pages use the abbreviation "JK 76", I treated it as this variety, and I say so below. Pages that named other kodo varieties (JK 13, JK 41, Jawahar Kodo-137, Jawahar Kodo-1/2/41, Jawahar Kodo-439, GPUK 3, CO 3) were discarded.

STRESS TOLERANCE (name matched: Jawahar Kodo-76 / JK 76)
Described as tolerant to drought and moderately tolerant to shootfly, with non-lodging habit -- https://vikaspedia.in/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cereals-and-millets/released-varieties-of-kodo-millet-in-india-for-cultivation
Same entry repeated on the English Vikaspedia page -- https://en.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cereals-and-millets/released-varieties-of-kodo-millet-in-india-for-cultivation?lgn=en
No flood, submergence, heat or salinity data found for this variety. The generic "hardy, drought-resistant crop" statements in the search results are about kodo millet in general, so I did not record them.

DISEASE AND PEST (name matched: JK 76)
Moderately tolerant to shootfly, per the Vikaspedia released-varieties table -- https://vikaspedia.in/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cereals-and-millets/released-varieties-of-kodo-millet-in-india-for-cultivation
Head smut resistance appears in the same table, but it is listed against JK 13 (a mutant of JK 76), not JK 76 itself. Not recorded for this variety -- https://en.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cereals-and-millets/released-varieties-of-kodo-millet-in-india-for-cultivation?lgn=en
No pathogen or disease screening data specific to JK 76 found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS (name matched: JK 76)
Maturity 85-90 days; yield 18-22 q/ha; early duration and high yielding, per the Vikaspedia table (the yield column is labelled q/ha) -- https://vikaspedia.in/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cereals-and-millets/released-varieties-of-kodo-millet-in-india-for-cultivation
No multi-location trial data, AICRP yield trial report, or field-trial results naming JK 76 were found. The Nature 2024 nutrient-management trial (Bangalore) does not name this variety, so it was discarded -- https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-024-83265-y (discarded)

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage: pure-line selection from local germplasm collected at Sidhi (Madhya Pradesh) -- https://vikaspedia.in/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cereals-and-millets/released-varieties-of-kodo-millet-in-india-for-cultivation
Breeding method: pure-line selection; the same table lists JK 13 as a mutant derived from JK 76 -- https://vikaspedia.in/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cereals-and-millets/released-varieties-of-kodo-millet-in-india-for-cultivation
Mutagenesis: JK 76 was reported to be more susceptible to gamma radiation than JK 41; a protogynous mutant with two spikelet rows was recovered from JK 76 after 5 kR gamma treatment; mutants with late maturity and auricle pigmentation were also reported -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/383947677_Kodo_Millet_Sowing_Sustainability_for_a_Flourishing_Future (also summarised at https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/agricultural-and-biological-sciences/paspalum-scrobiculatum)
Breeding-line codes beyond JK 76: none found.
QTL, marker or genome studies naming JK 76: No evidence found. The bioRxiv population-structure study covers ICRISAT kodo accessions in general, not this variety -- https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/499087.full.pdf (discarded for this record)

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION (name matched: JAWAHAR KODO-76 on the notified list; JK 76 in Vikaspedia)
Notification entry: JAWAHAR KODO-76, dated 16/08/1991, notification number 527(E) -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf
The CSC minutes name the institution as the All India Coordinated Research Project on Small Millets, College of Agriculture, Rewa (M.P.). The source and sentence describing the variety's own developing station are not in the retrieved text.
Breeder name: No evidence found. The Vikaspedia page names two authors (Deepika Cheruku, ICAR-IIMR; Gayathri Bandaru, ICAR-NRRI) but these are authors of the web article, not breeders of this variety, so they are not attributed to it -- https://en.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cereals-and-millets/released-varieties-of-kodo-millet-in-india-for-cultivation?lgn=en
The AICRP on Small Millets page lists 14 centres and five kodo varieties released up to 2012, but does not name JK 76 -- https://www.millets.res.in/aicrp_small.php (crop-level context only)
A ResearchGate review mentions kodo varieties developed at the Rewa centre in 1993 using material from Bangalore. The variety is not named, so it was discarded -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/383947677_Kodo_Millet_Sowing_Sustainability_for_a_Flourishing_Future (discarded)

CONTACT DETAILS
Breeder or scientist contact for this variety: No evidence found.
Institute-level contact (not the Rewa station): ICAR-Indian Institute of Millets Research, Rajendranagar, Hyderabad 500 030, as listed on the AICSIP breeder-seed document. Website per Wikipedia: millets.res.in -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip19/Sorghum/presentations19/07Seed-ProjectsAGM2020.pdf and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Institute_of_Millets_Research
Rewa centre contact (College of Agriculture, Rewa, M.P. / AICRP-Small Millets centre): No evidence found. No phone or email was retrieved.
Email and phone numbers for other IIMR scientists appeared on an unrelated project page (https://www.indiascienceandtechnology.gov.in/research/genetic-enhancement-grain-yield-and-contributing-traits-kodo-millet-paspalum-scrobiculatum-l). They were not recorded because they do not relate to this variety.

PUBLICATIONS (format: Authors (Year). Title. Journal/Report -- URL/DOI)
Compendium on released varieties of small millets, AICSMIP, Project Coordinating Unit, GKVK Bangalore. Year not shown in retrieved text. Released varieties listing, as cited by Vikaspedia -- https://vikaspedia.in/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cereals-and-millets/released-varieties-of-kodo-millet-in-india-for-cultivation
Authors not shown (Year not shown). Kodo Millet: Sowing Sustainability for a Flourishing Future. ResearchGate review (cites Yadava 1997a on gamma mutants of JK 76) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/383947677_Kodo_Millet_Sowing_Sustainability_for_a_Flourishing_Future
Yadava (1997a). Gamma-irradiation mutants of kodo millet, as cited in the review above. Original journal not retrieved; not verified -- no DOI or URL found
No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP annual report, KrishiKosh thesis or conference paper naming JK 76 was found. KrishiKosh was not returned by any search.

SEED AVAILABILITY (name matched: none)
No evidence found for Jawahar Kodo-76 or JK 76 from NSC, a State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or dealers. The searches returned only unbranded kodo seed listings (Kanha Trading Company, Jabalpur, "Kodo desi" -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/kodo-seed-22803334273.html; Sujima Grains Tec, Sivakasi -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/kodo-millets-seeds-9938787097.html). These do not name the variety, so they were discarded. A Madhya Pradesh contingency plan lists kodo varieties Jawahar Kodo-1, 2 and 41, not JK 76, and was discarded -- https://www.icar-crida.res.in/CP/madhya%

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Jawahar Kodo 439 (variety_name and seednet_variety_name both "Jawarhar/Jawahar Kodo 439"; SeedNet page not found, so no SeedNet evidence was retrieved; alias JK 439 / JK439 / JK-439 / जवाहर कोदो-439 used in sources). Crop: Kodo millet. Searches run: 4.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to JK 439. Related generic statement only: the variety is described as suited to shallow soil with marginal fertility, especially hilltop soils -- https://en.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cereals-and-millets/released-varieties-of-kodo-millet-in-india-for-cultivation?lgn=en
Kisan India describes JK-439 as suited to hill areas -- https://www.kisanindia.in/agriculture/millet-farming-kodo-crops-give-good-production-even-in-less-rainwater-know-what-are-the-top-quality-varieties-33458.html

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Vikaspedia lists JK 439 with maturity of 100-110 days and yield of 22-23 q/ha (release year given as 2004, not 2002) -- https://en.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cereals-and-millets/released-varieties-of-kodo-millet-in-india-for-cultivation?lgn=en
Kisan India gives 100-110 days to maturity -- https://www.kisanindia.in/agriculture/millet-farming-kodo-crops-give-good-production-even-in-less-rainwater-know-what-are-the-top-quality-varieties-33458.html
An ICAR-IIMR recommended package of practices lists JK 439 among Kodo varieties for Madhya Pradesh -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/3-Recommended_Package_of_Practices-Kodo_Millet.pdf
A JNKVV-linked extension report describes an improved-practices project on JK439 (with JK155, JK137, RK390-25) and foundation/certified seed hubs at JNKVV centres (Rewa and ZARS) -- https://bepls.com/beplsmay2019/20.pdf
A Kodo cultivation review lists JK 439 among varieties -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/377968033_Scientific_cultivation_practices_of_Kodo_millet

GENETICS AND QTL -- Vikaspedia records the breeding origin as pure line selection; the stated parentage "selection from germplasm RPS-123" was not found in any source (the RPS-123 label is unverified). No gene, QTL, marker, breeding-line code (beyond RPS-123 from the input record), or genome-resource evidence found -- https://en.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cereals-and-millets/released-varieties-of-kodo-millet-in-india-for-cultivation?lgn=en

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No named lead breeder or scientist found for JK 439. The input record gives JNKVV Jabalpur as institution; no retrieved page confirms this for JK 439 (JNKVV is linked to other Kodo varieties such as Jawahar Kodo 48 and JK 13 in a slideshare table, and to JK-41 in Kisan India, which are different varieties) -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/kodo-millet-ppt-made-by-ghanshyam-bairwa-college-of-agriculture-kumher-bharatpur-pptx/267806541 ; https://www.kisanindia.in/agriculture/millet-farming-kodo-crops-give-good-production-even-in-less-rainwater-know-what-are-the-top-quality-varieties-33458.html

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder contact, no institute email, phone, postal address or contact page URL was retrieved for JK 439. Searches did not reach seednet.gov.in, JNKVV or KrishiKosh pages.

PUBLICATIONS -- No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report entry, thesis or conference paper naming JK 439 was retrieved. Items naming JK 439 only in lists or extension material:
Anonymous (year not stated). Released varieties of Kodo millet in India for cultivation (compendium data, 1977-2012, from AICSMIP). Vikaspedia -- https://en.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cereals-and-millets/released-varieties-of-kodo-millet-in-india-for-cultivation?lgn=en
Authors not stated (year not stated). Recommended package of practices for Kodo millet. ICAR-IIMR -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/3-Recommended_Package_of_Practices-Kodo_Millet.pdf
Authors not stated (2019). Improved kodo millet production project report (BEPLS, May 2019). Bulletin of Environment, Pharmacology and Life Sciences -- https://bepls.com/beplsmay2019/20.pdf

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No variety-specific seed source found (no NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing for JK 439). The BEPLS report mentions foundation/certified seed hubs at JNKVV centres for improved Kodo varieties generally -- https://bepls.com/beplsmay2019/20.pdf
The nyspiceshop.com result is an unrelated US retail listing for "Kodo Millet (Bajra)" and was discarded.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh -- https://en.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cereals-and-millets/released-varieties-of-kodo-millet-in-india-for-cultivation?lgn=en ; https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/3-Recommended_Package_of_Practices-Kodo_Millet.pdf ; https://www.kisanindia.in/agriculture/millet-farming-kodo-crops-give-good-production-even-in-less-rainwater-know-what-are-the-top-quality-varieties-33458.html

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found. The only disease claims retrieved (MSV, gray leaf spot, rust resistance) belong to the Seed Co "SC 510" hybrid marketed in Nigeria, not to SSM-510 (https://htsfarms.ng/product/seed-co-sc-510-maize-seed-2kg/). They are discarded.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found. Retrieved agronomy text concerned Seed Co SC 510 (seeding rates and maturity), KS-510 white maize, and Kern 510 F1 spring maize. None concerns SSM-510 from India.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources): No evidence found. The parentage KML 321 / KML 372 / KML 33 / KML 99 was not found on any retrieved page. Pioneer and other US hybrid patent pages were returned and discarded.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: No evidence found. Retrieved people and institutions (Baldev Singh Dhillon, Jianming Yu at Iowa State, CIMMYT and IITA maize programmes, Zimbabwe's Crop Breeding Institute) are not linked to SSM-510 and are discarded as name-resemblance matches. No breeder name is attributed to this variety.

CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found. No breeder, institute or company contact for SSM-510 or Kanchan Ganga Seed Company was retrieved.

PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found. Retrieved papers (for example, the KS-510 white maize study and the Zimbabwe and CGIAR maize breeding papers) do not concern SSM-510. No DOI or URL is attributed to this variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found. Listings for "SC 510" and "SC 510 Early Maturity" (Seed Co, Nigeria) were returned. They are a different hybrid from a different company and are discarded. No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing for SSM-510 was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES: No evidence found. The input field says "Unknown", and no retrieved page gives a notified or recommended state for SSM-510.

Suggested next step: check the seednet.gov.in entry for code A0207002 directly, and search the CSC release minutes (1994) and the KrishiKosh/AICRP maize reports for "SSM-510" or "SSM 510" with the Kanchan Ganga company name.
