The Bihar list and ResearchGate table refer to DHM-109 by that name; the IIMR page and PJTAU report use "DHM-109" or "DHM 109".

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to DHM-109. The ResearchGate table has a "Tolerance to MLB & BSDM" entry sitting next to DHM 109, but the layout makes it unclear whether it belongs to DHM 109 or the neighbouring entry, so I have not attributed it. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010

DISEASE AND PEST -- Same caveat as above. The Scribd list of Indian maize cultivars includes a row for EH-40097 (Hyderabad, 1994) with a tolerance list (TLB, MLB, SDM and others), but that row is not clearly aligned with DHM-109 in the extracted text, so I have not used it as evidence. -- https://www.scribd.com/document/451634301/Maize-cultivars-1969-2017-pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found for DHM-109 trial or agronomy data. The ResearchGate table gives an average yield of 40 q/ha and extra-early maturity for an entry adjacent to DHM 109, but attribution is uncertain. The input's claim of 8.0 t/ha potential is not corroborated by any retrieved source. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) -- Parentage is not independently verified. The three-way cross (CM 119 x CM 211) x CM 133 appears only in the task input. The IIMR page classes DHM 109 as a three-way cross hybrid, which is consistent with that input but does not confirm the parental lines. No QTL, marker or genome-resource studies were found. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/hyderabad-telangana/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- The IIMR (ICAR-Indian Institute of Maize Research) Hyderabad (Telangana) page lists DHM 109 among cultivars and calls it the first kharif early three-way cross hybrid, released in 1993. No breeder names were found. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/hyderabad-telangana/
The PJTAU Maize Research Station, Rajendranagar report also names DHM 109 as an early-maturity hybrid released in 1993. That station is a separate institution, so this is supporting context rather than confirmation of the developing station. -- https://www.pjtau.edu.in/pdf1/16.pdf
The task input names the developing station as the Maize Breeder, Agricultural Research Station, Amberpet, Hyderabad. This is not confirmed by any retrieved page. The ResearchGate table lists the centre as ANGRAU, Hyderabad, for the DHM-series hybrids. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder name, email, phone or postal address for DHM-109 was retrieved. The only institute page found is the IIMR Hyderabad page, which I could not verify for contact details. Its URL is https://iimr.icar.gov.in/hyderabad-telangana/ and it is offered only as an institute-level reference, not a verified contact.

PUBLICATIONS -- No DHM-109-specific paper, thesis, AICRP report or conference paper was found. The items below cover the release list and are not research studies:
Anonymous (2015). List of Notified Varieties, Year of Release and Notification Date. Department of Agriculture, Government of Bihar -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf
Anonymous. Maize Hybrid and Composite Varieties Released in India (1961-2010). ResearchGate compilation -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010
Anonymous. Maize Varieties Released in India (1969-2017). Scribd compilation -- https://www.scribd.com/document/451634301/Maize-cultivars-1969-2017-pdf

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found for current seed sales from NSC, State Seed Corporations, KVKs, SAUs or private dealers. The PJTAU report notes seed-production MoUs for other hybrids (DHM 117, DHM 121) but not for DHM-109. A slideshare deck lists DHM-109 only as a hybrid example for CMS-based seed production, which does not establish availability. -- https://www.pjtau.edu.in/pdf1/16.pdf

RECOMMENDED STATES -- The input says "Unknown". The Bihar notification record gives the release entry (notification 636(E), dated 02/09/1994) but no adaptation states. The ResearchGate table's adaptation text for the DHM 109 entry is ambiguous. It may read "Bihar, Jharkhand, Orissa & WB", but this is probably the neighbouring entry's row, so the states are not confirmed. -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010

Release year: the Bihar notification list gives 02/09/1994 (notification 636(E)). The IIMR and PJTAU pages say 1993. Both are cited above; the discrepancy is unresolved.

Searches run: 4 (variety/notification; breeder/institute; research papers; seed availability). The Seednet portal itself was not returned by any search.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: DHM-105 (EH-40184), Maize

Names searched: "DHM-105 (EH-40184)" (CSC release-minute name and Seednet name, which are identical here). The sources use "DHM 105" without the EH-40184 code. I treated "DHM 105" as the same variety because it is the same designation, but no source mentions EH-40184, so none of the findings below can be tied to that code. Four searches were run.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Nothing reliable for this variety. The IIMR table lists "tolerant to TLB, charcoal rot and late wilt" for one column, but the columns are misaligned and cannot be matched to DHM 105 with confidence. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/hyderabad-telangana/

DISEASE AND PEST
- The same IIMR table mentions TLB and charcoal rot tolerance, with the same alignment caveat. No DHM 105-specific pest or disease evidence found. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/hyderabad-telangana/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- No evidence found. The IIMR yield row cannot be aligned to DHM 105 (values 1.5-2.0, 6.5, 6.6, 5.5-6.0, 7.5 t/ha). No trial data for DHM 105 was returned. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/hyderabad-telangana/

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- The parentage in the record, (CM 119 x CM 120) x (CI 21 (E) x X 108), was not confirmed by any search result. No breeding-line codes, QTL or genome-resource evidence found. The pedigree (CM 104 x CM 105) x (CM 202 x CM 201) in the ResearchGate compendium belongs to "Deccan" and was discarded. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010
- The DH 105 doubled-haploid line in the Martonvásár study is a different line and was discarded. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/250006771_Strategy_for_improvement_of_doubled_haploid_production_in_maize

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The release is credited in the sources to the Maize Research Station, Rajendranagar (PJTAU), which lists DHM 105 (1990) among five double-cross hybrids it released. This conflicts with the record's institution, the Agriculture Research Station, Amberpet, Hyderabad. No breeder name was found for DHM 105. -- https://www.pjtau.edu.in/pdf1/16.pdf
- The PJTAU breeder-seed page names Dr. D. Bhadru, Dr. N. Sunil and Dr. M. V. Nagesh Kumar, but it concerns DHM 206, DHM 182, DHM 211, DHM 213, DHM 218 and BML 101. These names are not attributed to DHM 105. -- https://pjtau.edu.in/dr-m-v-nagesh-kumar-director-seeds-pjtau-visited-breeder-seed-production-fields/
- Release year: 1990 (IIMR and PJTAU both agree). Nature of the variety: double-cross hybrid. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/hyderabad-telangana/ ; https://www.pjtau.edu.in/pdf1/16.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
- No evidence found. No breeder, institute email, phone or postal address for DHM 105 was returned. The PJTAU and IIMR pages were retrieved, but their snippets contain no contact details. Checking the institute contact pages directly is needed.

PUBLICATIONS
- No evidence found for a paper, AICRP report, thesis or conference paper that names DHM 105.
- Possible lead, not verified: Directorate of Maize Research (ICAR), "Maize Hybrid and Composite Varieties Released in India (1961-2010)", 3rd ed. The snippet did not show a DHM 105 entry, so it is not listed as a publication for this variety. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found for DHM 105. Results covered DHM 117 and DHM 121 (PJTAU MoUs with private seed companies) and other hybrids. These were not attributed to DHM 105. -- https://www.pjtau.edu.in/pdf1/16.pdf

RECOMMENDED STATES
- No reliable evidence found. The record says "Unknown". The IIMR area-of-adaptation row lists Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Maharashtra, but it cannot be aligned to DHM 105 with confidence. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/hyderabad-telangana/

Discarded: "Deccan 105" in the ICAR compendium snippet (a different name, and the entry could not be matched to DHM-105); USPTO patent pages for other maize varieties; and the Iowa State, Nature and PMC pages, which are not about this variety.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
VARIETY: Madhuri (Sweet Corn). Searched names: "Madhuri (Sweet Corn)" (CSC minutes name) and "MADHURI (SWEET CORN)" (Seednet name). No Seednet portal page was returned by any search, so all evidence below refers to the name "Madhuri" as it appears in the release tables and papers.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for this variety. Searches returned no stress-tolerance data (drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence) for Madhuri. A Seednet-style product page for a different sweet corn hybrid lists flood tolerance, but it names Madhavi, not Madhuri -- discarded.

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found for Madhuri specifically. A Phule Madhu hybrid trial paper lists Madhuri as a check with resistance scores, but the paper is about Phule Madhu (QMHSC-1182), so it is not attributed here -- https://jart.co.in/uploads/168/14487_pdf.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Nitrogen and plant population effects on super sweet corn 'Madhuri' at Maize Research Station, Amberpet: higher N increased primes, green ear and kernel yield -- https://www.indianjournals.com/article/ija-46-2-010
Plant population and fertility (NPK) trial with 'Madhuri' sown 2002 and 2003, green fodder yield 37.49-41.56 t/ha at highest fertility -- https://pub.isa-india.in/index.php/ija/article/download/4932/4607
Front line demonstrations with sweet corn variety Madhuri on farmers' fields (Khalingi village), higher green cob yield than local and hybrid checks, with Table 1 productivity and Table 2 economics -- https://www.ijcmas.com/7-11-2018/Kabita%20Mishra%20and%20Debasis%20Sarangi.pdf
Release-table entry for Madhuri (1990): maturity early, yield 30-40 q/ha, adaptation Andhra Pradesh throughout the year -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010
Phule Madhu trial comparing green cob yield against Madhuri as check (Madhuri is a comparator, not the subject) -- https://jart.co.in/uploads/168/14487_pdf.pdf
Other pages: Madhur (Known-You F1 hybrid), Madhavi (Seminis), Sanas Madhur and similar names -- discarded as different products.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage: release table gives pedigree "Florida Sweet Corn" -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010 (the fuller parentage string, including the simple recurrent selection, E.V. B-21 cross and backcrossing, comes from the variety record supplied, not from a search result)
Breeding method: no search result confirmed a method beyond the supplied record (simple recurrent selection, then backcrossing).
Genotype class: Najeeb et al. list Madhuri in a table as super sweet in taste (sugar-gene class) -- https://mnl.maizegdb.org/85/PDF/11najeeb.pdf
Breeding-line codes, QTL and marker studies: No evidence found for Madhuri.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing centre: ANGRAU (Acharya N.G. Ranga Agricultural University), Hyderabad, per release table -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010
Station: Maize Research Station, Amberpet, Hyderabad 500013 (affiliation on 2001 paper) -- https://www.indianjournals.com/article/ija-46-2-010

One aggregator site calls Madhuri "developed by ICAR" with no breeder or institute detail -- https://cornindia.com/blog/how-to-grow-sweet-corn-in-india-a-step-by-step-guide/ (conflicts with the ANGRAU attribution; not adopted)

EVIDENCE DIGEST: JH-3459 (Maize)

Note: Three web searches returned no pages about JH-3459 maize. A fourth search (seed availability) hit the tool-call limit and returned no usable results. The search tool does not identify any page as naming this variety, so every heading below is either "No evidence found" or a supplied-record note, not a web finding.

Name check: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "JH-3459", so no separate Seednet search was needed. No page confirmed either name.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. Search returned only a USPTO patent for maize line JH6530 (https://image-ppubs.uspto.gov/dirsearch-public/print/downloadPdf/9282700), a different variety, discarded.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. Same search; the JH6530 patent is a different variety, discarded.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. No trial or agronomy page named JH-3459.

GENETICS AND QTL -- No web evidence found. The parentage below comes from the supplied record, not from a web source: I 105 X SE 533; I 105 : (JS2 X J3022) HS 43-2-1-1-1-2-#-FS2-#-#-FS1-###; SE 533 (TARUN X MS1)-Y63-1G-2-1-1-3-1-2-1-2-1-1-FS-BULK-###.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No web evidence found. The supplied record lists the institution as the Senior Maize Breeder, Department of Plant Breeding, Punjab Agricultural University, Ludhiana-141004. No search confirmed the breeder's name or this institution's link to the variety. A search for "JH-3459 Maize breeder institute" returned a Bulgarian Maize Research Institute page (https://ic-kneja.com/site/index.html?language=en-US), a different institute, discarded.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. The Knezha (Bulgaria) contact details (+359 9132 7163, info@ic-kneja.com) belong to a different institute and are discarded.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. The search "JH-3459 Maize research" returned a Springer article on mycorrhizal infection and phosphorus efficiency in maize cultivars (https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s40011-012-0114-1). I saw only the abstract snippet and could not confirm it names JH-3459, so I have not listed it. Authors, year and journal are not in the snippet.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- Not searched. The fourth search hit the tool-call limit and returned no results. Suggested sources to check directly: seednet.gov.in (variety code A0207144), PAU Department of Plant Breeding, and Punjab/Haryana/Delhi/UP state seed corporations.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Supplied record only, not web-verified: Delhi, Haryana, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh.

Maturity, yield, release notification details, and the CSC release minutes entry: No evidence found. The variety's year of release, 2001, also comes only from the supplied record.

salinity.details: A study of the F1 hybrid Pusa Early Hybrid Makka 3 (PEHM 3), which the digest treats as the same variety under an alias, and its parental lines CM 213 and CM 142 under salt stress reported that the hybrid had higher membrane stability and chlorophyll content and lower superoxide and Na+ than its parents. search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pusa Early Hybrid Makka-3 (AH-58), Maize

Name check: the CSC name "Pusa Early Hybrid Makka-3 (AH-58)" and the Seednet name "PUSA EARLY HYBRID MAKKA-3 (AH-58)" differ only in case. The sources use the alias "Maize Hybrid AH-58 (PEHM-3)", which I treated as the same variety. Some sources also say "PEHM 3". Evidence for both names is listed together below.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Salinity: a study of the F1 hybrid "Pusa Early Hybrid Makka 3 (PEHM 3)" and its parents CM 213 and CM 142 reports that the hybrid had higher membrane stability and chlorophyll content and lower superoxide and Na+ than its parents under salt stress -- http://www.ueb.cas.cz/en/content/differential-response-maize-hybrid-and-its-parental-lines-salinity-stress-0
- High temperature: the AICMIP hybrid list has a truncated entry for this hybrid that appears to mention tolerance to high temperature, but the text is garbled and I could not confirm it -- https://aicmip.naarm.org.in/Documents/Hybrids%20of%20maize%20released-1.pdf
- Drought, flood, submergence: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found. The search returned no disease or pest resistance data for this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- The AICMIP list gives the hybrid as early maturity, grown in kharif, with yellow flint grain and a yield of 4.0-5.5 (units not stated in the snippet) -- https://aicmip.naarm.org.in/Documents/Hybrids%20of%20maize%20released-1.pdf
- A ResearchGate summary of released maize hybrids lists the hybrid as early maturing, yellow flint, with an average yield of 55 q/ha -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010
- No multi-location trial results specific to this variety were found.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage conflict: the ResearchGate summary gives the pedigree as CM 213 x CM 142, and the PPV&FR compendium also lists CM 213 x CM 142 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010 ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290899665_A_Compendium_of_maize_hybrids_and_composites_of_India_under_PPV_FRA_Technical_Bulletin_No_20104_pp_84
- The parentage in the record (IPA34-62-f-1-1-1-1 x IPA3-20-f-1-1-1) is not supported by these sources and needs checking against the official record.
- The salinity study's F1 and parent lines (CM 213 tolerant, CM 142 sensitive) are the same lines named in the pedigree above -- http://www.ueb.cas.cz/en/content/differential-response-maize-hybrid-and-its-parental-lines-salinity-stress-0
- QTL, markers, and genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The ResearchGate summary lists the centre as IARI, Delhi, for this hybrid -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010
- The PPV&FR compendium also lists the institution as IARI, Delhi -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290899665_A_Compendium_of_maize_hybrids_and_composites_of_India_under_PPV_FRA_Technical_Bulletin_No_20104_pp_84
- Lead breeder names: No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Breeder or scientist names, emails, phones, postal addresses, and institute contact pages for this variety: No evidence found. The breeder search returned an ICAR institute profile PDF, but it does not mention this variety, so I have not used it.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not captured (2010). A Compendium of Maize Hybrids and Composites of India under PPV & FRA. Technical Bulletin No. 2010/4 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290899665_A_Compendium_of_maize_hybrids_and_composites_of_India_under_PPV_FRA_Technical_Bulletin_No_20104_pp_84
- Authors not captured (year not captured). Maize Hybrid and Composite Varieties Released in India (1961-2010). ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010
- Authors not captured (year not captured). Differential Response of a Maize Hybrid and its Parental Lines to Salinity Stress. Journal not captured -- http://www.ueb.cas.cz/en/content/differential-response-maize-hybrid-and-its-parental-lines-salinity-stress-0
- Authors not captured (year not captured). Hybrids of maize released from 2000 (AICMIP list). -- https://aicmip.naarm.org.in/Documents/Hybrids%20of%20maize%20released-1.pdf
- No KrishiKosh theses, AICRP reports, or DOI-bearing papers specific to this variety were found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found. The seed search returned only unrelated retail listings (e.g., a squash seed and a wheat seed product) and general maize seed shops that do not name this variety. I have not used them.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- The AICMIP list recommends this hybrid for kharif in Punjab, Haryana, and Delhi -- https://aicmip.naarm.org.in/Documents/Hybrids%20of%20maize%20released-1.pdf
- The Bihar notified-variety list confirms notification on 02/02/2001 (Gazette 92(E)) but gives no state list -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf
- The states in the recommended_states_raw field (Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu) are not supported by any source I found and should be checked against the CSC minutes.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Priya Sweetcorn (Maize)

Name note: I searched both "Priya Sweetcorn" (CSC release name) and "PRIYA SWEETCORN" (Seednet name, with "MAIZE (MAKKA)"). None of the results named either form, so the findings below apply to neither name.

Searches run (4 queries, one per topic plus a seed-availability query):
1. "Priya Sweetcorn Maize variety"
2. "PRIYA SWEETCORN MAIZE (MAKKA) breeder developed by Amberpet"
3. "Priya Sweetcorn maize research paper"
4. "Priya Sweetcorn maize seed availability"

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. Searches returned general sweet corn production and unrelated sweet corn pages, none naming this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found. No page named this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found. The closest result was a general sweet corn production guide, which does not mention Priya Sweetcorn.

GENETICS AND QTL: No evidence found in search results. The parentage (simple selection from advanced generations of crosses involving Madhuri, Malaysian Sweetcorn, Thai Sweetcorn and Madhumakka) and the variety code A0207156 come only from the input record supplied with this request. They were not verified by any search result.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: No evidence found. The breeder and station ("Maize Breeder, Agricultural Research Station, Amberpet, Hyderabad") are taken from the input record only. No search result confirmed them.

CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found. No breeder, institute, email, phone, address, or contact page was returned for this variety.

PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found. The research search returned a ResearchGate listing of maize hybrid and composite varieties released in India (1961–2010) and an unrelated sweet corn paper ('Sweet Pearl F1' with vermicompost). Neither names Priya Sweetcorn in the text returned, so neither is recorded here.

SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found. The seed search returned only US retail seed listings (Burpee), which concern unrelated products.

RECOMMENDED STATES: No evidence found. The states in the input record (Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu) are unverified. The search returned no release notification or CSC minutes.

Suggested next steps: check the Seednet portal (seednet.gov.in) directly for variety code A0207156, and the ICAR/AICRP maize reports and the Agricultural Research Station, Amberpet (Professor Jayashankar Telangana State Agricultural University) for release records. The search tool did not reach these sources.

disease_resistance.summary: Tolerance claims from two sources: (1) JK Agri maize catalogue (seed-company page, not a trial report) lists tolerance to MLB (maydis leaf blight), TLB (turcicum leaf blight), BLSB and stalk rot. (2) ICAR table of maize genotypes with biotic-stress tolerance lists tolerance to MLB, BSDM and PFSR, using the source's abbreviations. The CSC record lists tolerance to Sorghum Downy Mildew, Turcicum Leaf Blight, Maydis Leaf Blight and Post Flowering Stalk Rot. BSDM is read as Sorghum Downy Mildew and PFSR as Post Flowering Stalk Rot consistent with the CSC record. BLSB appears only in the company catalogue and is not in the CSC record. The digest notes the catalogue claims are not backed by trial data.

pest_resistance.summary: The CSC record lists moderate tolerance to stem borer. The evidence digest found no insect-pest resistance data for this variety from the searched sources, so the CSC claim is not independently confirmed.

agronomic_details.yield: Ground truth (CSC and task input): 6000.00 to 6500.00 Kg/Ha (60-65 qtl/ha under normal conditions). AICMIP table lists yield 6.0-6.5 (units not stated in the digest). IIMR register lists yield value 6.3 (units not stated in the snippet).
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. The CSC record lists tolerance to lodging and high N responsiveness, but the digest does not confirm these, and no multi-environment trial data was found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for Kharif season in Andhra Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu and Uttarakhand (CSC record and IIMR register). The AICMIP table also lists J&K and the NEH region. A Sikkim maize review reports adoption in Sikkim, which is an adoption claim and not a trial result. A trade listing says it suits medium, light and heavy soils. A state package of practices lists it among short-duration maize hybrids for Rabi sowing in Andhra Pradesh. The digest describes the hybrid as suited to rainfed and irrigated systems (AICMIP).
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 88 To 101Days (CSC record). A trade listing gives 90-95 days, which is a dealer page and not a trial record.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Company page describes the hybrid as a fodder maize with good palatability, digestibility better than average fodder maize, and long broad dark-green leaves. AICMIP lists orange flint grain. The CSC record lists morphological characteristics as Unknown. These are company and dealer descriptions, not trial measurements.
agronomic_details.field_trials: No multi-location or replicated trial report for this variety was found in the digest. Results found: (1) IIMR register yield value 6.3 (units not stated). (2) AICMIP table yield 6.0-6.5 with early maturity and orange flint grain. (3) Trade listing: 90-95 days to maturity (dealer page, not a trial). (4) State package of practices (Andhra Pradesh): listed among short-duration maize hybrids under 90 days for Rabi sowing. (5) Sikkim maize review: reports adoption in Sikkim (adoption claim, not a trial result). (6) A pot trial in a Verma et al. (2018) paper uses JKMH-1701 with a Enterobacter cloacae strain; this is a microbiology study and not a variety performance trial.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
JKMH-1701 Maize: Evidence Digest

Name check: the CSC release name (variety_name) and the Seednet name (seednet_variety_name) are both "JKMH-1701". The searches did not reach seednet.gov.in, so no Seednet-specific record was found. Results also used the spellings "JKMH 1701" and "JKMH1701", and one paper called the hybrid "JK Surabhi gold JKMH-1701". I treated these as the same variety only where the page names it with this crop.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- The JK Agri maize catalogue lists the hybrid as tolerant to MLB, TLB, BLSB and stalk rot. -- https://jkagri.com/product-category/field-crops/maize/
- An ICAR table of maize genotypes with biotic-stress tolerance lists JKMH 1701 as tolerant to MLB, BSDM and PFSR, using the source's abbreviations. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/cs_0.pdf
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance data for this variety was found. Note that the MLB/TLB/BLSB/stalk rot claims come from a seed-company page, not a trial report.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Disease tolerance claims are listed under STRESS TOLERANCE above (the ICAR table and the JK Agri catalogue). No insect-pest resistance data was found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity is listed as early, with a yield of 6.0-6.5 and orange flint grain, suited to rainfed and irrigated systems. -- https://aicmip.naarm.org.in/Documents/Hybrids%20of%20maize%20released-1.pdf

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: D-994 (Maize, Seednet: MAIZE (MAKKA), code A0207224)

Search budget: the four web_search calls were all run in one batch, which exhausted the tool's usage limit. A follow-up check of the result text for "D-994" failed for that reason, so I could only review the first ~300 characters of each result. Any D-994 mention further down a page was not checked.

Name check: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "D-994", so no name conflict arose. All evidence below refers to the same name.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. The variety search (query "D-994 Maize variety") returned an ICAR-AICMIP list of maize hybrids released from 2000 (aicmip.naarm.org.in/Documents/Hybrids%20of%20maize%20released-1.pdf). Its visible rows covered other hybrids (e.g., Birsa Vikas Makka-2, Shalimar KG Maize-1), which were discarded. The D-994 row, if present, was not visible in the snippet. Please check that PDF directly.

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found. Same search and source as above; no D-994 text was visible.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found. The variety search returned no D-994 trial data in the visible text.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources): No evidence found. The research search returned MaizeGDB (ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC2518694/), a general maize genome database paper unrelated to D-994, so it was discarded. The parentage recorded in the variety file (advance generations of crosses among nine lines from Population 31 and one line from Suwan-1) was not verified by any web source.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: No evidence found. The breeder search returned an unrelated Bulgarian Maize Research Institute, Knezha (ic-kneja.com), which was discarded. The institution named in the variety file, the Department of Genetics & Plant Breeding, College of Agriculture, G.B. Pant University of Agriculture & Technology, Pantnagar, was not confirmed by any search result.

CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found. The only contact details returned belonged to the Bulgarian institute above, which is not related to this variety, so none are recorded. The institution address in the variety file (Pantnagar-263 145, Uttarakhand) is unverified. Please check the GBPUAT website and the Department of Genetics & Plant Breeding contact page.

PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found. The research search returned no paper, thesis or report naming D-994. Results were general maize papers (MaizeGDB, ScienceDirect review at sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2666154325009949), discarded as not about this variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found. The seed search returned only a general maize seed-quality review (ScienceDirect link above), which does not name D-994. No Seednet, NSC, state seed corporation, KVK or dealer listing was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES: No evidence found on the web. The states in the variety file (Assam, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal) come from the supplied record and were not verified by any search result.

Next steps (outside this tool budget):
1. Open the ICAR-AICMIP hybrid list PDF and search for "D-994" to confirm the release row, maturity and recommended zones.
2. Check seednet.gov.in for code A0207224.
3. Check the GBPUAT Pantnagar Maize breeding page and KrishiKosh for D-994 papers or reports.

drought.details: The CSC record describes PRC-3 as moderately resistant to drought and suitable for early and late sowing. The 2010 participatory study (Shanthakumar et al.) included PRC 3 among five little millet varieties assessed for harsh environments and resource-poor farmers, and discussed its drought-related traits, but the original-language detail is not confirmed for PRC 3 specifically. A compendium entry that appears to list PRC 3 says it can withstand water stress and suits early monsoon conditions; its table layout is garbled and the mapping is unverified. No quantitative drought data or mechanisms specific to PRC-3 were found. The level is based on the CSC record, with the search sources offering only partial, unverified support.

heat.details: No heat-stress evidence was found for PRC-3. The CSC record lists stress_reaction as Unknown.

salinity.details: No salinity-tolerance evidence was found for PRC-3.

flood.details: No flood or waterlogging evidence was found for PRC-3. The IIMR little millet brochure notes that little millet tolerates waterlogging in general but does not name PRC-3, so it cannot be attributed to this variety.

disease_resistance.summary: The CSC record states that disease reaction was not noticed (no disease problems recorded). A compendium entry that appears to list PRC 3 describes it as moderately resistant to neck and finger blast, but the layout is garbled and the mapping to PRC 3 is uncertain. No other disease evidence naming PRC-3 was found; general little millet blast sources do not name the variety.

pest_resistance.summary: The CSC record states that PRC-3 is moderately resistant to shoot fly. A compendium entry that appears to list PRC 3 describes it as tolerant to stem borer, but the mapping is uncertain. General shoot fly sources do not name PRC-3.

agronomic_details.yield: Participatory trial: 8.18 q/ha average. The CSC record lists average yield as Unknown. A compendium entry of uncertain mapping lists 25-26 q/ha average grain yield, which is not confirmed for PRC-3.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No AICRP multi-location trial data for PRC-3 was found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: The CSC record recommends release for cultivation in Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Bihar, Maharashtra and Karnataka, and for notification for the entire country. The record describes suitability for early and late sowing and lodging resistance. Search evidence does not confirm these state recommendations.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Per the CSC record: lodging-resistant; suitable for early and late sowing. A compendium entry of uncertain mapping describes the variety as non-shattering, non-lodging and responsive to fertilizer, and gives maturity of 120-125 days, which conflicts with the CSC maturity range and is not confirmed for PRC-3. Morphological characteristics are recorded as Unknown.
agronomic_details.field_trials: One farmer-participatory evaluation (Shanthakumar et al., 2010) recorded PRC 3 at an average of 8.18 q/ha, in the same range as OLM 20 (8.32 q/ha) and CO 2 (7.58 q/ha). No trial design, locations or replication details are given in the snippet. No AICRP multi-location trial data for PRC-3 was found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: PRC-3 (little millet, Panicum sumatrense)

Name note: the CSC name and the Seednet name are both "PRC-3". The search sources write it as "PRC 3" or "PRC-3". All findings below refer to that name. Four searches were run, and the evidence is thin: most results were about other little millet varieties, other millets, or commercial products.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Per the 2010 participatory study, PRC 3 was one of five little millet varieties assessed for harsh environments and resource-poor farmers, and its drought-related traits were discussed. Original-language detail is not confirmed for PRC 3 specifically. -- http://www.nuscommunity.org/uploads/tx_news/Shanthakumar_et_al.pdf
- A compendium entry that appears to list PRC 3 says it "can withstand water stress" and is suited to early monsoon conditions. The table layout is garbled and the entry may be mis-associated, so treat as unverified. -- https://www.dhan.org/smallmillets/docs/report/Compendium_of_Released_Varieties_in_Small_millets.pdf
- No other stress-tolerance evidence (heat, salinity, flood, submergence) was found for PRC-3. The IIMR little millet extension folder notes that little millet tolerates drought and waterlogging in general, but does not name PRC-3. -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/brochures/Little_Millet_Brochure.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- The compendium entry that appears to list PRC 3 describes it as moderately resistant to neck and finger blast and tolerant to stem borer. Layout is garbled and the mapping to PRC 3 is uncertain. -- https://www.dhan.org/smallmillets/docs/report/Compendium_of_Released_Varieties_in_Small_millets.pdf
- No other disease or pest evidence naming PRC-3 was found. Sources on little millet shoot fly and blast are general and do not name PRC-3. -- https://www.millets.res.in/aicrp_small.php

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Participatory trial: PRC 3 recorded an average of 8.18 q/ha, in the same range as OLM 20 (8.32 q/ha) and CO 2 (7.58 q/ha). This was a farmer-participatory evaluation; no trial design or locations are given in the snippet. -- http://www.nuscommunity.org/uploads/tx_news/Shanthakumar_et_al.pdf

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Kolab (OLM-36) / KOLAB (OLM-36), little millet (Panicum sumatrense)

Name check: The CSC name "Kolab (OLM-36)" and the Seednet name "KOLAB (OLM-36)" refer to the same variety. Sources write it as "OLM 36 (Kolab)", "OLM-36 (Kolab)" or "Kolab (OLM 36)". Every finding below refers to this variety. Several findings conflict with each other, and I flag those conflicts inline. The searches were: (1) variety and traits, (2) breeder and institution, (3) research papers, (4) seed. Searches 1 and 2 returned no breeder name or contact page for this variety.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Kolab is described as resistant to brown spot, sheath blight, and long duration with high yield, in a mutation-breeding review; the entry is listed in the mutant-variety table. OLM 36 2001 Resistant to brown spot, sheath blight, long duration, high yield (Kolab) -- https://oar.icrisat.org/13521/1/Cereal%20Research%20Communications_53_2047-2061_2025.pdf
- A separate Odisha extension table lists Kolab as resistance to brown smut, released 2001. This conflicts with the brown spot listing above. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/376981287_Little_millet_A_climate_resilient_crop_for_sustainable_millet_production_in_Odisha
- A compendium of small-millet releases gives a stress profile for OLM 36 (Kolab): moderately resistant to neck and finger blast and tolerant to stem borer, non-shattering and non-lodging, suited to early monsoon, and able to withstand water stress. Attribution is uncertain because the table layout in this PDF is scrambled. -- https://www.dhan.org/smallmillets/docs/report/Compendium_of_Released_Varieties_in_Small_millets.pdf
- Drought or waterlogging tolerance specific to Kolab: No evidence found. General little-millet drought statements were excluded because they do not name this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Brown spot / sheath blight resistance: see Stress Tolerance above (Cereal Research Communications review, 2025; ICRISAT repository).
- Brown smut resistance: see Stress Tolerance above (Odisha extension table, ResearchGate).
- Blast resistance and stem borer tolerance: see the compendium entry under Stress Tolerance (dhan.org PDF, attribution uncertain).
- Shootfly, rust, grain smut: No evidence found for Kolab specifically. These traits are listed for other varieties in the same tables.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity and yield (Odisha recommendation table): OLM-36 (Kolab), 95-100 days, 10-11 q/ha, resistance to brown smut, released 2001 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/376981287_Little_millet_A_climate_resilient_crop_for_sustainable_millet_production_in_Odisha
- Maturity and yield from the compendium: 120-125 days and 25-26 q/ha. This conflicts with the Odisha table and is flagged as uncertain. -- https://www.dhan.org/smallmillets/docs/report/Compendium_of_Released_Varieties_in_Small_millets.pdf
- Plant height and growth habit (DUS test guidelines): the table places OLM 36 in the semi-dwarf height class, 80–120 cm. -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/final-little-millet.pdf
- ICAR AICRP small-millet material lists Kolab (OLM 36) among recommended little-millet varieties. The document context is about technology packages, not a field-trial result for this variety. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/Circulars/AICRPsCropScience.pdf
- Multi-location trial results for Kolab: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage (Odisha and national tables): Kolab is a mutant of SS 81-1, developed at OUAT, Odisha, released 2001. -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/little_millet.pdf

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
VARIETY: Jawahar Kutki-36 (CSC name) / Jawahar Kutki-36 (Seednet name). Both names are identical, so the evidence below refers to the same name under both. Search results also used "JK 36", "JK-36" and "LMJK-36". No search returned the Seednet portal page or code A0208094.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Only variety-specific item: the ICAR-IIMR salient-features table lists JK 36 as tolerant to shoot fly -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/little_millet.pdf
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence evidence names JK 36. The only tolerance statements in the results (drought and waterlogging tolerance) describe little millet as a crop, so they are discarded. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/375186262_Production_Technology_of_Minor_Millets

DISEASE AND PEST
- JK 36 is listed as tolerant to shoot fly in the ICAR-IIMR table (see above). -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/little_millet.pdf
- No disease resistance evidence names JK 36. Rust and grain smut appear only as crop-level disease notes. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/375186262_Production_Technology_of_Minor_Millets ; https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/brochures/Little_Millet_Brochure.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- JK 36 is listed with a 75-80 day maturity and 10-12 q/ha average yield in the ICAR-IIMR table. -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/little_millet.pdf
- Breeder seed indent data show JK 36 (released 2009) was the main contributor to little millet seed indents in most years, at 8.3-100.0% of the indent. -- https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/94d6/2200bf2dc92fd6df62002b8cdea8c632ba8f.pdf
- Physical grain properties (geometric mean diameter, sphericity, thousand-grain weight, bulk and true density, porosity) were measured for LMJK-36 at three moisture contents. This is a post-harvest study, not a field trial. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/394285504_Influence_of_moisture_content_on_physical_properties_of_little_Millet_LMJK-36
- No multi-location trial results for JK 36 were found. -- No evidence found beyond the table above.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage: the ICAR-IIMR table records JK 36 as a selection from local material. This matches the supplied "selection from local germplasm no. 36", but no page gives the source accession number. -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/little_millet.pdf
- Breeding method: pure-line or selection origin is recorded for JK 36 in the same table. No breeding-line code was found. -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/little_millet.pdf
- Genome resources: no JK 36-specific marker, QTL, or genome study was found. The general little millet genomics pages (population structure, a transcriptome database, and the SMUASB crossing method) do not name JK 36, so they are discarded. -- https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/499087.full.pdf ; https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC10575755/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: AICRP on Small Millets centre at Rewa, JNKVV (Jawahar Lal Nehru Krishi Vishwa Vidyalaya), Madhya Pradesh. -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/little_millet.pdf
- Breeder name(s): No evidence found. No page names a lead breeder or scientist for JK 36.
- The Springer small-millets chapter and the Jawahar Kodo 137 entry are about other crops or varieties and are not attributed to JK 36. -- https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-981-16-9257-4_8

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder contact or Rewa/JNKVV station contact was found. No evidence found.
- Coordinating institute (ICAR-Indian Institute of Millets Research, not the developing station): Rajendranagar, Hyderabad, Telangana 500 030; website www.millets.res.in. Institute-level only; no email or phone found. -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/brochures/Little_Millet_Brochure.pdf

PUBLICATIONS
- ICAR (Krishi repository) (year not shown in the snippet). Breeding varieties and seed production chain of minor millets (title truncated in the snippet; seed-indent analysis of little millet). Journal/Report: not shown. -- https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/94d6/2200bf2dc92fd6df62002b8cdea8c632ba8f.pdf
- Author(s) not shown (ResearchGate record). Influence of moisture content on physical properties of little millet (LMJK-36). Journal not shown; year not shown. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/394285504_Influence_of_moisture_content_on_physical_properties_of_little_Millet_LMJK-36
- No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP annual report entry, or peer-reviewed paper specifically on JK 36 was found. No DOI was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- JK 36 is a major contributor to breeder-seed indents for little millet, per the ICAR seed-chain analysis. This indicates demand, not current retail supply. -- https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/94d6/2200bf2dc92fd6df62002b8cdea8c632ba8f.pdf

RECOMMENDED STATES

- Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh: ICAR-IIMR state-wise list includes JK 36 under both. -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/brochures/Little_Millet_Brochure.pdf

drought.details: Digest reports drought tolerance for the line at field level, linked to strong culms and semi-compact panicles. The release proposal describes the line as drought tolerant and suited to dryland, hilly and tribal areas. A review table also lists it as drought tolerant. No primary quantitative drought-screening data for this variety was found, so the level is rated medium rather than high.

heat.details: A 2025 TNAU growth-chamber study used seed described as ATL 1 from CEM Athiyandal and reported little millet germination of 84% at 35 C. The paper's species wording is ambiguous, so this is indicative only and no heat-tolerance rating is supported.

disease_resistance.summary: Tolerant to grain smut and sheath blight under sick plot conditions (variety reaction data). A review table lists the line as tolerant to grain smut and sheath blight. No primary field-screening data on these resistances was found for this variety. No evidence found for blast or other pathogen scores specific to TNPsu 177.

pest_resistance.summary: Tolerant to shoot fly. Variety reaction data states there is no incidence of storage pests. The review table lists the line as tolerant to shoot fly. No primary field-screening data was found for this variety.

agronomic_details.yield: Ground-truth data: grain 1587 kg/ha, straw 3109 kg/ha. Station trial: 1859 kg grain and 3633 kg straw/ha. Multi-location: 1343 kg grain and 2616 kg straw/ha. Large-scale demonstration: 2223 kg grain and 4106 kg straw/ha. Station average of 1966 kg/ha for TNPsu 177 with a 21.60% increase (TNPsu 176 averaged 1859 kg/ha with a 15.00% increase). Yield advantage over checks CO(Samai) 4 and Paiyur 2: 11.2% and 13.7% for grain, and 11.8% to 14.4% for straw.
agronomic_details.stability: Multi-location yield (1343 kg grain/ha) was lower than station yield (1859 kg/ha) and large-scale demonstration yield (2223 kg/ha). Stability across environments is not otherwise quantified in the digest.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Highly suitable for Eastern Ghats districts Dharmapuri, Tiruvannamalai, Vellore, Salem and Krishnagiri. Very much adaptive in the plains under rainfed systems. Suitable for both early and late sown conditions; if early sown, a second crop of horsegram or niger can be sown in the sequence.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Plant height 103.78 cm compared with 91.8 cm for CO 4. Short duration. Synchronous flowering and uniform maturity. Non-lodging and non-shattering. Strong culm and stay-green leaves. Long, semi-compact panicles. Positive response to nitrogenous fertilizer. Suitable for mechanical harvesting. Seed rate: 10 kg/ha for line sowing, 12.5 kg/ha for broadcasting. Nutrient-rich grains with high milling recovery; palatable and nutritious straw. Morphological descriptor data is not available in the digest.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Station trials: TNPsu 177 averaged 1966 kg/ha, a 21.60% increase over the check, and was promoted for MLT testing. Proposal summary: station 1859 kg grain and 3633 kg straw/ha; multi-location 1343 and 2616 kg/ha; large-scale demonstration 2223 and 4106 kg/ha. Advantage over checks CO(Samai) 4 and Paiyur 2 was 11.2% and 13.7% for grain and 11.8% to 14.4% for straw. AICRP 2022-23 used ATL 1 as a check at CEM Athiyandal. Trial data for disease and pest screening was not found.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: DNA fingerprinting with cereal SSR markers across five little millet genotypes including ATL 1. Maize-derived SSR markers phi213984 and phi295450 were polymorphic. Marker phi213984 gave a unique 310 bp amplicon in ATL 1 compared with 300 bp in the other genotypes. Chromosome positions were not stated.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: TNPsu 177 (ATL 1), Little millet (Samai)

Name check: The variety_name and seednet_variety_name fields are identical ("TNPsu 177 (ATL 1)"), so no name conflict arose. The sources use "Samai TNPsu 177" for the pre-release line and "ATL 1" after release. Several pages named "ATL 1" concern other crops (kodo TNPsc 176, ragi TNEc 1285, proso TNPm230, kodo TNSi 331, foxtail/tenai PS 4 x ISE 198) and were discarded. Searches used: 4 of 4 allowed.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Drought tolerance is reported for the line, with strong culms and semi-compact panicles. Samai line TNPsu 177 has strong and sturdy culm with long, semi-compact panicles and drought tolerance. -- https://doi.org/10.5958/0975-928X.2019.00173.X
- The release proposal describes the line as drought tolerant and suited to dryland, hilly and tribal areas. It is drought tolerant. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/VarietyRelease2019Booklet.pdf
- Heat response: a 2025 TNAU growth-chamber study used seed described as ATL 1 from CEM Athiyandal and reported little millet germination of 84% at 35°C. The paper's species wording is ambiguous, so treat as indicative. -- https://masujournal.org/112/MAJ-2025-1228_1759994232.pdf
- No evidence found for flood, submergence, or salinity tolerance for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
- A review table lists the line as tolerant to drought, shoot fly, grain smut and sheath blight. ATL-1 (TNPsu 177) 2019 85-90 - Tamil Nadu Early maturity, bold grains with high bulk density, tolerant to drought, shoot fly, grain smut and sheath blight. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369241196_High_yielding_varieties_for_enhancing_the_production_of_small_millets_in_India
- No primary field-screening data on these resistances was found for this variety. No evidence found for blast or other pathogen scores specific to TNPsu 177.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity: Little millet entries TNPsu 176 and TNPsu 177 ( 80 days). -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/hrd/pdf/Millet%20program.pdf. The 2019 paper gives 85-90 days under rainfed conditions. -- https://doi.org/10.5958/0975-928X.2019.00173.X
- Station yield: In little millet, the entries TNPsu 176 and TNPsu 177 registered an average yield of 1859 and 1966 kg/ha with an increase of 15.00 and 21.60 per cent, respectively under station trials and promoted for testing under MLT. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/hrd/pdf/Millet%20program.pdf
- Proposal trial summary: station 1859 kg grain and 3633 kg straw/ha; multi-location 1343 and 2616 kg/ha; large-scale demonstration 2223 and 4106 kg/ha. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/VarietyRelease2019Booklet.pdf
- Advantage over checks: It has yield advantage of 11.2 and13.7 percent for grain yield while 11.8–14.4 percent for straw yield over the check varieties viz., CO(Samai) 4 and Paiyur 2. -- https://indianjournals.com/article/ejpb-10-4-001
- Other traits: Drought tolerant and suitable for mechanical harvesting, Nutrient rich grains with high milling recovery. Palatable and nutritious straw. -- https://www.covaipost.com/coimbatore/tnau-releases-new-crop-varieties-for-pongal/
- Plant architecture: the line is short in duration with plant height of 103.78 cm, versus 91.8 cm for CO 4. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/hrd/pdf/Millet%20program.pdf
- AICRP 2022-23: ATL 1 was used as a check in little millet trials at CEM Athiyandal (the identity of this check as the Samai ATL 1 is inferred from the name). -- https://www.millets.res.in/aicsip22/Small_Millets/reports22/1-Breeding.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage: It is a derivative of CO(Samai) 4 x TNAU 141. -- https://doi.org/10.5958/0975-928X.2019.00173.X. The pedigree-selection method named in the request is not stated in the retrieved sources; they say only "derivative" or "cross derivative".
- Breeding-line code: TNPsu 177 (the release name is ATL 1). Also cited in the proposal as a cross derivative of CO(Samai) 4 x TNAU 141 and evolved by Centre of Excellence in Millets, Athiyandal. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/VarietyRelease2019Booklet.pdf
- Marker fingerprinting: DNA fingerprinting used cereal SSR markers across five little millet genotypes including ATL 1. Markers phi213984 and phi295450 from maize SSR were polymorphic, with phi213984 yielding a unique 310bp amplicon in ATL 1 compared to 300bp in others. -- https://www.academia.edu/74632437/Characterization_of_Little_millet_Panicum_sumatrense_varieties_using_Morphological_descriptors_and_SSR_based_DNA_fingerprinting
- Germplasm context: Researchers can obtain seed samples of little millet accessions from the ICRISAT genebank (http://genebank.icrisat.org/) following a standard material transfer agreement. -- https://acsess.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/csc2.20527
- No QTL, gene, or trait-marker study specific to TNPsu 177 was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Lead author and breeder: Angamuthu Nirmalakumari is the first author on the release paper, with co-authors A. Subramanian, A. Thanga Hemavathy, R. Kanchanarani, P. Parasuraman, M. Jayachandran, R. Ravikesavan, M. Rajesh, K. Sivagamy and K. Ananthi. -- https://doi.org/10.5958/0975-928X.2019.00173.X
- Developing institution: A high yielding and early maturing Samai TNPsu 177 was developed at the Centre of Excellence In Millets, Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Athiyandal and released as ATL 1. -- https://doi.org/10.5958/0

drought.details: A 2006 news report states RHB-121 has medium drought tolerance. The RARI and RACP pages describe RHB hybrids, including RHB 121, as suited to arid and semi-arid Rajasthan, which is consistent with the original variety data's 'tolerant to drought' statement. No physiological mechanism (for example root traits, osmotic adjustment or drought escape beyond the 75-78 day maturity) was found in the digest. The rainfed low-fertility adaptation in the original data is noted but is not drought-specific trial evidence.

heat.details: No evidence found for heat tolerance specific to RHB-121 in the searched sources.

salinity.details: No evidence found for salinity tolerance specific to RHB-121. The Jamnagar/AICPMIP table entries for other hybrids were not attributable to RHB-121.

flood.details: No evidence found for flood tolerance specific to RHB-121 in the searched sources.

disease_resistance.summary: Downy mildew (DM): resistance is stated for the RHB hybrid group, with RHB 121 named among hybrids resistant to downy mildew in the Rajasthan value-chain report and the RARI page. The Compendium of Registered Varieties lists RHB-121 (MH-892) under Pearl Millet, but the snippet does not show the disease entry, so it is not independent confirmation. The original variety data states 'resistant to DM and other diseases'; resistance to other diseases was not found in the digest. Sources: RARI Durgapura scheme page and RACP value-chain report (downy mildew); Compendium of Registered Varieties (listing only).

pest_resistance.summary: Insect pests: no pest-specific evidence for RHB-121 was found in the digest; the original variety data's claim of negligible insect damage is not independently verified. Bird damage: the Rajasthan value-chain report and RARI page describe RHB hybrids (including RHB 121) as having bristled ear heads for bird protection; the original data states bird damage is minimized by bristles.

agronomic_details.yield: The original variety data gives an average yield of 2500.00 to 2700.00 Kg/Ha (not verified by the digest). The AICPMIP Annual Report 2015 lists a yield row for RHB 121 (Check) of 2964, with units not stated in the snippet. These figures are not directly comparable without the units and trial context.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources beyond the 2011 workshop statement that RHB 121 performed better than other entries in zone A1.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for rainfed low-fertility conditions in Rajasthan, Gujarat, Haryana, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Delhi (original data). The RACP and RARI sources describe RHB hybrids as suited to arid and semi-arid Rajasthan. The original data also records that the variety is recommended for notification for the entire country.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: - MEDIUM TAIL WITH 3-4 TILLERS.;- HEAD CYLINDRICAL TAPERING TOWARDS TIP, BRISTLED.;- THE COLOUR OF BRISTLES IS PINK AT FLOWERING (DETAILED CHARACTERS ARE GIVEN ALONGWITH CHARACTERS OF MALE AND FEMALE)
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) AICPMIP Annual Report 2015: RHB 121 was a check in Zone A trials at 18 locations, with a yield row of 2964 (units not stated). (2) 46th Annual Pearl Millet Workshop proceedings (2011): RHB 121 performed better than other entries in zone A1 and is listed as a zone A recommendation; no quantitative data given. (3) The 2006 news report and the RACP value-chain report contain general bajra figures (medium duration; farmers sow 2-2.5 kg/acre against the recommended 1.5 kg). These are not RHB-121 trial data.

genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Not found in searched sources. A hybrid-breeding review mentions RHB 121, but no QTL, marker or genome study was found for RHB-121.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: RHB-121 (MH-892), Pearl millet (Pennisetum glaucum)

Name check: the CSC name and the Seednet name are both "RHB-121 (MH-892)", so the evidence below applies to both. Most sources write it as "RHB 121" (the hybrid). I found no source that names RHB-121 as a composite or open-pollinated variety.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- A 2006 news report says RHB-121 ripens in about 75-78 days and has medium drought tolerance. -- https://www.oneindia.com/2006/06/19/six-improved-varieties-of-bajra-in-rajasthan-1150715201.html
- Rajasthan's value-chain report lists RHB 121 among hybrids resistant to downy mildew, with bristled ear heads for bird protection, suited to arid and semi-arid Rajasthan. -- https://www.raridurgapura.org/Scheme-Millet.htm ; https://www.tourism.rajasthan.gov.in/content/dam/agriculture/Rajasthan%20Agricultural%20Competitiveness%20Project/valuechainreport/RACP_VC_Bajra.pdf
- No evidence found for salinity, flood, submergence or heat tolerance specific to RHB-121. The Jamnagar/AICPMIP table entries for other hybrids mention lodging tolerance, but I found none for RHB-121 specifically.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Downy mildew resistance is stated for the RHB hybrid group (including RHB-121) in the RARI and RACP pages above. No pest-specific evidence for RHB-121 was found. The Compendium of Registered Varieties lists RHB-121 (MH-892) under Pearl Millet, but the snippet does not show the disease entry. -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/compendiumfinal27oct2018.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- AICPMIP Annual Report 2015 lists RHB 121 as a check in Zone A trials at 18 locations, with a yield row for RHB 121 (Check) of 2964 (units not stated in the snippet). -- https://www.aicpmip.res.in/ar2015.pdf
- The 46th Annual Pearl Millet Workshop proceedings say RHB 121 performed better than other entries in zone A1, and list it as a zone A recommendation. -- https://www.aicpmip.res.in/pw2011.pdf
- The 2006 news report says RHB-121 is medium-duration, and the value-chain report says farmers commonly sow 2-2.5 kg/acre against the recommended 1.5 kg. These are general bajra figures, not RHB-121 trial data. -- https://www.tourism.rajasthan.gov.in/content/dam/agriculture/Rajasthan%20Agricultural%20Competitiveness%20Project/valuechainreport/RACP_VC_Bajra.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage is recorded as ICMA 89111 x RIB 3135-18 (the female is listed as ICMA 89111, which the task gives as MS-89111A; the "MS" vs "ICMA" prefix is a discrepancy to check). Method: single cross hybrid, cytoplasmic male sterility (CMS) system. -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf ; http://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf
- Mentioned in a hybrid-breeding review, but no QTL, marker or genome study was found for RHB-121. -- https://researchgate.net/publication/283573439_Hybrid_breeding_in_pearl_millet_past_and_present_status

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Notified as "RHB 121", AICPMIP, ARS Durgapura, Jaipur, S.O. 1134(E) dated 15.11.2001, under Rajasthan Agricultural University (now SKNAU). -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf ; https://www.sknau.ac.in/uploads/media/dor.pdf
- Lead breeder: no source names the breeder of RHB-121. The 2011 workshop proceedings list ARS Durgapura millet breeders (Dr. Shrikant; Dr. Yogendra Singh; Dr. L.D. Sharma) as attendees, which is not evidence that they bred RHB-121. -- https://www.aicpmip.res.in/pw2011.pdf
- Developing centre: ICAR AICRP on Pearl Millet, Durgapura (Jaipur), under SKNAU's Rajasthan Agricultural Research Institute (RARI). -- https://www.sknau.ac.in/uploads/media/dor.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
- Dr. S. K. Jain, In-charge, AICPMIP, RARI Durgapura: mobile 8824958070; email milletdurgapura@rediffmail.com. This is institute-level (AICPMIP project) and not a breeder contact for RHB-121. -- https://www.raridurgapura.org/Scheme-Millet.htm
- Postal address of RARI/ARS Durgapura: No evidence found in the snippets. RARI is described as a constituent of SKNAU, Jobner, but no street address was returned.
- SKNAU Directorate of Research (Jobner) contact details: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- AICPMIP (2015). Annual Report (RHB 121 in zone A trials). -- https://www.aicpmip.res.in/ar2015.pdf
- AICPMIP (2011). Proceedings of the 46th Annual Pearl Millet Workshop (RHB 121 zone-trial results). -- https://www.aicpmip.res.in/pw2011.pdf
- Singh, S. and others (2014). Hybrid breeding in pearl millet: past and present status. ResearchGate (review listing RHB 121). -- https://researchgate.net/publication/283573439_Hybrid_breeding_in_pearl_millet_past_and_present_status
- No peer-reviewed paper, KrishiKosh thesis or DOI devoted to RHB-121 was found in the searches.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Rajasthan State Seeds Corporation's Kharif 2023 availability list shows bajra varieties Raj-171, HHB-67(I), Dhanshakti and PC-701, but not RHB-121. -- http://rajseeds.org/AvailabilityOfSeeds.html
- Private players (Pioneer, JK, Proagro) control bajra seed supply in Rajasthan, but the report does not name RHB-121 as sold by them. -- https://www.tourism.rajasthan.gov.in/content/dam/agriculture/Rajasthan%20Agricultural%20Competitiveness%20Project/valuechainreport/RACP_VC_Bajra.pdf
- No current seed dealer, KVK or SAU seed-sale listing for RHB-121 was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Adaptation recorded for RHB 121: Rajasthan, Gujarat, UP, Haryana, MP and Delhi (the table columns are partly garbled, so treat as provisional). -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf ; http://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf
- Rajasthan is the main recommended state, and RHB-121 is in the state's zone A1 hybrid list. -- https://www.aicpmip.res.in/pw2011.pdf ; https://www.raridurgapura.org/Scheme-Millet.htm
- The raw field "recommended_states" was "Unknown". This digest supports replacing it with the states above, pending confirmation from the CSC minutes.
